kdw-1:
Document no. 20

Mieszko, Duke of Poland, 31 August 1173, at Gniezno; gives the estate of Wrąbczynek to the monastery of Ląd.

Original on parchment. The lower edge, folded over, shows 4 small holes for hanging the seal, in one of them threads of yellow silk. The script seems to be of the first half of the thirteenth century. The seal is lost.

Library of the Princes Czartoryski. Diplomata, vol. I, no. 1.

In the name of the Lord, amen. Forgetting is a stepmother to memory, and the course of deeds is darkened by the length of time, unless it is made known to those who come after by the living tokens of letters. Therefore I, Mieszko, by the grace of God Duke of Poland, make known to those present and to come that, meaning to increase the favour and grace which I bear especially towards the brothers of the Cistercian Order of the house of Ląd, of our foundation, so that they may the better persevere in the service of the name of God, at the request of the pious father Lord Bertold, abbot of that monastery, and of his devout convent, I have given them our estate called little Vronchin, with salt, lakes, fishing and hunting, and the other uses there at present and to come, free of all the rights of Poland by whatever names they are called, to be possessed by hereditary right. Witnesses of this are: Jarost, palatine of Kalisz; Bronis, castellan of Gniezno; Odolan the cupbearer; Ilik the chaplain; and many others worthy of trust. Given at Gniezno in the year of the Lord one thousand one hundred and seventy-three, on the day before the Kalends of September, in the sixth indiction. And that this may remain valid and firm, we have had the present document strengthened by the hanging of our seal.

Lendensis, that is of Ląd. Parvum Vronchin, today Wrąbczynek.
kdw-2:
Document no. 222

Fulko, Archbishop of the church of Gniezno, 1240 (sic), 30 September, without place; gives the monastery of Ląd the tithes of the chapels of St Peter and St Andrew.

Poznań. Royal State Archive. Ląd, Liber privilegiorum B, no. 38.

In the name of the Lord, amen. Since we must stand before the judgement seat of Christ on the last day, to receive good or evil according to what we have done in the body, it is fitting that we prepare ourselves a path to the homeland of eternal life by works of mercy. Therefore we, Fulko, by the grace of God Archbishop of the holy church of Gniezno, wish it to be known to all who will look on this page that, when the illustrious prince Lord Władysław, son of Odo, Duke of Poland, was settling the pressing business of the land with his barons at the monastery of Ląd on the day before St Remigius, it happened that, moved by God, he considered with the eye of piety the many burdens of the abbot and of the brothers serving God there, and, giving them the site of the castle that was called Lenda with its appurtenances, he assigned with most earnest devotion to their authority the chapels of St Andrew and St Peter, which had been of his patronage. And since it happened that we, called by the same prince, were present at this assembly together with our venerable brother and fellow bishop Lord Paweł of Poznań, moved by the prayers of the said prince and the most devoted entreaties of the barons, and pierced to the heart by the wretched poverty of the abbot and his brothers, we have given the tithes of the said chapels to God and to the blessed Mary ever Virgin, for the remedy of our soul and of our successors, for the use of the brothers, to be possessed for ever as they now are and as they may be in future, excepting no profit that may arise from their enlargement. And so that our devout gift may not be undone by any of our successors, we have named the estates in which the said tithes, with all their profits, are to fall to them: from Zagórów, Skokum, Kopojno, Trąbczyn, Szetlew, Łukom and Wrąbczyn; which tithes, by whatever right they are raised, whether the villages are divided or moved or called by another name, we give gladly, whatever of our right there may be, for the use of our brothers. And that all this may remain ratified and unshaken for ever, we strengthen the present writing by hanging our seal and that of the Chapter and that of our most beloved brother Lord Paweł, the bishop named above, who was present, and confirm it also by the witness of faithful men, whose names are these: Gotpold, the greater provost; Hugo, the dean; Mikołaj, the custodian; Wacław, the scholastic; and very many others worthy of trust. Given and done in the year of the Lord 1240 (sic), on the second day before the Kalends of October, in the twelfth indiction.

Landensis, of Ląd. Zagurow, Skokom, the same today. Kopanino, later Kopasino, today Kopojno. Trąbczyn, Szetlewo, Łukomie, the same today. Wronczino, today Wrąbczyn.
kdw-22:
Document no. 228

Kazimierz, Duke of Kujawy and Ląd, 17 June 1241, at Kopojno; exchanges his estates of Głowiewo and Wrąbczyn for the estate of the monastery of Ląd called Koszanów.

Original on parchment. On threads of white and blue linen a seal is hung, showing an armed rider riding to the right. On his head a flat helmet, at his left a triangular shield, the right hand holding upright a lance with a long pennon. Inscription: S. Kazim.... ucis Cuyavie. Besides this, 4 crosswise notches from the hanging of a second seal.

Warsaw. A private library. Diplomata.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, amen. What is done in time slips away with the time that slips, unless it is made everlasting by the memory of the living letter. Hence it is that I, Kazimierz, by the grace of God Duke of Kujawy and Ląd, make known to all, both present and to come, that I have exchanged with Jan, abbot of Ląd, and his brothers two estates with all their appurtenances, namely Glovevo and Wronecino, which once belonged to the huntsmen, for one estate of the said brothers which is called Coscheno; and in the said villages, namely Glovevo and Wronecino, we have granted every same liberty which the said brothers have had hitherto in the other estates of their church. And lest any scruple of doubt about this arise in the future, we have strengthened it with the hanging of our seal. The witnesses of this deed are: Bosek, castellan of Ląd, Mikołaj the treasurer, Gerard the treasurer, Lasch the under-judge, Brezdreve the under-cupbearer, Lancomir the under-falconer, Mikołaj of Rzgów, Golug and Pribizlaus, knights; Marek, Konrad, Piotr and Michał, chaplains; Jarosław, Jan and Michał, the duke's squires; Henryk the chief cellarer, Mikołaj and Wilhelm, brothers of the said house. This was done at Kopojno in the year of the Lord 1241, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of July.

Coavia, Kujawy. Landensis, of Ląd. Glovevo, Głowiew. Wronecino, Wrąbczyn. Coscheno, Koszanów. Yrgove, Rzgów. Copagnin, Kopojno.
kdw-3:
Document no. 238

Przemysł, Duke of Poland, 4 May 1243, in the church of the hospital at Gniezno; together with his brother Duke Bolesław hands over the hospital at Gniezno, most amply endowed with goods, to the rule of the Holy Sepulchre of the house of Miechów.

Poznań. Royal State Archive. Fasciculus Mączniki, B. IV. (A copy made in the 18th century from the original, which bore a seal.) Nakielski, Miechovia.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, amen. It is plain to all mortals how they are tossed by the turning of the times: that a long stretch of time gives birth to age, age to forgetting, and forgetting to the undoing of things done; for which reason it is needful that a thing worthy of memory be committed to writing, so that the greying past may be the more often renewed. I therefore, Przemysł, by the grace of God Duke of Poland, with my younger brother Bolesław and with our beloved mother Lady Jadwiga, make known to those present and to come who look on the present writing that, to the honour of God, in memory and for the remedy of our souls, with the consent of our venerable father Lord Fulko, Archbishop of Gniezno, and of his Chapter, and on the advice of our barons, we have given our hospital of Gniezno to the Holy Sepulchre, to be possessed by perpetual right under the rule and government of Lord Henryk, provost of the house of Miechów, and of his successors: for which the said provost shall be bound to provide through an honest and prudent man, a diligent rector, so that the alms given to the said hospital are not neglected or spent to no purpose. But if there should be, which God forbid, such a master as proved useful neither to God nor to his house, he shall be removed at our request and that of the Lord Archbishop and of his Chapter, if he has been canonically convicted and proved so, and another fit master shall be put in his place by the provost of the house named above, who will know how to keep favour and honour as far as God allows. In the hospital named above, as we have said, for the remedy of the souls of our forebears and successors and of our own, once it has been restored to a good state, all the sick in need of alms, not robbers, not men of violence, are to be cared for as far as the house can. Some poor scholars too shall be kept there at its cost, in food, not in clothing, at the will of the master of the hospital. And because, as our sins deserve, in these modern times when the little fire of charity grows cold on earth, there are found more invaders of spiritual houses than helpers or defenders, we wish to be true heirs and defenders in what belongs to the lay hand, and the Lord Archbishop with his Chapter in spiritual things. Done in the year of grace 1243 in the church of the said hospital at Gniezno on the feast of St Florian, in the presence of these witnesses: Lord Jan the dean, Krystian the custodian, Andrzej, Tomasz, Stefan the duke's chancellor, Wincenty and his brother Piotr, Izajasz and Piotr, canons of Gniezno, and many other canons and vicars; and these barons: Bogumił and Dzierżykraj, palatines of Poland; Cieciert, castellan of Gniezno; Tomasz, castellan of Poznań; Domarat the judge, and many other knights; the Dominican friars Jerzy and Piotr, and Artung, by whose mediation this is known to have been done. These are the villages of this hospital: Zdziechowa with those assigned to it, Lachowo, Imielno, Pawłowo with the lake called Prenevo, and Przysieka, Cielimowo, Ujazd, inns at Kłecko, and Ielemno with the whole lake and a mill and with beavers to be taken freely, Stasin too with the lake called Cubuchowo and with all its uses, Lozine, Konikowo, and a mill and an orchard and a field by the orchard and by the hospital. These are the villages excepted into one neighbourhood, which are free: Koreczno, Przysieka, Jezierzany, Zdziechowa, Ujazd; so that the huntsmen of any office are not to be received there, nor are they to feed our dogs or give carts, and we make them wholly free of every military expedition and the building of castles and of all other exactions and payments.

Hospitale Scti Sepulcri, the so-called Bożogrobcy (canons of the Holy Sepulchre). Mechoviensis, of Miechów. Zdechova, Zdziechowa. Leccovo, Lachowo. Chemelino, Imielno. Pawlowo, Pawłowo. Preseca, Przysieka. Cymellowo, Cielimowo. Ugasd, Ujazd. Clech, Kłeck. Ielemno cum pleno lacu et molendino, once probably a settlement on the river Wełna near the town of Kłecko, today vanished. Stasin, Lozine, not identified. Conicowo, Konikowo. Kurrino, Koreczno. Iezesani, Jezierzany.
kdw-4:
Document no. 393

Bolesław, Duke of Poland, 10 December 1261, at Sechowa; confirms the grants of estates and liberties made to the monastery of Ląd by Mieszko, Duke of Poland, in 1145 on the occasion of its foundation, and adds new ones on his own part.

Poznań. Royal State Archive. Ląd, Liber privilegiorum B, no. 4. (Compare charter no. 10, and Rzyszczewski and Muczkowski, Codex diplomaticus Poloniae I, no. 1.)

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, amen. Since every deed of men of our time is wont to be held doubtful that is not strengthened by the points of letters, we Bolesław, by the grace of God Duke of Poland, ordered the brothers of the house of Ląd of the Cistercian Order to show us their privileges on the foundation of that house. Having examined them with due care, we found in them with full certainty that our great-grandfather Mieszko, by the grace of God great Duke of Poland, having founded the said house in the year of the Lord 1145, for the support of the brothers serving God there, to the honour of our Lord Jesus Christ and of his glorious mother Mary ever Virgin, bestowed on the said house these estates with their people and all their uses present and future: namely Kościół, where he granted that there should be a market full of every liberty, Dolany, Mokra, Kłobia, Choceń. The people of these villages are bound each to pay on the feast of St Michael sixty sheaves of rye, a measure of oats, a measure of wheat, three urns of malt; to reap five heaps of corn, three cartloads of hay and as many of wood, two pine trunks; for three days on end with all the household to clean the crops, each to thresh for one day, and to give three bundles of flax. He also gave these estates listed below with their people and all their uses present and future: Szetlew with the cooks, Rzgów with the sanctuary people and the stable men, Grabienice with the chamberlains, Sławsk with the fishermen, Wiramowo, Kwaskowo, Chorzeń, Staralanka, Swiniarowo. The people of these villages are bound to draw the net between Sieradz and Władysław, and throughout all Poland, whenever the need of the brothers requires, to carry their orders, on horse as well as on foot. He granted too that the fishermen and huntsmen of the said brothers might freely follow fishing and hunting wherever his fishermen and huntsmen and those of his successors go. He also gave the said brothers, for providing lights, three markets with inns, namely Glev, Thur and Sobotka. He would also have the innkeepers of the said villages summoned nowhere but before the abbot. And since a gift given to God ought not to be subject to the laws of princes, he freed all the people living in the said villages from carting, from every conveyance, from watch, from tribute, naraz, podworowe, market and bridge tolls, from the building of castles or of any bridges, from receiving, guarding or escorting beaver-keepers, from the guarding and payment of falcons, which is called sokol, from the neighbourhood called in the common tongue opole, from every exaction or levy, from carting and military expeditions, and from all the rights established in Poland by whatever names they are called. Reserving to no judge or castellan any right to summon or judge the said people or their villages. But since the age of time does not let things which cannot be preserved by keeping stay in the same state, and it was to be feared that, the said privilege of our great-grandfather being worn away by great age, harm might in future arise to the said house, we, following with pious affection the devotion of our forebears, confirm the said estates with the people and liberties written above, and take moreover into our protection the estates given to them by hereditary right by the nobles of Poland, namely Skarboszewo, Marcinkowo, Jaroszyn, Górka, Zagórów, Skokum, Oleśnica. And for the remission of our sins we free all the people living in the said villages, bondsmen, free men and hired men serving in their courts, from every Polish right and from the levy which is called powolne (sic). We have also given the said brothers the water of the Warta with the streams adjoining it, from the bounds of the old castle as far as Drążyn of the bishop and on the other side as far as Kopojno, with the fishing, uses and beavers, to be possessed by hereditary right. And so that this our deed, to the honour of God and of his holy mother ever Virgin Mary, may be kept inviolably ratified, we have had the present document strengthened by the protection of our seal, on this condition: that if, which God forbid, any of our successors or of others should dare with rash daring to go against this our deed, he shall know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul and of all the Saints. Done at Sechowa in the year of the Lord 1261, on the fourth day before the Ides of December. There is also the witness of faithful men: Jan, by the grace of God Archbishop of Gniezno; Jan the chancellor; Erkenbold, palatine of Gniezno; Szymon, castellan of Gniezno; Mateusz, castellan of Ląd; Mateusz our notary, who also sealed the present document.

Landensis, of Ląd. Koscol, Kościół of St Nicholas, the place on which later stood the town of Lądek. Dolan, Dolany. Moscho, in no. 10 Morsk, Mokra, a vanished settlement near the town of Kazimierz, or else Mokre near the town of Rychwał. Cloba, Kłobia. Gocszene, as later appears, Choceń. Szethowo, Szetlewo. Coci, that is the village of the cooks, Kuchary Kościelne. Rzgowo, Rzgów. Sanctuarii, that is the village of the sanctuary people, Świątniki. Stabularii, perhaps the vanished settlement of Obory. Grabienice, Grabienice. Camerarii, perhaps the vanished settlement of Komorniki. Slavsko, Sławsk. Piscatores, perhaps a separate, vanished settlement, Rybitwy. Wiramowo, Kwaskowo, not identified. Chozen, Chorzeń. Staralanka, Swiniarowo, not identified. Seradz, Sieradz. Wladislav, Władysławów. Glev, probably Galewo. Thur, Tury. Sobotka, Sobotka. Skarbossewo, Skarboszewo. Marcinkowo, later renamed Kowalewo. Iarossyno, Jaroszyn. Gorzyza, Gorka. Zagorowo, Zagurów. Skokom, Skokum. Oleszyno, probably Oleśnica. Antiquum castrum, stood beside the monastery of Ląd. Dretino episcopi, Drążyn. Capayn, Kopojno. Sechowa, Czechowo, or else Szetlewo.
kdw-5:
Document no. 460

Bolesław, Duke of Poland, 27 March 1276, at Dłusk; gives Count Mikołaj, treasurer of Ląd, the village of Trąbczyn.

Original on parchment. On thick cords of faded silk thread three seals are hung. The first is Duke Bolesław's (seal XVI); the second is lost, only the strand of silk thread remains; the third is Duke Przemysł's (seal XXI).

Library of the Princes Czartoryski. Diplomata.

In the name of the Lord, amen. While the letter lives, the deed committed to it lives, whose assertion nourishes memory and, strengthened, takes increase. Therefore we Bolesław, by the grace of God Duke of Poland, together with our beloved little son Duke Przemysł and with our beloved wife Lady Jolenta, having regard to the faithful services of Count Mikołaj, our treasurer of Ląd, have finally and with pure intent given him our village which is called Trupcino, to be possessed by him and his descendants by hereditary right for ever .. (sic) although we had once given the said village to Count Janko son of Szymon, who died having no offspring, and so the said village came back to us .. (sic) and we had given the named village to Lord Mikołaj, who has gone the way of all flesh and had no lawful successors .. and so of right we have given the village named before to the said Count and his successors. And we free the said village altogether from these payments: from the ox, from the cow, from the opole, from the castle, from the poradlne, from the watch, from the podworowe, from carting, from conveyance, from the naraz. The privilege of Janko of blessed memory shall be of no force, as also that of the said Mikołaj, formerly parish priest of Środa .. And so that this our gift, which has come forth so duly from us all, may not be undone by anyone in the course of time, we have had the present writing strengthened by the protection of our seals, in the presence of these witnesses: Count Jarkelbold, palatine of Gniezno; Count Sykstus, castellan of Ruda .. Count Żegota, huntsman of Kalisz; Count Berwold, cupbearer of Ląd .. Count Sędziwój, under-chamberlain of Gniezno; Świętosław our scribe. Given in the year of the Lord 1276, written at Dłusk on the sixth day before the Kalends of April, on the eve of St Priscus the martyr and of Malchus.

Lenda, Ląd. Trupcino, Trąbczyn. Sroda, Środa. Rudensis, of Ruda. Dluscho, Dłusk.
kdw-6:
Document no. 27

Kalisz, 18 October 1280

Duke Przemysł II confirms the possessions of the Cistercian monastery at Ląd and endows them with certain liberties.

Original: Cologne, Historisches Archiv, Kl. Lond I, 15. Parchment 485 × 350+17 mm. On a pink silk cord the issuer's seal, showing (according to the editor in DKM) the standing figure of the duke holding a spear in his right hand and in his left a shield with a rampant lion; on both sides of the duke stand armed men blowing horns [probably on towers]. The description recalls the seal of Przemysł I, and of II (compare KDW IV, seal no. XV). On the back: Renovacio privilegii ducis Mesiconis (15th century).

Copy: The same, Copiarius, fols 15–16 (15th century).

Edition: DKM, pp. 356–358, no. 8 (from the original).

Regests: 1. Perlbach, Lond, p. 86 (from the original); 2. Krzyżanowski, Dyplomy, p. 168 (from edition 1).

|| In the name of the Lord, amen. || Since we are to pass with the swiftness of our days, as a shadow is wont to flee or smoke to vanish, | therefore we, Przemysł the Second, by the grace of God Duke of Poland, wish it to be known to all the faithful of Christ, present as well as to come, that for the love of our Lord Jesus Christ, the liberator of our | souls, and for the veneration of his glorious mother, Mary perpetual Virgin, and of All Saints, we renew for the brothers beloved in Christ who serve the Lord in the house of Ląd the privilege of our glorious | great-grandfather, the lord Mieszko, Duke of Poland¹, confirming to the said brothers these estates written below with their people and all the uses that are in them and may come in future, taking them into our protection and committing them to be defended by our successors for all time, in sole regard of divine reward. Now the places of the possessions are written below: namely Kościół², where we confirm that there shall be a market full of every liberty, Dolany³, Morsko⁴, Kłobia⁵ and Choceń⁶. The people of these villages are bound each to pay on the feast of St Michael [29 IX] sixty sheaves of rye, a measure of oats, a measure of wheat, three urns of malt, to reap five heaps of corn, three cartloads of hay and as many of wood, two pine trunks, for three days on end with all the household to clean the crops, each to thresh for one day, and to give three bundles of flax. We confirm too these estates written below with their people and all the uses that are in them and may be hereafter: Szechouo with the cooks⁷, Irgouo with the sanctuary people and the stable men⁸, Grabonowiz with the chamberlains⁹, Slausco with the fishermen¹⁰, Wiranouo¹¹, Quascouo, ¹², Choren¹³, Staralancha¹⁴, Suinareuo¹⁵. The people of the said villages are bound to draw the net within Sieradz¹⁶ and Włocławek¹⁷, and throughout all Poland¹⁸, whenever the need of the brothers requires, to carry their orders, on horse as well as on foot. We confirm moreover that the fishermen and huntsmen of the said brothers may freely follow fishing and hunting wherever our fishermen and huntsmen and those of our successors go. We confirm too to the said house, for providing lights, three markets with inns: Chlew¹⁹, Thur²⁰, Sobotka²¹; we confirm too that the innkeepers of these villages are summoned nowhere but before the abbot. And since a gift given to God ought not to be subject to the laws of princes, we free all the people living in the said villages from carting, from every conveyance, from watch, from tribute, from the naraz, podworowe, market and bridge tolls, from the building of castles or of any bridges, from receiving, guarding or escorting beaver-keepers, from receiving huntsmen of any kind, from the payment and guarding of falcons, which is called sokol, from the neighbourhood called in the common tongue opole, from every exaction or levy, from carting and military expeditions, and from all the rights established in Poland by whatever names they are called. Reserving to no castellan or judge any right to summon or judge the said people or their villages; but when a grave cause arises which cannot fittingly be settled before the abbot or his judge, they are to be summoned to our presence by our ring, the abbot to have whatever falls by right of judgement; and they are to be imprisoned nowhere but in the abbot's stable. And so that this our confirmation, to the honour of God and of his holy mother ever Virgin Mary, may have the strength of lasting firmness, we have had the present document strengthened by the protection of our seal. Done at Kalisz on the feast of St Luke the Evangelist in the year of the Lord @1280@, in the presence of these witnesses, namely: Lord Andrzej, archdeacon and chancellor of Kalisz²², Count Żegota, huntsman of Kalisz²³, Count Piotrek, cupbearer of Poznań²⁴, Count Naszan, equerry of Kalisz²⁵, Count Falisz, procurator of Kalisz²⁶, and given by the hand of Tylo, notary of our court²⁷.

¹Mieszko III (d. 1202) was the great-great-grandfather of Przemysł II. The document mentioned here is a forgery dated 23 April 1145 (KDW I, no. 10), kept in the form of a supposed original, in truth made in the 13th century, in the archive of Ląd, today in Cologne, Historisches Archiv, Kl. Lond I/1; compare also on it Z. Kozłowska-Budkowa, Repertorium, pp. 43–45. The present document repeats a large part of the document of supposedly 1145.

²Kościół, commonly identified with Lądek, east of Ląd.

³Dolany, see above, no. 26/4.

⁴Morsko, see above, no. 13/4.

⁵Kłobia, a parish village in Kujawy, south of Brześć.

⁶Choceń, a parish village in Kujawy, north of Chodecz, south-east of Kłobia.

⁷Probably Szetlew, south-east of Zagórów; but compare Kuchary Kościelne, 9 km east of Szetlew.

⁸Rzgów, north-east of Szetlew. Świątniki just west of Rzgów.

⁹Grabienice, just south of Rzgów.

¹⁰Sławsk on the Warta, west of Konin.

¹¹Wiranowo and Kwaskowo not identified; they occur also in the forgery of 1145.

¹²Wiranowo and Kwaskowo not identified; they occur also in the forgery of 1145.

¹³Chorzeń on the Warta, north-west of Konin, today within the town of Konin.

¹⁴Stara Łąka not identified; it occurs also in the forgery of 1145.

¹⁵Perhaps Świniarzewo (Siniarzewo), a parish village in Kujawy, north-west of Brześć, a village named also in the forgery of 1145.

¹⁶Sieradz.

¹⁷Włocławek.

¹⁸Polonia probably in the sense of Greater Poland.

¹⁹Chlew (rather this, not Glew), Tur and Sobótka are hard to identify; compare Zajączkowscy, Materiały II, pp. 108–109.

²⁰Chlew (rather this, not Glew), Tur and Sobótka are hard to identify; compare Zajączkowscy, Materiały II, pp. 108–109.

²¹Chlew (rather this, not Glew), Tur and Sobótka are hard to identify; compare Zajączkowscy, Materiały II, pp. 108–109.

²²Andrzej Zaremba, see above, no. 26/8.

²³Żegota, see above, no. 13/7.

²⁴Piotrek, Pietrzyk, son of Prandota, steward of Poznań 1275, cupbearer 1280, castellan of Poznań 1284, palatine of Poznań 1297–1299 (Spisy wlkp.).

²⁵Naszan, equerry of Kalisz 1280–1288 (Spisy wlkp.).

²⁶Chwalisz (Falisz), see above, no. 26/11.

²⁷Tylo, see above, no. 26/12.
kdw-23:
Document no. 535

Przemysł the Second, Duke of Poland, 18 February 1284, at Kalisz; allows Count Mikołaj, treasurer of Ląd, to locate his estate of Trąbczyn under German law.

Original on parchment, in whose lower folded edge are two holes for the hanging of the seal. Warsaw. The Rusiecki collection. Diplomata. — Rzyszczew. Muczkowski, Codex diplomaticus Poloniae I, no. 64.

In the name of the Lord, amen. While the letter lives, the deed committed to the letter lives, whose assertion nourishes memory and, strengthened, takes increase. Therefore we, Przemysł the Second, by the grace of God Duke of Poland, make known to all, both present and to come, who examine this page, that, having regard to the faithful service and the usefulness of our beloved knight Count Mikołaj, treasurer of Ląd, and wishing also to reform the state of our land for the better, we have given him free authority to locate his estate, which is commonly called Tropcssino, under German law, by the same right by which all the towns and villages through the district of our lordship are held. Namely so, that the same estate be for ever exempt from all the Polish payments by which our lordship is won: from the naraz, the povoz, the prevod, the stroza, the podvorove, the castle's summons, the opole, the ox, the cow, the cifo of honey, and from all other payments under whatever names they are counted. And that the said estate may be shaped the better, the settlers of the same estate are not to pay the poradlne. And that this our gift may persevere inviolate for ever, we have had the present page confirmed with the protection of our seal, in the presence of these witnesses: Count Przecław, castellan of Gniezno, Count Andrzej, judge of Gniezno, Count Sędziwój, castellan of Ruda. Given at Kalisz in the year of the grace of the Lord 1284, in the twelfth indiction, on the Friday next before the Sunday Esto michi, by the hand of Thilo, notary of our court.

Lendensis, of Ląd. Tropcssino, Trąbczyn. Rudensis, of Ruda.
kdw-24:
Document no. 672

Przemysł the Second, Duke of Poland, 1 August 1291, at Pyzdry; gives Henryk, citizen of Pyzdry, the village of Wrąbczyn, to be located under German law.

Wilanów. Library. The Register of the Reviewers of Greater Poland, fol. 121v.

In the name of the Lord, amen. While the letter lives, the deed committed to the letter lives, whose assertion nourishes memory and, strengthened, takes increase. We therefore, Przemysł the Second, by the grace of God Duke of Poland, make known to all, both present and to come, who examine this page, that, seeing by experience that the Polish law in our lordship brings us nothing or little use, and wishing to bring our village, located under Polish law, named Wronchino, into a better and more useful condition, we have bestowed it on Henryk, our citizen of Pyzdry, to be located under German law according to the law of the town of Pyzdry, so that by reason of his location the said Henryk and his successors and heirs shall have the sixth mansus free, a tavern, a fishpond (sic), a mill, and a free shoemakers' shop. We also give the woods and marshes, which cannot be rooted out and are not fit for tillage, for the pasture of pigs and of sows; and whatever of meadow there is in the district of the same village we join to the said Henryk and his successors with all its uses and appurtenances. And if the bees, which are in the wood of the same village, should perish through the improvement and the location, we shall not on that account blame the said Henryk or his heirs in any way. And that the said village may be the better located, we give a liberty of twelve years from every exaction and payment, from the feast of St Martin next coming; when that has passed, the inhabitants of the said village shall pay to us each year from each mansus six measures of rye, the same of oats, and a ferton of denarii, according as they shall be in Pyzdry. Henryk shall also have free authority with his heirs to build a church there, and to assign to it one free mansus for its adornment. Besides, we join the said village of Wronchino to our town which is called Sal, so that both have one district and one boundary. Moreover, the aforesaid Henryk and his heirs shall have free authority to hunt hares and partridges in the district of the said estate. And that this our gift may persevere inviolate for ever, we have had the present page strengthened with the protection of our seal. Done at Pyzdry on the day of the Chains of blessed Peter, in the year of the Lord one thousand two hundred and ninety-one, given by the hand of Jaszko, notary of our court.

Wronchino, Wrąbczyn. Sal, not identified; it appears nevertheless from the related documents that in the region marked above, that is the little town of Zagórów, the making of salt was common in the early centuries; cf. nos. 20 and 192. Pisdri, Pyzdry.
kdw-7:
Document no. 678

Przemysł the Second, Duke of Greater Poland, 21 October 1291, at Gniezno; confirms the exchange of the estates of the monastery of Ląd called Głowiew, Sławsk and Chocicza for the estate of Count Sędziwój the under-chamberlain called Kopojno, which he endows with the most ample privileges.

Original on parchment. On a thick cord of green silk thread hangs the seal of Duke Przemysł (seal XXVI).

Library of the Princes Czartoryski. Diplomata. Rzyszczewski and Muczkowski, Codex diplomaticus Poloniae I, no. 77; from another original, which has at the end: Data per Iasconem notarium curie nostre anno Domini M.CC. nonagesimo primo in Gnezna, on the day of the Eleven Thousand Virgins.

In the name of the Lord, amen. Since the forgetfulness inborn in human memory leads into error the settlements of temporal acts that have not been firmly strengthened by the point of letters or the subscription of witnesses, we, Przemysł the Second, by the grace of God Duke of Greater Poland, wish it to be known to all the faithful of Christ, present as well as to come, that the venerable abbot Lord Gerhard of Ląd and his convent made an exchange with our beloved under-chamberlain Count Sędziwój for the good of their house, with our gracious favour and consent, giving him three estates, namely Głowiew, Sławsk and Chocicza, for the estate called Kopojno, which the same Sędziwój had held by inheritance, exchanged with us for his patrimony, namely Górczyn, free and exempt from every Polish right by whatever name it is called; the sons of the said Sędziwój, namely Janko and Marcin, to whom the hereditary right belonged, resigning the said estate before us and yielding up the hereditary right, and the said abbot with his brothers entering the said estate of Kopojno to possess it by inheritance. And we, desiring to increase the affection which we have always had for the house of Ląd, will that the said estate with its inhabitants, their own or free, shall be exempt and free, as it was before when it was held by the said Sędziwój: from every conveyance, from carting, from watch, from tribute, from the naraz, from the podworowe, from market and bridge tolls, from the building of castles or of any bridges, from receiving, guarding or escorting beaver-keepers (sic), for we have given the beavers to the lord abbot and his brothers to hunt for ever. Moreover from the neighbourhood which is called in the common tongue opole, from receiving the under-huntsman or huntsmen of any kind, from the guarding or payment of falcons, which is popularly called socol, from every exaction or levy which is called povolove, from carting and military expeditions, and from all the rights established in Poland by whatever names they are called. We have given the said brothers, through their own judge, free authority to carry out all judgements, such as of strife, striking, maiming of limbs, or even beheading, so that we may have the greater trust towards God at the dreadful judgement, reserving to no castellan or judge any right to summon or judge in that estate. And that this our deed, to the honour of God and of holy Mary ever Virgin, may obtain the strength of lasting firmness, we strengthen the present page with the protection of our seal. Witnesses of this are: Filip, archdeacon of Gniezno; Berwold, castellan of Kalisz; Abraham, treasurer of Gniezno. These things were done in the year of the Lord 1291 at Gniezno, on the day of the Eleven Thousand Virgins.

Lenda, Ląd. Glovevo, Głowiew. Slavsco, Sławsk. Chociczha, Chocicza. Copaino, Kopojno. Gorcino, Górczyn.
kdw-8:
Document no. 685

Przemysł the Second, Duke of Poland, 29 September 1292, at Kalisz; ratifies the exchange, made five years before, of the estate of Wojsław son of Gosław called Niałek for the estates of Wisław son of Gerlach called Wrąbczyn and Bieganin.

Original on parchment. On threads of red silk hangs the seal of Duke Przemysł (seal XXVI).

Warsaw. Private library, Diplomata. Poznań, Royal State Archive. Ląd, Liber privilegiorum B, no. 22.

In the name of the Lord, amen. We wisely meet many inconveniences when we strengthen the business of our age with the protection of letters and witnesses. We therefore, Przemysł the Second, by the grace of God Duke of Poland, make known to all men, of the present age as well as of the age to come, that, being present before us and our barons, Count Wisław, son of the late Gerloch, on the one part, and Wojsław, son of Gosław, on the other, made between them this exchange of their own estates: that the said Wisław, receiving the estate of the Wojsław named above, called in the common tongue Niałek, gave and resigned in exchange two estates of his own, Wrąbczyn, which he had exchanged with Przybysław son of Lutogniew, and Bieganin, to be possessed by perpetual hereditary right. And we, considering these exchanges duly and reasonably made, approving and ratifying them, have decreed that they shall be valid for ever, all hindrance set aside. And of the fullness of our power we have freed and exempted the said villages of Wrąbczyn and Bieganin from every Polish exaction, and make them free as they were of old, namely from the naraz, from carting, from conveyance, from watch, from the podworowe, from the ox, from the cow, from the opole, from summons to the castle. And if a homicide is committed among the inhabitants of the said villages, the said Wojsław and his posterity shall take the capital penalty. But if the homicide is between one of his inhabitants and a stranger, he shall nonetheless take the penalty for homicide after his inhabitant (sic). The inhabitants of the said villages shall be summoned nowhere but before us, by letter, with our seal or ring, and shall be bound to answer there to those who complain of them. In witness of which we ordered Jaśko our notary to write the present letters, strengthening them with the protection of our seal, in the presence of these witnesses: the counts Piotrko, castellan of Poznań, Zbylut (sic), castellan of Nakło, Wit, cupbearer of Gniezno. Given at Kalisz on the feast of the blessed Michael, when we went out on campaign to Sieradz against the King of Bohemia, and then this same exchange was renewed and confirmed, which had been done and made five years before. In the year of the grace of the Lord 1292.

Nalcho, Niałek. Wroncino, Wronczyn. Beganino, Bieganin. Nakel, Nakło. Syracz, Sieradz.
kdw-25:
Document no. 795

Władysław, Duke of the kingdom of Poland etc., 9 September 1298, at Pyzdry; allows Count Wojsław to locate the village of Wrąbczyn under German law.

Original on parchment, whose seal, hung on threads of red silk, shows the arms of the land of Kujawy. Warsaw. The Rusiecki collection. Diplomata. — Rzyszczew. Muczkowski, Codex diplomaticus Poloniae I, no. 90.

In the name of the Lord, amen. We prudently provide against many inconveniences when we confirm for ever with letters and witnesses the things done in the time of our own age. Therefore we, Władysław, by the grace of God duke of the kingdom of Poland, of Pomerania, of Kujawy, of Łęczyca and of Sieradz, commend to the memory of all present and to come, that we give to Wojsław, our faithful servant, and to his lawful posterity the power to locate his village, which is named Vronztino in Polish, under German law, freeing the said village and its inhabitants from the naraz, the povos, the prevod, the podvorove, the stroza, the ox, the cow, the pig, the ham, the poramb, the stan, the falcons, the huntsmen, the urn of provincial honey, the cart of hay, the head of rye, the opole, the poradlne, and the castle's summons — so that, cited, they need not appear or answer before any official, but before us alone, appeal being made to us through our ring or our seal by letter. We also will that the said Count Wojsław and his successors shall judge all the causes, greater, middling and lesser, which shall arise within the bounds of the same estate of Vronczino, and receive the penalties judged entirely and completely for themselves. For the evident firmness of this matter we have had these presents written, strengthening them for ever with our seal. This was done at Pyzdry in the presence of these counts: Roscone, huntsman of Kalisz, Świętomir, castellan of Biechowo, Świętosław, huntsman, and many others worthy of trust. Given there on the morrow of the Nativity of the blessed Virgin Mary, by the hand of the Lord Dominik, notary of our court, in the year of the Lord 1298.

Vronztino, Wrąbczyn. Piysdir, Pyzdry. Bechovia, Biechowo.
kdw-26:
Document no. 1044

Władysław, King of Poland etc., 9 August 1324, at Pyzdry; gives the monastery of Ląd the site of a water mill on the river Warta below the castle of Pyzdry, and confirms its possession of certain villages.

Original on parchment. On a cord of green silk the seal of Władysław the King is hung (seal XLIV). Warsaw. The Rusiecki collection. Diplomata.

In the name of the Lord, amen. As the frailty of the human condition cannot escape temporal death, so no deed done in the shifting time can obtain the strength of firmness, unless it is renewed in writing and strengthened with the protection of a seal. Hence we, Władysław, by the grace of God King of Poland, Duke of Kraków, of Sandomierz, of Sieradz, of Kujawy and of Łęczyca, make known to present and to come, that, for the honour of our Lord Jesus Christ and of his pious and glorious mother, the ever-virgin Mary, in remission of our sins and of all our forefathers', and on account of the great desolation and destruction which we worked upon the house of Ląd of the Cistercian Order when we were in Poland with our army, we have bestowed on the said house and its brothers the site of a water mill below the castle of Pyzdry on the river Warta, which is known to belong to our lordship and kingdom, to be possessed by hereditary right, granting to the brothers of the said house every liberty to build a mill in that place at their own pleasure, or to repair anew the old mill that belongs to them. Lest therefore this our gift be troubled by anyone in the future, we will and command all the captains, castellans, procurators, advocates, consuls, aldermen and every citizen constituted in the town of Pyzdry, that they in no way impede, nor presume to impede, the said brothers in building or repairing the mill, wherever they wish in the two places aforesaid. Moreover, for the regard of the divine reward alone, we confirm to the said house of Ląd these estates written below, given to them by the nobles of Poland by hereditary right, or honestly bought by the brothers themselves, nevertheless receiving them into our defence, namely Mynzelino, Zramlyz, Bronchowo, Cysowo, Wardosino, Wszonowo, Wronchyno, with the lake which is called Seborowo. We also will that the people of the said villages enjoy the same liberty which is contained more fully in the founding privilege of our great-grandfather of blessed memory, Mieszko the Great, illustrious Duke of Poland. Given and done at Pyzdry with suitable witnesses: Klemens, palatine of Sieradz, Count Piotr, castellan of Poznań, Count Slavanta, castellan of Kalisz, Count Mikołaj, castellan of Biechów, and Piotr, vice-chancellor and canon of Kraków, in the year of the Lord 1324, on the vigil of the blessed Laurencjusz, martyr and levite. In testimony of which we have ordered the present document to be strengthened with the protection of our seal.

Lendensis, of Ląd. Mynzelino, Mycielin. Zramlyz, Chrzamlice. Bronchowo, Bronki. Cysowo, Czyżew. Wardosino, Wardężyn. Wszonowo, Sczonów. Wronchyno, Wrąbczyn. Lacus Seborowo, today a marsh north of Wrąbczyn. Pyser, Pyzdry. Bechoviensis, of Biechów.
kdw-9:
Document no. 1252

Dobiesław, judge of the lands of Gniezno and Kalisz, 13 November 1346, at Pyzdry; adjudges to the church of Gniezno the estates of Stropiszyn and Pępocin against the claims of the brothers Jan and Przedpełk, heirs of Trąbczyn, and the estate of Kokanin against the suit of Pietrasz, heir of Rzegocin.

Gniezno. Archive of the Metropolitan Chapter. Liber privilegiorum of the 15th century, fol. 93v.

We, Dobiesław, judge of the lands of Gniezno and Kalisz, make known to all and acknowledge to those present that, concerning the estates of Stropiszyn and Panpicza, in the presence of the noble men Mikołaj, captain of Poland, Maćko of Poznań and Mikołaj of Kalisz, palatines, and of the other witnesses written below, we absolve by the tenor of these presents Lord Kiełcz the custodian and the church of Gniezno from the claim and suit of the brothers Jan and Przedpełk, heirs of Trąbczyn; and likewise the venerable father in Christ and reverend lord, Lord Jarosław, Archbishop of the holy church of Gniezno, from the suit and claim of Pietrasz, heir of Rzegocin, for the estate of Kokanin, adjudging the said estates to them and imposing perpetual silence on the said heirs concerning them; in witness of which our seal is hung on these presents. Done and given at Pyzdry on the feast of St Brice, in the year of the Lord one thousand three hundred and forty-six, in the presence of the noble men, the palatines Maćko of Poznań and Mikołaj of Kalisz; the castellans Tomisław of Poznań, Zbylut of Gniezno and Janusz of Kalisz, and others worthy of trust.

Tropessino, Stropiszyn. Panpicza, below with the addition: alias Kopydlowo, perhaps Pępocin, or else Kopydłowo. Trampczino, Trąbczyn. Stregoczino, Rzegocin. Cokanino, Kokanin.
kdw-10:
Document no. 1253

Dobiesław, judge of the lands of Gniezno and Kalisz, 13 November 1346, at Pyzdry; adjudges to the church of Gniezno the estates of Stropiszyn and Pępocin against the claims of Andrzej, heir of Trąbczyn, and his kin.

Gniezno. Archive of the Metropolitan Chapter. Liber privilegiorum of the 15th century, fol. 93v.

We, Dobiesław, judge of the lands of Gniezno and Kalisz, make known to all and acknowledge by these presents that at Pyzdry on the feast of St Brice, in the year of the Lord 1346, in the presence of Mikołaj, captain of Poland, Maćko of Poznań and Mikołaj of Kalisz, palatines, Tomisław of Poznań, Zbylut of Gniezno and Janusz of Kalisz, castellans, and others worthy of trust, on their counsel and command we adjudged to Lord Kiełcz the custodian and to the church of Gniezno the estates of Stropiszyn and Panpycze to be possessed for ever, absolving him and the church of Gniezno from the suit and claim of Andrzej, heir of Trąbczyn, and of all his kin, who, setting him up before us, entrusted to him, in his name and theirs, the power to go to law for those estates; having heard his pleadings and those of the opposing party on both sides, we imposed perpetual silence concerning that estate on him and all his kin, granting to the said Lord Kiełcz and the church of Gniezno these our present letters, strengthened with our seal, concerning this judgment. Given and done at Pyzdry on the feast of St Brice, in the year of the Lord 1346, in the presence of the witnesses named above.

Troppessino, Stropiszyn. Panpycze, added in the margin: sive Kopydłowo, probably Pępocin; Kopydłowo lies 5 miles from the latter. Trampczino, Trąbczyn.
kdw-27:
Document no. 1363

Wyrzbenta, general captain of Poland, 14 August 1357, at Konin; attests that the monastery of Ląd exchanged the estate of Szczonowo for the third part of the village of Wrąbczyn, the estate of Zemka, wife of Albert.

Original on parchment. On a scrap of parchment hangs a seal showing on a triangular shield the arms of the Niesobia family; the inscription effaced. Warsaw. The Rusiecki collection. Diplomata.

We, Wyrzbenta, general captain of Poland, make known to all and singular, present as much as to come, who shall have notice of these presents, that there came before us, on the one part, Lord Jan, by divine mercy abbot of the monastery of Ląd of the Cistercian Order, with the full will of his convent, and, on the other, the reverend lady named Zemka, wife of Albert; not compelled, not forced, nor led astray by any kind of fraud or deceit, but of their own good and spontaneous will they made and ordered between themselves an exchange of goods, that is of estates; in this manner, that the said lord abbot with his convent of Ląd exchanged and resigned the estate of his monastery, commonly called Usczonowo, with all its uses, to the said lady Zemka for the third part of great Wroenschino; and conversely the said lady Zemka exchanged, gave and resigned the third part of the estate of Wronschino for the whole estate of Usczonowo aforesaid to the said lord abbot and his monastery; in this manner, that when the mother of the said lady Zemka dies, the said lady Zemka shall not be able, on account of any portion of her mother in the third part of the aforesaid estate of Wroenschino, to move any matter, nor is she bound to. And lest the said exchange, or the attestation of the exchange and of the resignation, be brought to nothing through the frailty of any calumny, we have had these presents written, strengthening them with the impress of our seal, in the presence of these witnesses: Predslao of Poznań, Andrzej of Kalisz, castellans; Franczko, heir of Wilków, Barnaba of Bieganowo, Marcin, burgrave in Konin, Wysław, parish priest there. Done and given at Konin on the vigil of the glorious Assumption of the Virgin, in the year of the Lord 1357.

Land, Ląd. Usczonowo, Szczonowo. Magnum Wroenschino, Wrąbczyn. Vilcowo, Wilków. Beganowo, Bieganowo.
app5314550221-4:
Privilege, or exchange, of the village of Little Wronczyn and of the mill in the suburb of Pyzdry with Kazimierz, King of Poland, for the forest Czernietz, in which the village of Drzewce [uncertain: est] was afterwards founded. 25.

In the name of the Lord. Amen. Lest the affairs or deeds of mortals that are done and ordained in time pass away and waver with the course of time, it is necessary that they be brought to perpetual memory by the safeguard of letters and the noting of witnesses. Therefore let the present age, as well as the future, know: that we, Kazimierz, by the grace of God King of Poland, and also lord and heir of the lands of Kraków, Sandomierz, Sieradz, Łęczyca, Kuyavia, Pomerania and Ruthenia, after mature deliberation, and with the common counsel of our barons joining in it, have made an exchange of our royal goods, namely of the deserted forests described expressly below, with the venerable and religious man Brother Jan, abbot, and the convent of the brothers of the monastery of Ląd, of the Cistercian Order, of the Gniezno district, in this manner. The heritage of that monastery, namely Little Wronczyn near the town of Pyzdry, and the mill below the castle of Pyzdry, also of the said monastery of Ląd, with all and singular rents, fruits, profits and appurtenances belonging in any way of old to the said heritage of Wronczyn and the said mill, as they are marked off all round in their boundaries, being received, appropriated and incorporated in perpetuity for us and our kingdom by way and in the name of exchange: which heritage of Wronczyn with the mill above-said the lord abbot aforesaid, in his own name and that of his convent, by way of exchange, freely and willingly resigned from himself and his said monastery of Ląd to us and our kingdom, to hold and have in perpetuity, as he is permitted, with all right and dominion. In recompense for the said heritage and mill, we give, donate, ascribe and appropriate to the same lord abbot and his monastery and convent aforesaid, in the manner and by way of exchange, our forest in the part commonly called Czirnetz, situated in the district of Konin, fit for the cultivation of fields, containing sixty Franconian mansi in their due measure, measured by our authority and by our special messengers, and duly bounded and surrounded all round on every side, from all heritages, our royal ones as well as those of any nobles lying around, by its certain boundaries, which are commonly called kopce, with all profits and fruits whatever that are in that forest or may in any way be in it in future; and by the tenor of these presents, for all time, with all right and dominion, as it

belonged to us, we incorporate it under our protection, to be possessed for their benefit. We give the abbot and convent aforesaid full and complete power to found in the forest of the said sixty mansi as many villages as they can, under Polish or German law, as shall seem to them more useful and expedient. And we will that the villages founded in the said forest shall fully enjoy and possess, by our special grace, every freedom from our royal payments whatever which the other possessions of the said monastery of Ląd enjoy, as is more fully contained in the ancient privileges made on the freedom of the possessions of that monastery. But if the same abbot and convent should be unwilling or unable to settle these sixty mansi to the full, then in whatever part of them they leave as a grove or forest, the hunting of deer and boar being reserved in it for our royal pleasure, all other profits, fruits and revenues, namely in pastures, spaces, and the hunting of any wild beasts or birds, and also by name all and singular profits customarily had by us in the said forests, as they belonged to us and as we alone held them under our royal power: all the foregoing the abbot and convent of the above-said monastery of Ląd shall hold for all time, as from now ascribed and incorporated to them by us, and shall possess peacefully and quietly, with our special requisition made beforehand, to sell, give, exchange and turn them in any way to the use of themselves and their oft-said monastery of Ląd. In witness of which our seal is hung on these presents. Done at Pyzdry on the Tuesday after the octave of the Epiphany of the Lord, in the year of the same 1,362. Present these witnesses: Albert, voivode of Brześć; Wyrzbięta, castellan of Poznań and captain of Poland; Janusz of [uncertain: Bechovien.] and Dobiesław of Kruszwica, castellans; Adam of Kalisz and Trojan of Brześć, sub-chamberlains; and Florian, chancellor of Łęczyca, by whose mandate the present privilege [uncertain: transmitti]; and very many other witnesses worthy of trust.
kdw-28:
Document no. 1478

Wyrzbenta, castellan of Poznań and the same general captain of Poland, 31 May 1362, at Konin; attests that Laurentius, heir of Królikowo, castellan of Ląd, sold the third part of the estate of Wrąbczyn to the monastery of Ląd.

Poznań. Royal State Archive. Ląd, Liber privilegiorum B, no. 20.

We, Wyrzbenta, castellan of Poznań and also general captain of Poland, wish to commend to the notice of the present and to the memory of the future, in these presents, that there came before us and the other nobles of the land of Poland the valiant knight Lord Laurentius, heir of Królikowo and castellan of Ląd; not compelled, not forced, nor led astray by any kind of fraud or deceit, but by the mature counsel of his friends had over this, to the religious man Lord Jan, by divine mercy abbot, and to his monastery in Ląd of the Cistercian Order, he sold, gave and resigned for all time the third part of the estate commonly called Magnum Wronchyno, with all and singular the uses and all the revenues belonging to the same third part of the same estate, which the said Lord Laurentius, castellan of Ląd, had held peaceably and quietly for three years, for fifty-six marks of ready groschen, counting twenty-four scotos for each mark and two groschen for the scotus, by hereditary right and the title of ownership, to be possessed, held, had, sold, exchanged, resigned and turned to such uses as shall seem good, quietly and peaceably, as it shall seem better or more useful to the said Lord Jan, abbot, and his abbey of Ląd. In testimony of this matter the impress of our seal is hung upon these presents. Done and given at Konin on the third day within the octave of the Lord's Ascension, in the year of his birth 1362, in the presence of these witnesses and lords: Wacław the treasurer, Presprawo, banner-bearer of Kalisz, Lasczone the under-huntsman, Marcin, burgrave of Konin, Jaszko called Menczyc, and many others worthy of trust.

Krolikowo, Królikowo. Landensis, of Ląd. Magnum Wronchyno, Wrąbczyn.
kdw-29:
Document no. 1490

Wyrzbenta, castellan of Poznań and the same general captain of Poland, 16 March 1363, at Ląd; attests that Stasco, together with his consort Iachna, sold the third part of the estate of Wrąbczyn to the monastery of Ląd.

Original on parchment. A scrap of parchment from the hanging of the seal. Warsaw. The Rusiecki collection. Diplomata.

We, Wyrzbenta, castellan of Poznań and also general captain of Poland, declare publicly and make known to all and singular, present as much as to come, to whom the present document shall have descended, that there came before us and the other nobles of the land of Poland the noble man Stasco, together with his consort the reverend lady Iachna, heirs of great Wronczino; not compelled, not forced, nor led astray by any vice or error whatsoever, but by the mature counsel of their friends had over this, to the reverend father in Christ Lord Jan, by divine mercy abbot of Ląd, and to the said abbey of St Mary and the monasteries there of the Cistercian Order, they sold, gave, assigned and resigned the third part of the estate commonly called great Wronczino, with all and singular the uses, the revenues and the incomes, and also the jurisdictions which they have or shall be able to have from anyone in the future, for seventy marks of ready groschen, by hereditary right and the title of ownership, to be possessed, held, had, sold, exchanged and turned to whatever uses for all time quietly and peaceably, as it shall seem better and more useful to the said lord abbot and his monastery aforesaid. In testimony of this matter the impress of our seal is hung upon these presents. Done and given at Ląd on the fifth day after the Sunday on which Laetare is sung in the church, in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1363, in the presence of these witnesses: the Lord Lasczone, under-huntsman of Ląd, the Lord Mikołaj of Wysoczsko, Andrzej of Dreczkowo, Laskarz of Sławoszew, Piotrko of Strzałkowo, Jan of Bieganowo, heirs, and many others worthy of trust, specially asked for this.

Magnum Wronczino, Wrąbczyn. Land, Ląd. Wysoczsko, Wysokie. Dreczkowo, Drzeczkowo. Slawosewo, Sławoszew. Stralcowicze, Strzałkowo. Beganowo, Bieganowo.
kdw-30:
Document no. 1491

Wyrzbenta, castellan of Poznań and the same general captain of Poland, 16 March 1363, at Ląd; attests that Mikołaj, subdapifer of the bishop of Poznań, resigned the half of the lordship in the village of Wrąbczyn to the monastery of Ląd.

Original on parchment. On a scrap of parchment hangs a seal showing on a triangular shield the arms of the Niesobia family; the inscription effaced. Warsaw. The Rusiecki collection. Diplomata.

We, Wyrzbenta, castellan of Poznań and also general captain of Poland, acknowledge openly and plainly to all and singular, present as much as to come, whose ears the present document shall have been recited to, that there came before us and the other nobles of the land of Poland the noble man Mikołaj, subdapifer of the venerable father in Christ, the Lord bishop of Poznań, together with his consort the honoured lady Czerska; not compelled, not forced, nor led astray by any scruple of calumny, but with the good deliberation of their mind first had, to the venerable man Lord Jan, by divine patience abbot, and his convent in Ląd of the Cistercian Order, they sold, gave, assigned and resigned the half of the lordship in the village commonly called great Wronczino for fourteen marks of ready groschen, by hereditary right, to be possessed, held, had, sold, exchanged and turned to such uses as shall have pleased their will, for all time. In testimony of this matter the seal of our title is hung upon these presents. Done and given at Ląd on the fifth day after the Sunday on which Laetare is sung in the churches, in the year of the Lord's birth 1363, in the presence of these witnesses: the Lord Lasczone, under-huntsman of Ląd, the Lord Mikołaj of Wysoczko, Andrzej of Dreczkowo, Laskarz of Sławoszew, Piotrko of Strzałkowo, Jan of Bieganowo, heirs.

Magnum Wronczino, Wrąbczyn. Wysoczko, Wysokie. Dreczcowo, Drzeczkowo. Slawosewo, Sławoszew. Stralcowicze, Strzałkowo. Beganowo, Bieganowo.
kdw-31:
Document no. 1519

Wyrzbenta, castellan of Poznań and the same general captain of Poland, 27 April 1364, at Ląd; attests that Dobrocha, heiress of Wrąbczyn, acknowledged that all the substance she possessed was the abbot of Ląd's.

Original on parchment. A scrap of parchment from the hanging of the seal. Warsaw. The Rusiecki collection. Diplomata.

We, Wyrzbenta, castellan of Poznań and also general captain of Poland, acknowledge openly and plainly to all and singular to whom it shall have been needful to know, that there came before us and the other knights of the land of Poland the noble lady named Dobrocha, heiress of great Wronczino, being sound and unharmed by the grace of Jesus Christ, and she acknowledged, protesting publicly, that all the substance she has, both the untamed beasts of burden and the cattle, with the flocks and all the rest that she has and possesses — these are not hers, but the religious man Lord Jan's, by divine mercy abbot in Ląd, and his monastery's in Ląd; yet so, that after the death of the said lady Dobroslawa, neither the children nor any of her friends shall have right or regard in all the substance aforesaid, but the Lord Jan, abbot of Ląd, with his monastery aforesaid. In testimony of this matter the seal of our title is hung upon these presents. Done and given at Ląd on the Saturday after the day of St Mark the evangelist, in the year of the Lord's birth 1364, in the presence of these witnesses and lords: Laurentius, castellan of Ląd, Przesprawo, banner-bearer of Kalisz, Jan of Bieganowo, Henryk of Wola, heirs, and many others worthy of trust.

Magna Wronczino, Wrąbczyn. Land, Ląd. Bieganowo, Wola, today the same; of villages of the last name there are 5 in the neighbourhood of the town of Konin.
kdw-11:
Document no. 1739

Przecław, palatine of Kalisz, and the other judges, 27 May 1377, at Gniezno; declare before King Louis that the villages of Wrąbczynek and Adamierz, with the mill lying near the town of Pyzdry, have belonged to the monastery of Ląd from of old.

Original on parchment. On strips of parchment 6 small round seals are hung. The first is lost; the second is wholly worn; the third shows on a triangular shield the arms of the Poraj family, legend: S. Iohannis d. Nancowo; the fourth shows on a triangular shield the arms of the Zaremba family, legend: ...crol...; the fifth has its impression chipped; the sixth shows on a triangular shield the arms of the Doliwa family, legend worn.

Warsaw. Collections of the Rusiecki family. Diplomata.

To the magnificent prince Louis, King of Hungary and of Poland, Przecław the palatine, Tomisław the judge, Jan the castellan, Mikołaj the under-chamberlain of Kalisz, Wawrzyniec, castellan of Poznań, and Janusz, castellan of Biechowo, their most humble service at every pleasure of his commands. Before your royal majesty and all and each who are present we acknowledge, publicly professing: that little Wrąbczyn with the village of Nadamirza adjoining it, lying near Pyzdry, with all its uses, namely fields, plains, meadows, waters, woods, forests and the lake called Prziborowo, and also the mill lying below the town of Pyzdry, is of the property of the monastery of Ląd of the Cistercian Order; and we declare openly and publicly that this same village, namely little Wrąbczyn with its adjoining village, has belonged from of old, with full and entire lordship and all rights, revenues, fruits and incomes whatsoever, always to the said monastery of Ląd as its true property, as it does now. And in greater evidence of this our declaration we have had the present letters strengthened with our seals. Done and given at Gniezno on the eve of Corpus Christi, in the year of the Lord one thousand three hundred and seventy-seven, we being then gathered there for the general courts.

Behoviensis, of Biechowo. Parvum Wronczino, Wrąbczynek. Nadamirza, Adamierz. Lacus Prziborowo, today a marsh lying north of Wrąbczynek. Landensis, of Ląd.
kdw-12:
Document no. 283

Poznań, 31 January 1384

Mikołaj of Wenecja, judge of Kalisz, adjudges Wrąbczyn(ek) to the Cistercian monastery at Ląd.

Original: Kraków, WAP. D. Dep. 344. Parchment 229–219 × 130–126 + 23 mm. Three holes in the right margin, the bottom frayed. Slits from the strip for hanging the seal. On the back notes on the content and shelfmarks (14th–18th century).

In the name of the Lord, amen. We, Mikołaj, judge of Kalisz¹, make known to all whom it concerns | that at Poznań on the Sunday before the Purification of the glorious Virgin Mary, in the year of the Lord one thousand | three hundred and eighty-four, there came before us Piotrko, heir of Łęg², also | on behalf of his uterine brother, on the one part, and the religious man Rudger, key-keeper and procurator of the brothers and convent of the mo- nastery of Ląd³, on the other, in the presence of the reverend father in Christ Lord Jan, Duke of Opole and Bishop of Poznań⁴, and of the strenuous knights and nobles: Pielgrzym, captain of Poland⁵, Dzierżek, castellan of Santok⁶, Franczek the cupbearer⁷, Stefan the under-cupbearer of Poznań⁸, and of the honourable men: Wojciech, archdeacon of Poznań⁹, Mikołaj, cantor of Poznań¹⁰; and on the peremptory term set for them they went to law before us for the estate called Vronczino¹¹. And we, weighing their causes well on the information of the lords already written and of other elders of the land, adjudged that the said Rudger the key-keeper, in the name of the whole convent of the said monastery, should be given the investiture of the said village, and have adjudged it by these presents, not removing Piotrko or his brother from acting at law against the said village. Provided that they may try for the said village by law, doing no violence to the said monastery. In witness of which we have had our seal hung on these presents. Given and done at Poznań on the day, in the year and at the place above.

¹Mikołaj of Wenecja, see above, no. 228/23.

²Piotr of Łęg near Śrem), most probably the same as the later steward of Kalisz 1392, then deputy judge of Poznań 1393–1398 (Spisy wlkp.; SHGWlkp.). His brother not identified.

³The key-keeper of Ląd, Rudger, not otherwise known.

⁴Jan Kropidło, see above, no. 282/1.

⁵Peregryn, Pielgrzym, of Węgleszyn (in the land of Sandomierz), of the Jelita arms, under-chamberlain of Sandomierz 1379–1400, captain of Greater Poland 1383–1387 (PSB XXV, pp. 602–603).

⁶Dziersław, Dzierżek, Grochola of Ostroróg, of the Nałęcz arms, castellan of Santok 1383–1387 (Spisy wlkp.).

⁷Franciszek of Cerekwica, see above, no. 190/1.

⁸Stefan the under-cupbearer occurs only here; most probably, though, this is the steward of Poznań 1376–1399, Stefan of Trląg and Głogowiec (see above, no. 258/2).

⁹Wojciech of Będlewo, see above, no. 227/17.

¹⁰Mikołaj, cantor of Poznań, confirmed 1380–1384 (here), probably the deputy of (or the same as) Mikołaj Strosberg (see above, no. 250/4).

¹¹Wrąbczyn, just west of Zagórów, or Wrąbczynek (west of Wrąbczyn): in both these settlements, called Wronczyn (Little and Great), the monastery of Ląd later had its shares.
app5314550221-1:
Privilege of Mikołaj, heir, on the boundaries or limits of the village of Makownica. 14.

In the name of the Lord, Amen. For the perpetual memory of the matter. We, Mikołaj, heir of Venacia, general judge of the land of Kalisz, wish it to be known to all and each, present and to come, who will have knowledge of these presents: that, after mature deliberation and sound and sufficient counsel taken on it, desiring, with the help of the Almighty [uncertain: suffragio] first secured, to obtain a saving remedy for our soul and for the souls of our kin, and wishing our heritage, namely Makownica, which had earlier been resigned to our monastery of Ląd in the presence of the Most Serene Prince and Lord, Lord Władysław, by the grace of God illustrious King of Poland etc., and confirmed in perpetuity by his letters patent, to be more fully known and manifest in its bounds and boundaries, we ordered it, according to the custom of our land, a court summoner having been taken, to be marked with [...] or mounds, otherwise kopce in the vernacular, from the boundaries of the village of Malenin up to the boundaries of the heritage called Ruchocin, to dig them, in the vernacular [uncertain: odsuć], and to make the boundary: and so half of the thicket called Kobielnica, which flows or runs, Samica in the vernacular, shall belong in perpetuity to the said heritage of Makownica. We add besides to the foregoing, as a final disposition for a testament: that after our death the said monastery and the whole convent of its brothers of the Cistercian Order shall have, and shall possess peacefully for all time, the substance of all our goods contained there in the aforenamed heritage and [uncertain: postmo] to be contained there, namely the bees, cattle, sheep, mares, beasts, and generally all things, movable as well as immovable. In witness of which, lest it be annulled by those who come after, we have ordered these our letters to be written firmly and have strengthened them with the protection of our seal. Done at Ląd on the Sunday within the octave of Corpus Christi, in the same year 1,399. Present: the discreet man Jakusz, parish priest at [uncertain: Czaten], and the noble men, the lords Jan [uncertain: Siemenci] Pech, castellan of Czarnków, Mikołaj [uncertain: Retch], burgrave of Pyzdry, [uncertain: Vito] Lukomski Jaszko of the same place, and very many others worthy of trust.
kdw-13:
Document no. 2014

Dobrogost, Archbishop of the holy church of Gniezno, 13 October 1399, in the stone room of the monastery of Ląd; adjudges the sheaf tithe of the village of Trąbczyn to the monastery of Ląd against the claim of Jan, parish priest of Trąbczyn.

Włocławek. Liber privilegiorum of the monastery of Ląd, p. 181.

In the name of the Lord, amen. We, Dobrogost, by the grace of God and of the Apostolic See Archbishop of the holy church of Gniezno, make known to all whom it concerns who will have knowledge of these presents that, whereas a matter of dispute had arisen before us between the venerable man Lord Gerard, abbot, and the whole convent of the monastery of Ląd of the Cistercian Order, of our diocese of Gniezno, plaintiffs, on the one part, and the discreet man Jan, rector of the church in Trąbczyn, defendant, on the other, concerning the sheaf tithe of the fields there in Trąbczyn: we therefore, the said parties appearing in person before us, having heard the propositions of the parties and the proofs brought forward which the said parties were wont to use, having taken the counsel of men learned in the law and with the consent, will and assent of the parties themselves, simply and plainly, without the noise and form of a trial, all the windings of lawsuits cut off, having invoked the name of Christ and having Him alone before our eyes and fearing Him, sitting as a tribunal, by this our definitive sentence pronounce, decree and declare in writing: that the sheaf tithe of the fields in Trąbczyn has belonged and belongs, has pertained and pertains, to Lord Abbot Gerard and the said convent, imposing perpetual silence on Jan, the said parish priest of Trąbczyn, concerning that tithe. In testimony and fuller evidence of which we have ordered the present sentence of ours to be written and published by Jan, public notary, our own and the scribe of this cause, and to be strengthened by the hanging of our seal. Done and given in the year of the Lord 1399, in the seventh indiction, in the tenth year of the pontificate of the most holy father and lord in Christ, Lord Boniface the Ninth, Pope by the worthy providence of God, on Monday the thirteenth day of the month of October, in the stone room of the monastery of Ląd, in the presence of the honourable men, the lords Mikołaj Strozberg, provost, Jarosław, archdeacon of Gniezno, and Maciej, rector of the church of Błędów, witnesses to the foregoing.

And I, Jan son of Wojciech of Wielatowo, cleric of the diocese of Gniezno, public notary by imperial authority and scribe of the most reverend father the Lord Archbishop and of this cause, since I was present together with the witnesses named above at all and each of the foregoing while they were (being done) as is set out above, and saw and heard all and each of them being done so, and, being busy with other arduous affairs, had them written by another faithful notary and brought into this public form, at the command of the said Lord Archbishop with the hanging of his seal I have subscribed here and signed it with my usual sign and name, in faith and testimony of the foregoing.

Landensis, of Ląd. Trambczyno, Trąbczyn. Blandowo, Błędów. Wielathow, Wielatowo.
kdw-14:
Document no. 117

1407, 19 November, at Niepołomice.

Władysław II, King of Poland, gives the monastery of Ląd the power to found a town in the village of Zagórów.

In the name of the Lord, amen. For the perpetual memory of the matter. The common good is well served, and the government of the realm is ordered with pleasing moderation, when among the other offices of rule granted from above to princes increase is ordained for each of the parts of the realm, and their conditions are changed both in kind and in particular, in public as well as in private. Therefore we, Władysław, by the grace of God King of Poland, and also supreme prince of the lands of Kraków, Sandomierz, Sieradz, Łęczyca, Kujawy and Lithuania, lord and heir of Pomerania and Ruthenia, etc., make known by the tenor of these presents to all and each, present as well as to come, whom it concerns, that, having had diligent regard to the honesty of praiseworthy life and the constancy of devotion of the religious man Gerhard, abbot, together with the brothers of his convent in Ląd, of the Cistercian Order, by which they have very greatly deserved to be commended in the sight of our majesty, at the urgent and humble requests of the said abbot and convent, wishing (to make) the condition of that convent better and to increase its profits, we give full power and grant every faculty by the tenor of these presents to found a town in their village called Zagórów,¹⁾ lying in our land of Greater Poland and in the district of Konin, and to make it to last for ever: giving and granting to the same town Sogorow(s) all the civic rights which the other towns of our realm enjoy in every way. And so that the said town of Zagórów may the better be founded and become populous, we transfer it from Polish law to the German law which is called of Magdeburg, to last for ever; removing there all Polish rights, ways and customs whatsoever which were wont to disturb the said German law of Magdeburg and might in any way hinder it. We further exempt, absolve and for ever free the advocate, burghers and inhabitants of that town from all jurisdiction and power of all the palatines, castellans, judges, under-judges and any officials (and) servants of our realm, so that they shall in no way have to answer when summoned before them or any of them in causes great or small, nor be bound to pay any penalties; but the townsmen and inhabitants of that town shall answer only before their advocate for the time being, and the advocate before his abbot, or, if the abbot is negligent and remiss in doing justice, then before us or our general assembly, when he has been called and summoned by our letter sealed with our seal, and not otherwise than by his German law of Magdeburg, to those who complain of him; and in criminal and capital causes, such as theft, blood, homicide, maiming of limbs and arson, and any other enormous offences, we give full power and grant by the tenor of these presents every faculty to the advocate of that town for the time being to judge, sentence, correct, punish, chastise and condemn within its bounds and limits, as the German law itself demands and requires in all its points, conditions and clauses, our royal rights however always saved in all things. We also establish in the same town of Zagórów a weekly market day on every Wednesday, to be held for ever without prejudice to the other towns; at which market it shall be lawful and free for all and each merchant and any men to sell, buy, exchange and carry on any trade. In witness of these letters, to which our seal is hung. Given at Niepołomice on the very day of St Elizabeth the widow, in the year of the Lord 1407. In the presence of the reverend fathers in Christ and lords: Mikołaj, Archbishop of the holy church of Gniezno, Wojciech, Bishop of Poznań, Jan of Tarnów, castellan and captain of Kraków, Piotr Kmita of Kraków, Jan Ligęza of Łęczyca, Jakusz of Koniecpol of Sieradz, palatines; our faithful beloved knights and very many others worthy of trust. On the report of the venerable lord(s) vice-chancellor of the Kingdom of Poland, etc.

From the Cologne copy-book of the privileges of Ląd, fol. 3.

¹⁾Zagorów, a town in the voivodeship of Kalisz, district of Konin.
kdw-15:
Document no. 191

1411, 30 November, at Ląd.

Gerhard, abbot of the monastery of Ląd, exchanges with Piotr, schultheiss of Nowe Zagórowo alias Drzewiec, the schultheiss's office in Kownaty for the schultheiss's office in Drzewiec.

In the name of the Lord, amen. Lest things done in time vanish together with the passing of time, it is expedient that every transaction which is to be dealt with hereafter be firmly strengthened by the point of letters and the trustworthy subscription of witnesses. Hence it is that we, Brother Gerhard, abbot in Ląd, of the Cistercian Order, of the diocese of Gniezno, wish all who see or hear this, those to come as well as those of now, to know that, the common consent of our elders having first been had, we have made an exchange, and by the witness of these presents do exchange, by the right, manner and form in which it is the custom to exchange, with the provident man Piotr, schultheiss in Nowe Zagórowo,¹⁾ called alias Drzewiec, and his lawful successors: giving to the said Piotr the schultheiss and his lawful successors a mansus and a half in Kownaty,²⁾ our village, situated there, with the schultheiss's office of that our village of Kownaty, for his other half mansus and all its appurtenances with the schultheiss's office in Drzewiec, our said village, over which the same Piotr the said schultheiss and his lawful successors renounce plainly and wholly, reserving to themselves no right at all in that estate and schultheiss's office, all deceit and fraud excluded; yet on these conditions written below. First, that we have sold and do now sell to the said Piotr the schultheiss a mansus and a half in Kownaty, our said village, for which he has given, paid in full and assigned to us twelve marks of broad groschen, reckoning 48 groschen to each mark, so however that the same schultheiss and his lawful successors shall have and possess three mansi there in Kownaty, our said village, freely and peacefully. Further, from the date of these presents the schultheiss shall have a freedom lasting twenty-four years, and likewise the peasants, reckoning from the time they come, shall know without doubt that they will have twenty years of freedom. We have also given and assigned, and by these presents give and assign, to our said schultheiss one arable iugerum beyond the three said mansi, on which we license him to settle a gardener or gardeners and an innkeeper as he pleases.
