Likewise the same schultheiss may build and set up a bakery, a smith, a shoemaker and a butcher's stall on his estate wherever it seems good to him, with our leave, consent and will. The said schultheiss and his descendants are also bound to us to all the services to which our other schultheisses are bound to serve, for which services both he and his descendants shall have and keep one horse worth three marks of broad groschen; and he and his successors shall have the third penny of every matter judged, and enjoy the same freedom as the schultheisses set up in our other villages have been wont to enjoy until now. Moreover the peasants living in our said village shall, after their freedoms have run out, give, assign and pay in full every year on the feast of St Martin a mark of broad groschen from each mansus. Our said peasants are also bound to give us every year two chickens each at the feast of the Assumption of the Blessed Mary and half a threescore of eggs each at the feast of Easter; and at the great court, which is held every year according to the common custom of the land, the schultheiss is bound to pay, give and assign to us six scots, and the peasants half a mark. Likewise the peasants in our said village shall be bound to plough for us from each mansus three times a year, one iugerum each time. And so that all dispute hereafter over the service and freedom of the peasants may be utterly removed, the peasants of our said village are bound to us in the same way to all things to which the peasants of knights are bound. In testimony of all which and for the strength of lasting firmness, we have had the present letter fortified with our seal and that of our convent. Given in our monastery of Ląd, in the year of the Lord 1411, on the day of St Andrew the Apostle. In the presence of the discreet and religious men, the brothers: Feliks, prior; Filip, the old abbot; Jan, subprior; Goblin, bursar; Syfryd, cellarer; and many others worthy of trust, called and asked specially for this in testimony of all and each of the foregoing.

From the Cologne copy-book of the privileges of Ląd, fol. 29, no. 64, and fol. 36, no. 77.

¹⁾Zagorów, once a small town, today a parish village in the district of Słupca.

²⁾Kownaty, a village in the district of Słupca, parish of Wilczyn.
kdw-16:
Document no. 733

Ląd, 13 June 1414

Notarial instrument. Mikołaj Kicki, archdeacon of Gniezno, attests the handing over of the parish church at Zagórów to the Cistercian monastery at Ląd.

Original: Warsaw, AGAD, parchment document 1930. Parchment 290 × 422–409 + 39 mm. Notary's sign: on 3 steps a cross set in a square, its arms ending in lilies that stand out beyond the square. At the crossing of the arms a four-petalled rosette. At the foot of the cross the letter m. On parchment strips 3 seals in yellow wax: 1. round, about 23 mm across, with the Godziemba arms, legend illegible (of Mikołaj Kicki); 2. pointed oval, about 37 mm wide, with the image of a standing figure under a canopy (?), legend illegible, partly crumbled (of Abbot Gerard?); 3. round, about 50 mm across, with the image of the enthroned Madonna, legend illegible (of the monastery of Ląd). On the back notes on the content and shelfmarks (15th–18th century).

ᵃIn the name of the Lord, amen. We, Mikołaj, archdeacon and canon of the holy church of Gniezno¹, make | known by the tenor of these presents to all that, whereas the venerable and religious men, the brothers Lord Gerard, abbotᵇ, and the convent | of the monastery of Ląd of the Cistercian Order of the diocese of Gniezno² had procured that the parish church in Zagórów of the said diocese³ | be incorporated by the Apostolic See into the said monastery, for bearing the burdens of the hospitality of the said monastery, so that whenever that church fell vacant by the resignation or death of its rector for the time being, the lord abbot with his convent might freely take and lawfully keep bodily possession of that church, without asking the leave of the diocesan of the place or of anyone, and turn its fruits, revenues and incomes to the use of the said monastery, and have the church governed by a fit professed brother of that monastery, removable at the willᶜ of the lord abbot and convent whenever it seems good to them, as is set out more fully in the apostolic letters of the late Gregory the Twelfth⁴ and in the process of the executor appointed for this; in consideration therefore of this hospitality and these burdens the discreet man Lord Paweł, rector of the said church in Zagórów⁵, having special love for the said monastery and wishing that the said grace of incorporation should have its due effect, has of his own will and freely, not compelled nor led astray by fraud, given up and ceded the same church and its possession to the same lord abbot and convent, keeping for himself suitable food and clothing for the rest of his life. And the said Lord Gerard, abbot, with his convent, wishing to repay such great love to the same Lord Paweł with a benefit, has graciously taken the same Lord Paweł into the house of the said monastery for his fitting support. For his food he has assigned him the abbot's table, and for his clothing at each of the Ember seasons through the year a mark and a half, and also one tunic of the cloth usually given to the brothers of the convent, of eight ells, and also a fur, if he needs it, of lambskins, and also four pairs of shoes each year for the rest of his life, all to be faithfully supplied to the same Lord Paweł by the same Lord Gerard, abbot, and his successors and the convent; the same lord abbot shall also be bound to keep at his own cost a servant needed for the service of the said Lord Paweł, whose wages the same Lord Paweł will provide. And the same Lord Paweł has assigned and bequeathed to the said monastery, for the remedy of his soul, all and each of the foregoing things left after his death, in whatever goods or sums of money they may be. And we, Gerard, the said abbot of Ląd, with the brothers of our convent, promise in good faith to hold and keep all the foregoing expressed above to the same Lord Paweł, and to keep them we bind ourselves and our successors in good faith; and if, which God forbid, the foregoing should be broken by us or our successors, and the said Lord Paweł not be provided with the said food and clothing according to the needs of a priest's state, as is expressed above, then, lest the same Lord Paweł be seen to beg and suffer want to the shame and disgrace of the honour of the clergy, it shall be lawful for him to have recourse to taking the fruits, revenues and incomes of the same church and maintaining himself from them, in which fruits he is not to be disturbed in any way by us or our successors. And if he should be disturbed, then of our own will and freely we subject ourselves and our successors in this respect to the jurisdiction and coercion of the said Lord Mikołaj, archdeacon, and his successors, and we take upon ourselves the sentences of excommunication and interdict, in so far as he shall have pronounced them against us and the said monastery and the church of the monastery for the foregoing, and promise to obey them and keep the church interdict, renouncing in the foregoing the privileges of exemption of the said monastery and order granted by any Roman pontiffs or other ordinaries, and also the exceptions and appeals and the help of the laws and canons that belong or might in any way belong to us and our said successors, by which the said submission and coercion to be done by the said lord archdeacon might in any way be hindered, which we wish to avail us and our successors in nothing. In faith and testimony of all and each of the foregoing we have ordered these present letters or this present public instrument to be written and published by the notary written below and to be strengthened by the hanging of our seals and those of the said convent. Done and given in the monastery of Ląd in the year of the Lord one thousand four hundred and fourteen, in the seventh indiction, in the fifth year of the pontificate of the most holy father and our lord in Christ, Lord John the Twenty-third, Pope by divine providence, on Wednesday the thirteenth day of the month of June, at about the sixth hour, there being present the religious men, the lords: Jan, prior⁶, Feliks, rector of the parish church in Ląd⁷, Goblin, bursar⁸, Syfryd, cellarer⁹, and Gerard, brothers¹⁰ of the said convent of Ląd, and also the noble and discreet Trojan and Marcin, heirs of Kiki¹¹, and Przybysław, servant of the church of Zagórów¹², witnesses called and asked specially to the foregoing.

Notary's sign. And I, Maciej, son of the late Jan Linko, cleric of Gniezno, public notary by imperial authority¹³, since I was present together with the witnesses named above at the said giving up, promise and ordinance and at all and each of the foregoing while they were being done and made as is set out above, and saw and heard them done so, therefore, writing with my own hand, I have subscribed here and brought this into this public form, signing it with my usual and accustomed sign and name, asked and requested, in faith and testimony of all and each of the foregoing.

ᵃAn initial the height of the whole text of the original.

ᵇabb as in the original, an erasure in the middle.

ᶜreading not quite certain. Mikołaj Kicki, see above, no. 439/8.

²Abbot Gerhard, see above, no. 412/9.

³Zagórów, a town in the district of Konin, the property of the monastery of Ląd.

⁴Gregory XII, Roman pope 1406–1409 (1415), d. 1417. His letter concerning Zagórów not otherwise known.

⁵The parish priest Paweł not otherwise known, though perhaps the same as the one mentioned in the necrology of Ląd (MPH V, p. 498).

⁶The prior Jan not identified.

⁷The parish priest Feliks occurs only here, perhaps the same as the monastery's steward of 1395 (KDW VI, no. 342/5), prior in 1411 (KDW V, no. 191), d. 1418 (MPH V, p. 484).

⁸Gobelin occurs already in 1411 (KDW V, no. 191) and still in 1431 and 1433 (KDW IX); compare also MPH V, pp. 492, 498, and the prior of that name in 1402 and 1404 (KDW V, pp. 27 and 37).

⁹Zewrzyd occurs as cellarer from 1402 (KDW V, pp. 28 f.), perhaps the same as the later abbot Zygfryd 1418–1428, d. 1429 (MPH V, p. 494).

¹⁰Gerard not identified.

¹¹Kiki in the land of Sieradz (Zajączkowscy, Materiały, I, p. 129). Trojan and Marcin were probably kinsmen (brothers?) of Mikołaj Kicki.

¹²Przybysław occurs only here.

¹³Maciej not identified.
kdw-17:
Document no. 755

Gniezno, 16 April 1415

The captain general of Greater Poland attests that Święszek and Olbracht (?), brothers of Gulczewo, sold a plot in the suburb of Gniezno to the Cistercian monastery of Ląd.

Copy: Włocławek, Diocesan Archive, Cistercians – Ląd, MS 3 (Liber privilegiorum monasterii, 18th century), p. 173.

In the name of the Lord, amen. For the perpetual memory of the matter. We, Jan of Szczekociny, castellan of Lublin and captain general of Greater Poland¹, make known by the tenor of these presents to all whom it concerns, present and to come, who will have knowledge of these presents, that, coming before us and other nobles of the same land, Swanseck and Supracht, brothers german of Gulczewo², not compelled, not forced, nor led astray by any error, relying on the counsel of their friends, being sound in mind and body, have duly and reasonably sold for ever to the venerable man Lord Gerhard, abbot, and his convent of the monastery of Ląd³ their whole plot with the square, lying near the church of St Lawrence in the suburb of Gniezno, for sixteen marks of common current money, of Polish reckoning, reckoning forty-eight groschen to each mark, with all its uses, appurtenances and divisions in length and breadth in any way belonging to that plot, and with all right and lordship as they alone held and had it, reserving nothing of right for themselves and theirs, and have resigned it before us in the usual way for ever, to be held, had, used and enjoyed, exchanged, sold and turned to their own pleasure, as shall seem better and more useful to the said Gerhard and his convent of the monastery of Ląd. In witness of these, to which our seal is hung. Done and given at Gniezno on the Tuesday next after Misericordia Domini Sunday, in the year of His incarnation one thousand four hundred and fourteenᵃ, in the presence of the noble men: Piotr of Gunice⁴, Mikołaj of Trąbczyn⁵, Andrzej of the same⁶, Pełka of Kuchary⁷, Jan [ofᵇ] Świniary⁸, Mikołaj of Grabienice⁹ and many other witnesses worthy of trust, called and asked specially to the foregoing.

ᵃSo the copy, but this must be a copyist's error (quarto – quinto), since in 1414 Jan of Szczekociny was not yet captain of Greater Poland. The date 1415 agrees with his itinerary; see the next document.

ᵇmissing in the copy.

¹Jan of Szczekociny, see above, no. 635/6.

²Gulczewo (Golczewo), parish of Marzenin, north of Września (Koz. 1, pp. 54, 89, 412; 3, pp. 560, 671; 4, p. 239). Świętosław (Święszek) occurs 1404–1447 (SHGWlkp.), later for many years burgrave and salt-mine administrator (żupca) at Gniezno, Pyzdry and Konin, 1418–1447 (GUrz., p. 171); compare also MPH V, p. 476. His brother Supracht, Czupracht, occurs only here; compare however Czuprachtowe Gulczewo (Koz., l.c.).

³Abbot Gerard, see above, no. 412/9.

⁴Piotr of Gonice, see above, no. 433/1.

⁵⁻⁶Trąbczyn, a parish village south-east of Zagórów (Koz. 5, p. 414). Mikołaj occurs from 1402 (SHGWlkp.), later deputy standard-bearer at Gniezno 1434–1440 (GUrz. C 95). Andrzej occurs 1414 (here) to 1428 (SHGWlkp.).

⁷Kuchary Kościelne, a parish village north-west of Rychwał (Koz. 4, p. 432). Pełka, deputy standard-bearer at Konin 1411–1414, burgrave 1414–1416, then often an assessor of the court at Konin (GUrz. C 472, 363, 412).

⁸Świniary, parish of Kłecko, north-east of Kłecko (Koz. 1, p. 317; 5, p. 379). Jan occurs 1396–1426 (SHGWlkp.).

⁹Grabienice, a parish village north-west of Rychwał in the Konin land (Koz. 4, pp. 260–261). Mikołaj occurs 1413–1428 (SHGWlkp.).
kdw-18:
Document no. 280

1418, 3 June, at Ląd.

Zygfryd, abbot of the monastery of Ląd, exchanges with the peasant Wawrzyniec Jeleniowicz the farm in Wronczyno Wielkie for the farm in Drzewce.

In the name of the Lord, amen. For the perpetual memory of the matter. Since among the goods of human nature nothing is held worthier than memory, it is fitting that the acts of men be made lasting by the points of letters and the noting of witnesses, lest they vanish with the passing of time. Therefore we, Zygfryd, abbot, and the whole convent of the monastery of Ląd, of the Cistercian Order, make known by the tenor of these presents to all whom it concerns, present and to come, who will have knowledge of these presents, how, wishing to increase the goods of our monastery with the gain of profits, and to bring its fruits and revenues to betterment in the time of our rule, and because (between) us, the convent, on the one part, and the provident Wawrzyniec Jeleniowicz, peasant of Great Wronczyn¹⁾, we have made and agreed such a perpetual and irrevocable exchange: that to the same Wawrzyniec Jeleniowicz and his descendants and lawful successors we have given, granted, inscribed and exchanged for ever our farm in Great Wronczyn, with the fields belonging to it of old and with the meadows there called Obroczna and Dokolowka, for our other farm in Drzewce,²⁾ which he had formerly bought from Brother Henryk of good memory, abbot, our predecessor, for a certain sum of money, namely for fifteen marks of current money, reckoning forty-eight groschen to each mark, by a true exchange duly and reasonably made by us with him, and we give, grant, inscribe and exchange it for ever. To this Wawrzyniec and his descendants we have also assigned and exchanged by these presents, by reason of his beehives, which are called barcz, standing between our estates of Great Wronczyn and Zagórów, which he had and held in our forest, four gardeners there in Great Wronczyn, who formerly belonged to our court. And this Wawrzyniec and his successors shall be bound and obliged to pay us, the convent, and our successors as rent one mark and a half in such money as his other neighbours and our people of the said farm in Great Wronczyn pay on the feast of St Martin: adding also to him and his descendants one weir called yaz, for fishing freely in the stream, otherwise strumyen, flowing and standing between the estates of Skrzynica and Kościół. Moreover the same Wawrzyniec and his descendants are to give the sheaf tithe from all the fields and ploughlands of the said farm to no one else but us and the convent: this being added and specially expressed, that the said Wawrzyniec and his descendants shall be bound and obliged to perform and do any services for us and the convent at our command, and to defend, guard and look after our forest and woods from damages and dangers with our help. In witness of these letters, to which our seal and that of the convent are hung. Done and given in our monastery of Ląd on the Friday after the octave of Corpus Christi, in the year of the Lord 1418. In the presence of these lords: the venerable Donin, protonotary of the Apostolic See, dean of Kraków, vice-chancellor of the Kingdom of Poland, Dobek Kobyła, etc.

From the Cologne copy-book of the privileges of Ląd, fol. 35.

¹⁾Wronczyn, a village in the district of Poznań.

²⁾Drzewce: which of the many villages of this name it was, I cannot judge. In the district of Poznań there is no village of this name.
kdw-19:
Document no. 2000

Trąbczyn, 15 May 1434

Notarial instrument. Wojciech of Trąbczyn, canon of Kruszwica, authorises his brother Jan of Trąbczyn to collect a debt from Jarand, scholastic of Kruszwica.

Copy: Kal. 9175, p. 373. Title: Mandatum ad levandum debitum.

Remarks: 1. On the date see below, note a; 2. See also the next document.

In the name of the Lord, amen. In the year from His birth 1435ᵃ, in the twelfth indiction, in the fourth year of the pontificate of the most holy father in Christ and our lord, Lord Eugenius the Fourth, Pope by divine providence, on Saturday, the eve of Pentecost, at about the hour of terce, in the house of the noble Mścichnaᵇ, wife of Otto, heir in Trąbczyn, the honourable Lord Wojciech, son of Otto of Trąbczyn, canon of Kruszwica¹, being present in person, in all the better manner, way, form of law and style in which he could, made, set up and solemnly appointed as his true, lawful and undoubted proctor, agent, factor and manager of his affairs the noble Jan, his brother german, heir in Trąbczyn², who was present and took the charge of the proxy upon himself of his own will, giving him full and every power to demand, take, collect and dispose of at his pleasure, receive, and make a pact of not asking further, from the venerable man Lord Jarand, scholastic of Kruszwica, canon of the churches of Włocławek and Wieluń³, seventy Hungarian florins, on account of the agreement made by the venerable lords Jan of Niewiesz, dean⁴, Świętosław of Wrząca, archdeacon and official of Włocławek⁵, Maciej Dryja, dean⁶, and Mikołaj of Głęboczek, archdeacon of Poznań⁷, concerning the canonry and prebend of the collegiate church of Wieluń between Wojciech on the one part and Jarand on the other, to give letters of quittance under his name and seal, and in general to do all and each of the things that are needful concerning what has been so received, collected and acquitted. Concerning all which etc.

And I, Jo(hannes)⁸ etc., since at the said appointment and all the other things etc.

ᵃSo the copy, instead of quarto, as follows from the other elements of the dating (indiction, pontificate); but it cannot be ruled out that this is a dating in the Pisan style.

ᵇSo the copy.

¹Trąbczyn, a parish village south-east of Zagórów in the Konin land (Koz. 5, p. 414). Otto, Ota, occurs still in 1426 (Roty V, no. B455). Mścichna, Otto's wife, not otherwise known. Her son Wojciech, canon of Kruszwica, not otherwise known.

²Jan of Trąbczyn, son of Otto, brother of the canon Wojciech and of a younger brother, Tomasz Ocic, hard to tell apart from his namesake who occurs at the same time in Trąbczyn.

³Jarand son of Stanisław, scholastic of Kruszwica and canon of Włocławek already in 1432 (BullPol V, no. 111), most probably the same as Jarand of Niewiesz, later also canon of Gniezno in 1441 and official in 1450–51, d. 1451 (GąsSkOf, pp. 79, 85).

⁴Jan son of Chebda of Niewiesz.

⁵Świętosław son of Alberyk of Wrząca (north-east of Koło), canon of Włocławek 1412, custodian 1426, canon of Płock 1413, of Poznań 1429, archdeacon and official of Włocławek, d. 1471 (Radzimiński II, pp. 147–148).

⁶Maciej Dryja of Modliszewo.

⁷Mikołaj of Głęboczek.

⁸The public notary Jan of Łęczyca (as in the next document) not identified. [Ju]
kdw-20:
Document no. 1520

Buda, 10 August 1440

King Władysław III charges 300 marks on the villages of Wrąbczynek, Adamierz and Borzykowo in favour of Stanisław Czarny.

Copy: Warsaw, AGAD, Metryka koronna, vol. 109, pp. 11–12. Entered on 27 April 1570 (from the original).

We, Władysław, by the grace of God King of Hungary, Poland, Dalmatia, Croatia, etc., supreme prince of Lithuania and heir of Ruthenia, etc., make known by the tenor of these presents to all that we have received from the noble Stanisław Czarny, our beloved and faithful familiar¹, a horse or charger for one hundred marks of money and of Polish reckoning by a contract of market; and for his services which he has done for our majesty on this Hungarian journey to take up the insignia of our happy coronation, now by God's gift accomplished, we give him two hundred marks; of which three hundred marks of money and of Polish reckoning, reckoning XLXVIIIᵃ gr(oschen) to each mark, together and jointly, assuringᵇ the said Stanisław and his descendants, wishing it, we give, donate, show and inscribe to him by these presents the same three hundred marks in and upon our villages of Wrąbczynek², Adamierz³ and Borzykowo, lying in the district of Pyzdry⁴, to be had, held, used and enjoyed and peacefully possessed by the same Stanisław and his lawful successors with all the uses of the said villages, fruits, rents, revenues, incomes, fields, meadows, plains, woods, heaths, rivers, ponds, fisheries, mills, emoluments, appurtenances and incomes whatsoever [p. 12], for so long until the said three hundred marks are paid to him or his successors in full. When they are paid, the possession of the said villages shall return to us and our successors with full right. Our royal hospitality dues always saved. In faith of which our seal is hung on these presents. Given at Buda on the Wednesday of the feast of St Lawrence the Martyr, in the year of the Lord one thousand four hundred and forty⁵.

On the report of the magnificent Mikołaj of Szarlej, castellan of Wł(ocławek)⁶.

ᵃSo the copy, instead of XLVIII.

ᵇSo the copy, instead of assecurare.

ᶜSo the copy.

¹Stanisław Czarny, see above, no. 1479/1.

²Wrąbczynek, parish of Zagórów; Niedamierz, today Adamierz, parish of Zagórów; and Borzykowo, parish of Pyzdry: royal villages near Pyzdry.

³Wrąbczynek, parish of Zagórów; Niedamierz, today Adamierz, parish of Zagórów; and Borzykowo, parish of Pyzdry: royal villages near Pyzdry.

⁴Wrąbczynek, parish of Zagórów; Niedamierz, today Adamierz, parish of Zagórów; and Borzykowo, parish of Pyzdry: royal villages near Pyzdry.

⁵The date agrees with the king's itinerary.

⁶Mikołaj Szarlejski of Ściborze, castellan of Inowrocław, later palatine of Brześć, one of the commanders at Chojnice in 1454, captain of Bydgoszcz, d. 1457?
kdw-21:
Document no. 1532

Buda, 22 November 1440

King Władysław III charges 200 marks on the villages of Adamierz, Borzykowo and Wrąbczynek in favour of Stanisław Czarny.

Copy: Warsaw, AGAD, Metryka koronna, vol. 109, pp. 8–9. Entered on 27 April 1570 (from the original).

Mention: MRPS V, no. 4154 (from the copy).

We, Władysław, by the grace of God King of Hungary, Poland, Dalmatia, Croatia, etc., supreme prince of Lithuania and heir of Ruthenia, etc., make known by the tenor of these presents to all whom it concerns that, having regard to the faithful services of the noble Stanisław Czarny of Pietrzyków¹, beloved by us, shown to us faithfully and constantly for a long time and especially in the preparation of the happy coronation of this our Kingdom of Hungary, and to be shown by him still more diligently in future, we give him for their sake two hundred marks of Polish reckoning and money [p. 9], reckoning 48 g(roschen) to each mark, in and upon our villages of Adamierz², Borzykowo³ and Wrąbczynek, of the district of Pyzdry⁴, which we have allowed him to free from the hands of the noble Bartosz Płomikowskiᵃ ⁵, ᵇ⁻ᶜwe give, donate

and inscribe by these presents, we bestow them on him with all the uses, fruits, rents, revenues, incomes, fields, meadows, plains, woods, heaths, all ponds, fisheries, waters, mills, emoluments, beehives, emolumentsᵈ, fowling, appurtenances and incomes whatsoever, to be had, held, used and peacefully possessed for so long until the said two hundred marks are paid to him or his descendants in full by us or our successors. When they are paid, the possession of the said villages shall return to us and our successors with full right. Our royal rights and hospitality dues always saved. In witness of these letters, to which our seal is hung below. Given at Buda on the Tuesday after the feast of St Elizabeth, in the year of the Lord 1440⁶.

The report of the generous Andrzej of Tęczyn⁷.

ᵃSo the copy.

ᵇ⁻ᶜSo the copy (praesens).

ᵈSo the copy (word repeated).

¹See above, no. 1520.

²See above, no. 1520.

³See above, no. 1520.

⁴See above, no. 1520.

⁵Bartosz of Płomykowo (today Płonkowo in Kujawy), not more closely known.

⁶The date agrees with the king's itinerary.

⁷Andrzej Tęczyński, son of Andrzej, castellan of Wojnicz, captain of Rabsztyn 1441, of Chełm 1455, d. 1461.
app5314550221-3:
Confirmation of Grądzyń by King Kazimierz. 16.

In the name of the Lord, Amen. For the perpetual memory of the matter. We, Kazimierz, by the grace of God King of Poland, and also of the lands of Kraków, Sandomierz, Sieradz, Łęczyca and Kuyavia, Grand Duke of Lithuania, lord and heir of Pomerania and Prussia etc., make known by the tenor of these presents to all whom it concerns, present and to come, who will have knowledge of them, how, coming to our presence and that of our prelates and barons

the venerable and religious Maciej, abbot of the monastery of Ląd, our devout and beloved, made known to us by his statement that he had made a contract of purchase with the noble Mikołaj, Jan and Warsz, brothers german of Koscielec, heirs, and with their stepson, for three mansi or łany of fields lying in the village of Łukomia in the district of Konin, and for the forest called Grądzyń, and also other forests and woods, meadows, fields, heaths, fishponds, beehives, waters and their courses, and all other profits, uses and revenues belonging in any way of old to the said three mansi or łany, as the heirs written above have possessed them until now, reserving to themselves and their successors no right of property or dominion in them; and humbly and devoutly besought our majesty with due instance that we might give our gracious consent and assent to the said contract of purchase. We, then, wishing to buy heavenly things for earthly ones and to enlarge divine worship in that venerable monastery of Ląd, and especially considering the lack of forests and woods, with which that monastery might be restored in its [uncertain: Casanis] and old ruins, since it lacks them elsewhere, namely forests and woods; and so that, for our happy arrival when we happen to come down there, the necessaries might be had the better: graciously inclined to the prayers of the said abbot, we have given our gracious will to the said contract of purchase of the said three łany, forests, woods and all other appurtenances, made, as is touched on above, by the abbot himself and his convent; we have assented, and by these presents assent, decreeing that it shall have the strength of perpetual validity. In witness of which our seal is hung on these presents. Done at Gniezno on the Tuesday before the feast of St Lawrence the Martyr, in the year of the Lord [uncertain: 1,447]. Present: the Reverend Father, Lord Andrzej, bishop, and the magnificent and noble Łukasz of Górka, of Poznań, and Marcin of [uncertain: Rasko], of Kalisz, voivodes; [uncertain: Dobrogosto] of Szamotuły, of Poznań, Przedbor of Koniecpol, of Sandomierz, and Piotr of Kurów, of Sącz, castellans; and many other witnesses worthy of trust to the present. Given by the hands of the magnificent Jan of Koniecpol, chancellor, and Piotr of [uncertain: Tczenaczmy], vice-chancellor, our sincerely beloved.
app5314550221-2:
Privilege "Gradziem Ruchowia". 15.

In the name of the Lord, Amen. For the perpetual memory of the matter. We, Piotr of Szamotuły, castellan of Poznań, general captain of Greater Poland, make known by the tenor of these presents to all whom it concerns: that, coming to our knowledge and to the presence of other nobles of the same land, the honourable and noble lords Jan

Jan Wochneth, parish priest at Koscielec, Mikołaj Wochneth of Bartodzieje, and [uncertain: Barlyus] Wochneth of Osiecza, three brothers german, undivided; and also the honourable and noble Marcin Bochneth, Jan Bochneth and Maciej Bochneth, brothers german, heirs german of the aforesaid Jan Bochneth, parish priest at Koscielec, of Mikołaj of Bartodzieje and of [uncertain: Wardzch] of Osiecza, undivided in their said goods with their said paternal uncles; not compelled, not forced, nor led astray by any other error, but sound in mind and body, having used the wholesome counsel of their friends and having first deliberated maturely among themselves, resigned in perpetuity three whole mansi with gardens in the village and heritage of Łukom in the district of Konin, lying in the parish of Zagórów; the forest Grądzyń with the woods and groves and the Pyzdry mounds; with the forest Chmielniki and with the forest Lome, up to the road called Rosiszewska, which goes from Łukom and the village of Lomowo to the hill Karczemne gory, and the marshes otherwise called Karczemne Lugi; and with the field above Imielno; and with all right, dominion and property, as they alone held, had and possessed them, reserving for themselves and their lawful successors no right whatever of dominion or property in them; with all and singular plots, courts, houses, barns, fields, meadows, pastures, grasslands, forests, woods, groves, thickets, enclosures, brushwood, oak woods, scrub, pine woods, hills, rises, [uncertain: Stenis], marshes, lakes, ponds, peasants, labours, burdens, gardens and gardeners, and generally with all and singular useful fruits, incomes and revenues, by whatever name and word they are called, belonging and pertaining in any way to the said mansi and the other goods described and designated above, far and wide, as the said mansi are marked off and bounded round about in their bounds and limits; for four hundred marks of good broad middle groschen of the coin and count customary in Poland, reckoning forty-eight groschen to each mark; to the Reverend Father, Lord Cornelius, abbot, and the religious Jan, prior, and Wolmar, rector of the parish church at Ląd, and to the whole convent of the monastery of Ląd, having for this the consent and special will of the Most Serene Prince and Lord, Lord Kazimierz, by the grace of God King of Poland etc., our most gracious lord: for the said lords the abbot, the prior and the whole convent and their successors to hold, have and possess, to use and enjoy, to sell, alienate, exchange, give, donate, and turn to their own uses and pleasure, as shall seem better and more useful to them and their successors for the time being. In witness of which our seals are hung beneath these presents. Done and given at Pyzdry on the Monday next after the feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, in the year 1,461. Present there the well-born and noble lords Jan Swidwa the younger, Jan Sobocki, burgrave of Poznań, Mikołaj Kamski, [uncertain: Gavisso] Gorecki, Mikołaj Dabrowski, Krystyn Goszdychowski, and many others worthy of trust in the matters above.

app536017-1:
Łukomski shall carry out the judicial site inspection

Disputes having arisen between the underwritten parties upon a written citation of the Konin land court, whereby the Honourable Albertus Thrąmpczyński Otha, acting from his own interest as Plaintiff, has cited the Honourable Thomas Łukomski for the second time after the penalty of contumacy — for this reason: that he himself, in the present year, having constructed a pond together with his other neighbours, with whom he has reserved to himself his right of action intact, in the estate of the village of Łukom — by which pond he has flooded, so far as concerns the interest of that same Plaintiff, an enormous quantity of woodland and pine forest, of barren pastures and also of meadowlands, through the excessive retention of water, in the same estates of the villages of Trąbczyn, Nowa Wieś and Osiny — namely: drowned and dried up, through that flooding, the timber of common productive oak, beech and ash, suitable for building and for bee-trees —

doing the aforesaid to the grave damage and injury of the Plaintiff, of the value of ten thousand Hungarian florins of pure gold and of just weight, and as much again in damages; the citation itself, with its copy, setting out the aforesaid more fully.

The present land court of Konin, having heard the disputes of the aforesaid parties made before the present court, at the legal request of the cited party, adhering to the common law, has decreed and by these presents decrees a judicial site inspection; and none the less it has added, as by these presents it adds, a land court Messenger, whom the cited party shall choose for itself, namely to see and to inspect in what place and on whose ground the aforesaid injury was inflicted, and whether it was done or not. Which judicial site inspection the cited party, at its own expense, having hired the Messenger, from the date of the present decree, within exactly six

weeks, the consent of the parties being added thereto, is bound to carry out at the place of the differences, under the penalties [uncertain: raised], to be won and lost by the cited party in default of the carrying out. At which inspection both parties are bound to be present. And so, whether the inspection has been carried out as aforesaid or not, both the aforesaid parties shall have, at the next future land court terms of Konin, to be held next and immediately at Konin, a peremptory term to hear, upon the aforesaid inspection, the restitution of right before the court through the Messenger, and to do all else that shall be of law in the present cause — the present decree of inspection, the keeping of the term, and the record, with no party's right harmed.
app536036-1:
The Trąmpczyńskis, in default

The Honourable Jerzy Chełmski, plaintiff: the Honourables Marcin, Wojciech, Władysław and Andrzej, full blood brothers of the Otto-Trąmpczyński family, sons of the late Stanisław, and likewise Anna of Słończyce, widow of the same late Stanisław Trąmpczyński, and lady dower-holder and life-tenant of the goods left by his death, being cited before the present Konin land court in respect of all their goods generally — the minors, if any there be, together with their guardians [uncertain: assigned to them] — for the reason that they themselves, not content with the prior injuries, damages and grievances, through the sending in of their own subjects against that same plaintiff, into the pinewood of that same plaintiff's own village of Łukom, made notches on trees after the manner of boundary marks, eighty on this side or beyond, and cut them, and procured others who did in fact cut them — intending by such an act to annex a great part of the ground of that same plaintiff, his own, and to appropriate it to their own ground — doing the aforementioned things to the serious detriment of the plaintiff, which he reckons for himself against them, the ground itself left untouched, at one thousand Polish marks, and damages of the same amount, or as the court shall decree; and that none the less, the office of the Sub-chamberlain having been brought out, they shall annul the same marks, the penalties being paid —

[Translator's note: Lat. ad instar signorum granicialium — "after the manner of boundary marks" — describing the tree notches as functionally equivalent to formal boundary marks, which is the legal basis of the complaint. The defendants are alleged to have created de facto boundary evidence on Chełmski's own land.]

the citation concerning the aforementioned matters being fuller — them, lawfully proclaimed through the General Royal Messenger, the Honest Mikołaj Jaworowski of Karmin, and not appearing at the first term, he has judicially condemned in the penalty of contumacy, the same court admitting it.

And here standing in person, the General Royal Messenger, the Worthy Bartłomiej Koelmarek of Łukom, openly acknowledged that he had laid the citation issued on account of the aforementioned matters, on the Monday last past,

at the manor of the cited, in the village of Trąbczyn, in the presence of the household of the house.
app536036-2:
A similar [judgment] against the same [defendants], in these words: for the reason that they themselves, not content with prior injuries — nay, adding injury to injury — to the desolation of the pinewoods and forests belonging to the village and estate of Łukom, in those same woodlands and forests recently cut trees of various kinds suitable for building, especially pines, approximately one hundred, but for firewood three hundred cartloads, on this side or beyond, and converted them to whatever use they wished — doing the aforementioned things to the serious detriment of the plaintiff, which he reckons for himself against them, the ground itself left untouched, at three hundred Polish marks. The remainder from the preceding [entry] to the end.

[Translator's note: Lat. iniuriam iniuriae addendo — literally "adding injury to injury" — iniuriam accusative (the injury being added), iniuriae dative (to the prior injury). A standard legal intensifier characterising the defendants' conduct as aggravated and repeated.]

app536040-1:
Done in Konin, in the particular land courts of the same district, on the Monday nearest after the Sunday Septuagesima in the year of the Lord one thousand seven hundred and twenty-eight — this from the adjournment made by that same court on the Monday next after the Feast of Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist, most recently passed, in the now-elapsed year one thousand seven hundred and twenty-seven — lawfully proceeding and arriving at the present day.

Between the Honourables Chełmski and the Honourable Prusimski — Decree of Location.

In the judicial cause and action described below, instituted and initiated — having fallen to the party cited below, at a sitting of the particular land courts here in Konin held on the Monday nearest after the feast of the Most Holy and Undivided Trinity in the most recently elapsed year 1727 — by the plaintiff party named below, but not then decided owing to the press of business at that time, and remaining and pending in the dockets awaiting adjudication among other causes: — the instigator of the present court and his informants, the Honourables Franciszek and Józef Ścibor Chełmscy, heirs and possessors of the goods of the villages of Łukom, Łomowo, and others belonging thereto, plaintiffs — have cited before the present Kalisz land court and the particular land terms of the district of Konin — the Honourables Krzysztof Prusimski as principal defendant, and further Antoni Prusimski his son, and the noblemen Niłecki, Kałuzoski, Jerzmanoski, Cieszkoski, Zdzęnicki, Tomaszeski, as retainers, and other noblemen whose surnames are at present unknown and are to be stated at the time of the session, and likewise the subjects of the goods of Trąbczyn whose names are at present unknown but are to be specified after they become known — the co-principals carrying out the orders of the same Honourable Prusimski — in respect of their persons and goods in general, and of any and all sums of money held and to be held — the sons with their parents, the retainers and subjects with their lords, to adhere to the protest made or to be made by [the plaintiffs] against the same — cited for the penalties prescribed by the laws of the Kingdom, which they have indeed incurred and merited, for the reason that the same Honourable Prusimski, having observed no neighbourly friendship and having given no consideration to it — nay, having set it altogether aside — not content with prior damages, acts of violence, injuries, and grievances — which, for the sake of preserving

the friendship that belongs to living as neighbours, have up to this time not yet been submitted to the public records of the Kingdom and set out — most particularly, at a certain time to be stated at the hearing of the cause, ordered shingles, otherwise called Szkudeł, a hundred sixties (kopy) of them — six thousand shingles — prepared on the plaintiff's own estate and present there, together with a certain dwelling (gaza) to be burned by fire; and he was unwilling, despite being frequently called upon, to make good the damages caused thereby; and suffered the force of that same over-kindled fire to all but consume the children dwelling in that same dwelling (gaza) and endure it for anyone to suffer — and most recently, at a time to be declared at the session, ordered four plough-oxen kept for the use of the glassworks (officina vitraria) to be seized, without any pretext or claim, on the plaintiff's own estate, during his violent invasion of it in arms and in a band, to be detained by him for some time, to be deprived of their labour, and damage to be caused thereby — nay, on the occasion of a demand made by the Honourable Józef Chełmski, to scheme against his very life — not in the least satisfied with these things, and although he knew full well that the present plaintiffs had attended to their business at the ordinary general courts and at the tribunals of the Kingdom at Piotrków, and were residing there amid the various persons and causes there being pursued — he dared to instruct that same Honourable son of his and the above-mentioned retainers and subjects to commit additional violence upon [the plaintiffs]; and those so instructed were ordered to invade the plaintiffs' own estate, which belongs from antiquity to the goods of Łukom and has been in continuous use, with an armed force in groups, with sabres (frameis), with long and short firearms (bombardis) and other kinds of weaponry, forcibly and violently, and by such means — allegedly appropriating that same estate to themselves — to seize the hay gathered into carts from that same estate, in no small number of cartloads, to see to it that it be [uncertain: conveyed] to the goods of Trąbczyn, and thereby to cause the loss of livestock, and to carry out other acts of violence to be proven by full inquisition — through which they incurred penalties — for the decreeing of which penalties and for restitution of damages they are cited — the citation itself with its fuller copy in respect of the foregoing existing against them — the present Kalisz land court, in the particular land terms of the district of Konin, [examining] the controversies of both aforementioned parties — the plaintiff party of the Honourable Chełmski appearing personally through the Honourable Józef Chełmski in his own name and in the name of his brother, and the cited party of the Honourables Prusimski, husband and wife,

and of the other defendants appearing before it through the Honourable Konstanty Marszyński, and contesting judicially — having heard what was judicially done in the foregoing — deciding the term of the plaintiff party, instituted before the present court on account of the appropriation of the estate and of the violence and damages caused: since the cause of the estate is being ventilated before its own court, it finds that a commissarial descent of the Sworn Commissioner of the Palatinates of Poznań and Kalisz together with two arbitrators to be appointed from each side is necessary — decreeing that both parties together shall convey, at their mutual cost, the aforesaid Honourable Commissioner, namely the Honourable Albertus Biskupski, chosen by their mutual consent, and two arbitrators each, to and at the estate from which the controversy between the inheritances of the goods of Łukom and Trąbczyn has arisen on the Monday nearest after the Sunday Misericordiae; and the said Honourable Commissioner and arbitrators shall inquire both into the ownership of the disputed estate and into the transgressions and damages caused as set out in the protests of both parties, shall conduct sworn inquiries (inquisitiones juratorias) in that name through sworn witnesses of advanced age well acquainted with the matter, and shall decide and adjudicate whatever is found by them among the parties according to justice and equity in all their claims — save for the right of appeal from the definitive sentence alone, reserved and safeguarded for the party that feels itself aggrieved, [such appeal] only to the present court, however — and both parties are to perform all the foregoing, [the default penalty being] a fine of fourteen Polish marks, payable by each party — half to the [opposing] party and half to the court — instantly and in the present [term] — under penalty of banishment and proscription from the Kingdom of Poland and its annexed dominions, which is hereby decreed by the present court and imposed upon the party contravening the present decree in the event of non-performance of the foregoing — and any General Royal Messenger present in [the relevant] place is appointed to proclaim and announce in the customary manner the penalty of the same banishment and proscription from the Kingdom of Poland and its annexed dominions, as hereby decreed and imposed in the manner aforesaid upon the party contravening the present decree, to the party complying with the present decree — and after the proclamation of the penalty, as well as after the proclamation of the same penalty of banishment and proscription from the Kingdom of Poland and its annexed dominions, the present cause together with its whole effect and the parties themselves are hereby remitted by the present court to the Magnificent

Captain of the place or to his competent captain's municipal court (officium capitaneale castrense), under the jurisdiction of which the party contravening the present decree — with his person and goods — is subject, for further and final execution in the foregoing to be carried out and determined in proper legal order — and the return of the exported citation having been acknowledged before the records of the present court and drawn from those same authentic records is herewith delivered to the plaintiff party; and the present court and its chancellery are hereby discharged in respect of that delivery.
app53170koningr136-1:
Judicial site inspection conducted in Trąbczyn and its adjacent appurtenances, namely in Nowa Wieś, Osiny, Łazy, and the olędry, of manorial buildings and likewise village ones, on 9 July in the year of the Lord 1754.

[Translator's note: Wizja as judicial site inspection. Rule 17 translates wizja as 'judicial site inspection' throughout. In this document the term covers two distinct uses: (1) the building and estate survey forming Section 1, which is an administrative inventory conducted at the instance of the widowed proprietress rather than a court-ordered boundary inspection in the sense of the 1776 proceedings; and (2) the forest inspection forming Section 3, formally witnessed, signed, and registered at the municipal court three days later. Both are translated as 'judicial site inspection' per Rule 17; the different character of Section 1 is noted here.]

The old manor in Trąbczyn is thoroughly bad — both walls and roof with everything — which can by no means be repaired.

The new manor, of hewn log construction, finished — the roof on one side laid in part, that is, with roof tiles, the remainder lightly strewn with bundles of thatch — two small rooms finished, though not entirely; one chimney carried to the top; frames ready for all windows; and casings for such doors.

[Translator's note: 'Hewn log construction.' Z rąb, genitive plural of rąb (a hewn or notched log; squared timber). A log-frame technique using hewn timbers rather than sawn planks or earthen infill. Distinct from framed construction (w wiązaniu) and daub construction (w lepianką) used elsewhere in this survey.]

[Translator's note: 'Lightly strewn with bundles of thatch.' Snopkami posproszy, past passive participle from prószyć (to strew or scatter thinly), with po- prefix. The grammatical agreement with reszta (the remainder, feminine) is irregular in the source. The sense is a roof surface loosely covered with straw bundles — a temporary or provisional covering — as opposed to the properly laid tiles on the other side.]

[Translator's note: 'Casings for such doors.' Futra takiej drzwi. Futro (a door or window casing; the wooden surround fitted to a prepared opening). Takiej drzwi is a scribal case variant of takich drzwi (of such doors). The passage lists ramy (frames) for windows and futra (casings) for doors as the items ready for fitting — both implying the openings are prepared but not yet hung or glazed.]

The kitchen at this manor, of hewn log construction, complete in every respect, of two rooms and a pantry with sawhorses, but not boarded nor thatched.

[Translator's note: 'Sawhorses.' Z kozłami. Kozły (sawhorses, trestles, or roof trusses) in a building context; here possibly referring to roof trusses or construction supports.]

The barns are [away] from the new manor, in the farmyard.

[Translator's note: '[Away].' Poge is an unresolved reading in the source transcription. The most contextually plausible sense is 'away from' or 'at some distance from,' locating the barn complex away from the manor house proper. The manuscript requires re-examination.]

[Translator's note: Farmyard. Gumno (the threshing yard or farmyard; the enclosed service yard of a noble estate comprising the barn complex, threshing floors, and related agricultural outbuildings). Distinct from the manor house precinct.]

Barn on the left, of one threshing floor, of split planks into posts, newly built, with both gates.

The second barn in the first corner, good as new, built in framed construction by a carpenter, of small sawn planks, [fitted], with double gates and a wicket gate on one side; in the middle, covered from below with three courses of shingles.

[Translator's note: '[Fitted].' Pirzona (second barn) and pierzona (sheepfold) are the same or near-identical word appearing twice. No confident reconstruction has been established; the word likely denotes some finishing treatment, lining, or fitting of the plank cladding. Translated tentatively as '[fitted]' in both occurrences. The manuscript requires re-examination.]

[Translator's note: Shingles. Szkudła (singular szkudła), from German Schindel: thin wooden roofing tiles. Szarami is rendered as 'courses' — probably from German Schar (a row or course of roofing material), denoting horizontal layers in which shingles are laid. The term szary in this sense is not attested in standard Polish dictionaries and may be a regional or trade term.]

The third barn in the second corner of the same, of split planks into posts, built of one threshing floor — [the walls of which] are collapsing to the ground, only that they are propped.

The fourth, likewise also collapsing to the ground.

[Translator's note: 'The fourth, likewise also collapsing to the ground.' Czwarta tukasz i tyta także upadająca na ziemię. The words tukasz i tyta are unresolved in the source. The most plausible reading is tudzież i ta (likewise and that one also), producing 'the fourth, likewise that one also collapsing.' The translation follows this reading. The manuscript requires re-examination.]

The sheepfold at these barns, large, built from the top in framed daub construction, from below with small sawn planks, [fitted] in every respect, with [new] gates, good, [moss-covered], covered with courses of shingles from below; and both gables fastened with boards.

[Translator's note: Daub. Lepianka (wattle-and-daub or earthen-infill construction; from lepić, to mould or plaster). Lepianka pruska (Prussian daub; pruska roboty, of Prussian construction) denotes a half-timber or Fachwerk technique using a timber frame with clay infill, common in Greater Poland in this period. In the Owczarnia (sheepfold) passage, the upper section is framed daub (w wiązaniej lepianką) and the lower section is clad with small sawn planks.]

[Translator's note: '[Fitted].' Pirzona (second barn) and pierzona (sheepfold) are the same or near-identical word appearing twice. No confident reconstruction has been established; the word likely denotes some finishing treatment, lining, or fitting of the plank cladding. Translated tentatively as '[fitted]' in both occurrences. The manuscript requires re-examination.]

[Translator's note: '[New] gates.' W notami fortkami. Fortkami is instrumental plural of fortka (wicket gate; a small gate): the reading is clear. Notami is uncertain — possibly a misread of nowymi (new, instrumental plural), giving 'with new gates.' The preposition w may also be a misread of z (with). Translated tentatively as '[new] gates.']

[Translator's note: '[Moss-covered].' Om~a: a contracted form, the tilde indicating a suspension. The most likely expansion is omszała or omszona (moss-covered; weathered with age). Translated tentatively; the manuscript requires re-examination.]

The granary between these barns — small, of two storeys, old, in daub construction, in which the sill beams are rotted, the walls pushed out, and indeed thoroughly bad.

Outbuildings. The carriage house for carriages, of split planks into posts, built, old.

[Translator's note: 'Outbuildings.' Chlewy (pigsties; also used loosely as a generic term for farm outbuildings) appears to function here as a section heading introducing the series of service buildings that follows — the carriage house, pig sties, cowshed, stables, and pen. The specific pig sties (Świńskie chlewy) behind the carriage house are then identified separately in the next entry.]

Behind that carriage house, pig sties of planks into posts, old.

A cowshed for cattle behind those pigsties, of split planks into posts, built, of old construction.

Guest stables at the carriage house, of planks into posts, built, walls leaning toward the garden, old.

[Translator's note: 'Walls leaning toward the garden.' Pohilone ściany ku ogrodowi. Pohilone = pochylone (leaning, tilted), with h for ch and i for y, consistent with this hand. The garden-facing walls of the guest stables are structurally compromised.]

A second small stable for the lord's carriage horses, of posts and split planks, built, old.

Stables for draught-team horses, of split planks into posts, built, of old construction, thatched with bundles; and other buildings above.

[Translator's note: Draught-team horses. Konie cugowe, from cug (German Zug: a carriage team or draught team). Distinguished in the survey from konie wozowe (the lord's personal carriage horses) in the preceding entry. The two stables serve animals of different function and rank.]

[Translator's note: 'Other buildings above.' I insze budynki wyże: a summary phrase indicating further structures enumerated in the preceding text. The passage closes the outbuilding inventory.]

A pen for pigs, of split plank, not large, covered with two courses of shingles.

[Translator's note: 'Pen for pigs.' Kup dla ruczenia wieprzy. Kup (pen, sty). Ruczenia is uncertain — possibly dialectal from rucić (to cast or throw) or from ruch (movement, roaming). Translated as 'for pigs' as a working rendering; the structure houses boars (wieprze) for fattening or keeping.]

The distillery for [-----] vodka: a room of sawn planks; the vestibule in Prussian daub construction; a storeroom next to the vestibule of small sawn planks, with a door from outside; a second storeroom behind the room likewise of small sawn planks, with a door from the room and a second from outside — the entire building good, covered with shingles. In this distillery: still-pots — one larger, one smaller — with covers, good pipes, condenser fittings, mash tubs, a barrel for a distillation run, buckets, old ladles.

[Translator's note: [-----]. Palonia remains unresolved in the source. Two readings have been proposed: (1) palona (heated, fired), describing the still-room as the fired or heated space of the distillery; (2) a qualifier of wódki (vodka), possibly indicating a specific type such as Polish-style vodka. Neither has been confirmed from the manuscript. Left untranslated pending resolution.]

[Translator's note: Prussian daub. See note [^12].]

[Translator's note: Still-pots. Garce (singular garc: a vessel or pot used in the distilling apparatus, probably from German Gar or a related term). The number in the source (do [20.?]) is uncertain in the manuscript; it may read as 'two' (dwa) or as a capacity or count figure. The two pots described — one larger, one smaller — may be the garc vessels themselves.]

[Translator's note: Condenser fittings. Rurnicami: a technical term for components of the distilling condenser or pipe fittings. The exact meaning is uncertain; possibly from rurnik (one who works with pipes or condenser tubes).]

[Translator's note: Mash tubs. Kłodami do zacieru. Zacier is the mash — the mixture of grain and water fermented in the initial stage of vodka or beer production. Kłody are large wooden tubs or containers.]

[Translator's note: Distillation run. Do [??]gru: the word following do is incompletely legible in the manuscript. Przegon (a single pass of liquid through the still; a distillation run) is the most plausible candidate, giving 'a barrel for the distillation run.' Translated tentatively.]

[Translator's note: Ladles. Wybirkami: small scooping or ladling vessels, from wybierać (to scoop out; to ladle). Distinct from wybirki (selection remnants) in Section 3 — same root, different nominal form and meaning.]

The malthouse, large — not very: one room of log construction, old, sill beams dragged beneath it; the vestibule for brewing beer, of daub construction; in this vestibule a lower drying kiln, good, with a brick-built oven; behind this drying kiln there is a room of log construction, unfinished in every respect; from this room, two storerooms with one door from the room, from one to the other; from this vestibule, a door to the vault for storing beer; behind this vault, a storeroom for storage; from this vestibule, stairs upward above the room, from the gates — on which grain storage is made. On the second half of the malthouse, unfinished — no ceiling boards, doors, or windows; a clay-built chimney; in this chimney a small kettle holding three barrels of water, old, patched; vats, sufficiently good; one trivet; twenty barrels; and other vessels needed for the malthouse — the entire building recently covered with shingles, both gables fastened with boards.

[Translator's note: Malthouse. Mielcuch: a combined malthouse and brewery for producing malt and beer. A standard feature of larger Polish noble estates in this period.]

[Translator's note: Ceiling boards. Posowy: a technical term for the planks forming the ceiling or loft floor of a building, dividing an upper grain storage area from the rooms below. The unfinished half of the malthouse lacks these.]

[Translator's note: 'Sufficiently good.' Kadzie z[?] dobre. The word following z is unclear in the manuscript; dość (sufficiently) or zdatne (serviceable) are the most plausible candidates.]

[Translator's note: Trivet. Trybusek, from German Dreibuss: a three-legged stand placed over a fire for supporting cooking or distilling vessels.]

[The description of the village houses, one by one, which follows here on the rest of leaf 121 verso, on leaf 122 and at the top of leaf 122 verso, is not transcribed.]

[Section 2 — Tenant Enumeration]

Village of Nowa Wieś:

Fifteen olędry; the sixteenth plot empty. Some have built well, whereas others have only earth dugouts.

[Translator's note: 'Plot.' Huba, from German Hufe: the standard unit of land allocated to each olęder settler family. The 'sixteenth plot' (szesnasta huba) is vacant — one of the sixteen expected settler holdings is unoccupied.]

Enumeration of dependent people in Trąbczyn:

[Translator's note: Dependent people. Ludzie zaciężni: persons tied to the estate by obligation — serfs or bound tenants. The enumeration lists them by category in descending social and economic order.]

Full farmers: 4. Each of them has — working cattle: 8 of the lord's; oxen: 4; horses: 4; cows: 2; wagons: 2; pigs; ironware — all as is proper — and sowings both: winter grain and spring grain.

[Translator's note: Full farmers. Kmiecie (singular kmieć): the highest category of dependent peasant, holding a full farm unit and obligated to provide full labour services with a complete draught team.]

Half-farmers: 5. Each of them has — working cattle of the lord's: 4; a cow; a pig; an ox; ironware — all as is proper — and sowings both.

[Translator's note: Half-farmers. Półrolnicy (singular półrolnik): dependent peasants holding a half farm unit, with correspondingly reduced draught teams and labour obligations.]

Cottagers: 7. These have no lord's cattle.

[Translator's note: Cottagers. Chałupnicy (singular chałupnik): dependent peasants holding only a cottage and garden, with no arable land allocation and reduced labour obligations.]

Female lodgers: in all, 8.

[Translator's note: Lodgers. Komornicy / komornice (singular komornik / komornica): the most dependent category of rural resident, holding neither land nor a full cottage, typically lodging with another household. This use of komornik is entirely distinct from komornik graniczny (Boundary Surveyor) throughout the main project documents.]

In Osiny:

Full farmer: 1 — has all as the Trąbczyn [full farmer].

Half-farmers: 2 — have as the Trąbczyńskis.

Cottagers: 2.

Female lodgers: 3.

In Łazy:

Full farmer: 1 — has a team as the others.

Cottagers: 3.

In Nowa Wieś:

Half-farmers: 2 — one has all the cattle; the other has for work only 3.

Cottagers: 2.

Lodger: 1.

Cottages in which people live — that is, [free] peasants — but these do not perform labour obligations nor do they have the lord's cattle.

[Translator's note: Cottages. Chatew: a regional or period genitive plural form of chata (a simple peasant cottage or dwelling). The word governs w których mieszkają ludzie ('in which people live'); który in the source is a scribal case slip for których.]

[Translator's note: '[Free] peasants.' Chłopów (genitive plural of chłop): peasants who, notably, owe no labour obligations and hold no lord's cattle — indicating a distinct contractual or personal status from the bound tenants enumerated above. The word 'free' is supplied in brackets as an interpretive clarification; the source has only chłopów.]

[Translator's note: Labour obligations. Robota: obligatory serf labour owed by dependent peasants to the estate lord, typically measured as a set number of days of field work per week. The formulaic phrase nie robią ('they do not work') signals exemption from this obligation.]

[Section 3 — Forest Testimony]

The undersigned testify, together with the Court Summoner Bartłomiej, having been at the judicial site inspection of the Trąbczyn pine forests stretching from Osiny along the Drzewce boundaries — that we saw: that the pines, the better and finer ones, and most especially past the boundary post and at the approach of the thickets known as [-----], the larger half has been felled as far as Łomów. From Łomów, the finer pines have been selectively taken all the way to the Biskupice boundaries; and from the Biskupice boundaries — both before Czarny Bród and beyond the ford, above Szetlewek toward Łazy — only selection remnants stand, from which nothing can be chosen for building. And likewise past Łazy and Osiny, between the Huta, where the finest timber was — there too, felled, only selection remnants stand. Likewise the oaks standing in the woodlands — to this day only selection remnants stand — only because the olędry took [the timber] from the plots long since allocated to each of them, where the finer timber was. In witness and confirmation of this we sign with our own hands. Done in Trąbczyn on 9 July in the year of the Lord 1754.

[Translator's note: 'At the approach of the thickets.' Przy przychodu kniejów: przychód (approach, entry-point); knieje (thickets; dense sections of woodland). The preposition nimo (past, alongside — a variant of mimo) governs both słupa (the boundary post) and przychodu kniejów (the approach of the thickets), reading: 'past the boundary post and past the approach of the thickets.']

[Translator's note: [-----]. The name or descriptor of the thickets (nazywających się — 'known as [X]') appears to be absent or illegible in the manuscript at this point.]

[Translator's note: 'Selectively taken.' Poprzebierane: past passive participle of przebierać (to pick through; to select the best and leave the rest). The word describes selective logging — the finest trees removed, the lesser ones left.]

[Translator's note: Selection remnants. Wybirki: from wybierać (to select, to pick out). Trees or timber remaining after selective felling — those not considered worth taking. The word appears three times in the forest testimony. See also note [^26]: the same verbal root yields wybirkami (ladles) in Section 1, a different nominal form with a different meaning.]

[Translator's note: Huta. The glassworks on the Trąbczyn estate. A glassworks (huta szklana) consumed large quantities of timber as fuel and raw material, explaining its association with the depletion of fine forest. The Huta appears in the Latin registration record below as Chuta, with Ch- for H- as a Latin orthographic convention. It is also mentioned in the 1776 commission document as the destination of timber illegally felled from the Trąbczyn woodlands by the Chełmski predecessors.]

[Translator's note: 'Plots.' Hubami: instrumental plural of huba. The olędry had received specific land allocations including wooded portions; they had taken the finest timber from within their own allocated plots.]

Kazimierz Świerczewski, by his own hand

Józef Puchalski, by his own hand

[Section 4 — Registration Record]

In Konin, on Friday, the eve of the Feast of Saint Margaret, Virgin and Martyr, 12 July 1754.

Before the present records and acts of the Konin Starost's Municipal Court, appearing in person — the General Court Summoner of the Realm, the Honest Bartłomiej Szeptycki [Szepczyński] of Trąbczyn, known to the present office, being of sound mind — declared: having with him the Honourables Kasimierz Świerczewski and Józef Puchalski — who, although at present absent [from the court], were at the time present at the place of the matter described below — at the instance and official requisition of the Right Honourable Katarzyna Prusimska of Rozdrażew, surviving widow of the late Right Honourable Paweł Prusimski, Sub-chamberlain of His Royal Majesty, not long since deceased — hereditary lady and consort of the Trąbczyn estate with its appurtenances, and by the said late husband endowed with life-tenure and dower in all his goods — on Tuesday immediately preceding had made a formal descent in person to the same Trąbczyn estate first, then to the villages of Osiny, Łazy, Nowa Wieś, the olędry, and the Huta belonging to it, then to the pine forests and woodlands pertaining to those same goods; and being everywhere throughout those same places in succession, in accordance with the form of law and custom, had duly viewed and inspected — to be entered as follows. Which aforesaid matters he attested before the said office as having duly viewed and inspected — of which he made and makes this his report in the present act.

[Translator's note: Szeptycki [Szepczyński]. Bartłomiej is named Szeptycki in this 1754 record and Szepczyński in the 1782 document; in the 1776 document he is uczciwy Bartłomi z Trąpczyna (the Honest Bartłomiej of Trąbczyn). All three designations refer to the same individual, who served as Court Summoner of Trąbczyn across at least the period 1754–1782. The variant spellings are preserved as written in their respective documents.]

[Translator's note: Life-tenure and dower. Dominae Reformatoriae et advitalitialis (Latin). Reformatoria denotes the right of a widow to reform or reclaim her dower on the death of her husband, a standard provision of Polish noble inheritance law. Advitalis denotes a life interest or life tenancy in the goods. Katarzyna Prusimska thus held both a dower-reform right and a life tenancy in all of Paweł Prusimski's goods.]

[Translator's note: Formal descent. Condescenderat (Latin, pluperfect of condescendere): a technical legal term denoting the formal act of proceeding to an estate for an official on-site inspection. The Tuesday in question was 9 July 1754 — three days before the registration on 12 July 1754 (the eve of the Feast of Saint Margaret, Virgin and Martyr).]

[Translator's note: 'To be entered as follows.' Utpote Inseratur (Latin): a formulaic note indicating that the content of the inspection — that is, Sections 1–3 above — is to be inserted into the court record at this point. The three Polish sections (building survey, tenant enumeration, and forest testimony) are thus the material being formally registered by this relatio.]

app53170koningr114-1:
Done at Konin on the Wednesday next after the Solemn Feasts of Holy Easter in the year of the Lord 1767.

Judicial Site Inspection of the Embankment on behalf of the Right Honourable Prusimski

Coming in person to the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, the Honest Bartłomiej Szepczyński of the village of Trąbczyn, Royal Court Summoner, being of sound health, declared that he, having taken with him two noblemen, namely the Honourables Stanisław Lipiński and Józef Rudkowski, though absent here from the court,

being nonetheless present at the time at the location of the below-written matter — at the instance and official requisition of the Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski of Kolno, heir of the estates of the village of Trąbczyn with its appurtenances — on the Holy Saturday not long past had descended upon the hereditary estates of Trąbczyn, and being there in such manner according to the form of law and custom, saw and duly inspected:

an embankment recently raised at the end of the stawisko, by the raising of which the water flowing from that stawisko through the Trąbczyn estates had turned back, and had flooded the olędry settled in the Trąbczyn woodlands, together with their fields manured for cultivation and their meadows;

which aforementioned things he asserted had been done in these times by the people of the neighbouring hereditary estate of the village of Łukom, on the mandate of the heir of those estates;

concerning which the same above-written Royal Court Summoner made and makes this his present report.
app53170koningr114-2:
Done in Konin on Thursday, on the very day of the Feast of the Transfiguration of Our Lord Jesus Christ, in the year of the same 1767.

Boundary Judicial Site Inspection — on behalf of the Heir of Trąbczyn

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Bartłomiej Szepczyński of Trąbczyn, Royal Court Summoner, General, being sound, certified — because he, having with him two noblemen, namely the Honourables Józef Gołembiewski and [Józef] Rudkowski of the same name, although absent here from the court, being nonetheless present at the time at the location of the below-written matter — at the request and official requisition of the Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski of Kolno, heir of the estates of Trąbczyn with its appurtenances — on the Friday next after the Feast of Saint James the Apostle in the present year had descended to the estate of Trąbczyn, and there, being present in such manner according to the form of law and custom, saw and duly inspected:

namely, an embankment [grobla] raised in the woodland at the stawisko known near the boundary of the Łukomia estates, on Trąbczyn ground, by the raising of which embankment the water dammed in the pond causes overflows onto the grounds and meadows of the Trąbczyn Olędry, to such an extent that the meadows of the four aforementioned Olędry, being flooded, cannot be mowed;

which aforementioned things the same above-named Court Summoner, together with the aforementioned noblemen, asserted that he had duly seen and inspected; and likewise received that the said embankment, raised some years ago by the heirs of Łukomia and now repaired, by virtue of the present report.

No. 39: The Excellent Jan Tracholz, merchant and inhabitant of Witkowo, sound in mind and body, openly, withdrawing, etc., acknowledged that he himself, wholly and entirely, his own monetary sums, one of them being 1,053 imperials, 13 groszy and 6 Pfennig[?], due from the late Right Honourable Paweł Prusimski, for trees bought by the present acknowledger, the honourable Tracholz, in the pine forests and woods of Trąbczyn by means of a contract written out for the said late Right Honourable Prusimski for the purchase of those same trees [...], worked out from the honourable acknowledger Tracholz's own funds and care (although the same late Right Honourable Prusimski had once received from the same acknowledger full satisfaction according to the tenor of the aforesaid contract), the trees having been seized from the same acknowledger by force in the said pine forests and woods of Trąbczyn by this late Right Honourable Prusimski and sold by the same Right Honourable Prusimski to the honourable Simon, merchant of Szczecin; received in this amount (as the written acknowledgement of the same honourable Simon, merchant of Szczecin, commonly called an *Auscuk* [the German Auszug, an extract of account], attests);
