and also explained by various annotations, called [...]; these sums belonging to the acknowledger by right of legacy, reserving and excepting nothing from the aforesaid sums for himself and his successors thereafter, he has ceded, conferred, transposed, transferred and made over (as he cedes, confers, transposes, transfers and makes over) into the person of the Right Honourable Stanisław Chełmski, as one paying these sums to the acknowledger by his own right[?] and fully satisfying him for the foregoing, and to his successors, with full, total and entire right, dominion, ownership and competence, together with any and all rights of claiming that relate to these sums and set these sums out, together[?] with the interest arising from the same principal sums and with[?] the legal process instituted by the acknowledger against the successors of the Prusimskis; and by the present act [...] and conceding [...], this his personal acknowledgement freely assenting to the foregoing.

Jan Tracholz, by his held hand

On the transfer of his right in[?] the person of the Right Honourable Chełmski
app53150kaliszgr414-1:
Done in the woodland, or rather the pine forest called Lusnia, pertaining to the estates of Łukom from antiquity, now possessed by the olędry to be specified below, and with the house situated there — on the Monday next after the Feast of All Saints in the year of the Lord one thousand seven hundred and seventy-one — in the presence of the Honourables and noblemen Cajetan Grabski, Antoni, father, and Konstanty, son, of the Fulwarski family, and Józef Jaroszewski, steward of Trąbczyn, and likewise of the General Authentic and Sworn Royal Court Summoner of the Realm, the Honest Joannes Bikierski of the village of Węgierce, proclaiming the present act.

[Translator's note: sylva seu Borra Lusnie: the seu ("or rather") signals a scribal self-correction: the act was first described as taking place in the sylva (woodland), then corrected to the Borra (pine forest) called Lusnia. The same self-correction with seu recurs in the [403] enrollment entry. Both terms are translated in accordance with the established vocabulary: sylva → woodland; borra/bór → pine forest.]

[Translator's note: Holendos infraspecificandos: "the olędry to be specified below" — a Neo-Latin gerundive compound (infraspecificandos, to be specified below), referring forward to the list of twelve settlers delivered later in the Polish section.]

[Translator's note: The presence of Józef Jaroszewski, steward of Trąbczyn — that is, Prusimski's own estate manager — among the witnesses to this delivery of possession is legally significant. It establishes that Prusimski's own representative was present at the formal handover, making any subsequent claim of ignorance difficult to sustain. The 1776 commission considered this delivery in full and found it unlawful, overturning it and ordering the olędry returned to Prusimski.]

The below-named office, adhering to the Constitutions of the Realm and executing the condemnations or deliveries of possession of estates sanctioned [thereby], at the request and official requisition of the Right Honourable Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski, heir of the estates of Łukomia with their appurtenances and prevailing by right [of law], and for the production of decrees — or rather the penalty of outlawries with their publications —

[Translator's note: Condemnationibus seu Traditionibus Bonorum Sancitis: "condemnations or deliveries of possession of estates, sanctioned [by the Crown Constitutions]." The office acts in its capacity as executor of Crown-sanctioned legal instruments — both the condemnations (default judgements) and the deliveries of possession that flow from them.]

the first, namely, on the Monday after the Feast of Saint Bartholomew the Apostle, in the disputed ground, in the year of the Lord 1761, and submitted for enrollment in the Konin municipal court records on the Wednesday after the Feast of Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist, in the same year;

[Translator's note: The Konin Municipal Court is the court before which the entries of the Konin registers Gr. 114 and Gr. 115 were filed. The 1761 condemnation decree, filed there on Wednesday after Saint Matthew's, is one of the instruments referenced by both parties throughout the subsequent proceedings.]

then [pursuant to] the Tribunal condescension decree of the Crown Tribunal in the ordinary general sessions, on the Tuesday before the Feast of Saint Giles, Abbot, in the year of the Lord 1766 — between the same Right Honourable Chełmski on the one part and the Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, on the other part, and others appearing for that decree — issued at Bydgoszcz, by which, before all else, it was decreed as the primary matter that the estates of Łukom together with the estates of Trąbczyn be demarcated;

[Translator's note: in Comparitionem Decreti illius intrantes: "entering [i.e. appearing] for [the execution of] that decree" — the parties who had registered their court appearance in respect of the 1766 Bydgoszcz Tribunal decree. The 1776 commission assessed this decree at length: it found that Prusimski had contravened it but ultimately released him from the full penalty, as the decree was subsequently superseded.]

[Translator's note: Cathegoria: used here in the sense of "the primary matter decreed" or "it is ordered as the first category of business that." Not classical usage; in Neo-Latin legal documents cathegoria can function as a term for a matter formally decreed or classified. Rendered as "it was decreed as the primary matter."]

[Translator's note: Bonorae: scribal error for Bonorum (genitive plural of Bonum/Bona, estates).]

by the mandate of another [decree]: the Thursday after the Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, in the year of the Lord 1767, in the ordinary general sessions of the Crown Tribunal at Poznań;

[Translator's note: de Mandata alterius: "by the mandate of another [decree]" — introducing the 1767 Poznań Tribunal decree as having issued pursuant to the 1766 Bydgoszcz decree. The expected form would be de Mandato (ablative singular); Mandata appears to be either ablative plural or a scribal error. The 1776 commission identified this 1767 decree as a second default judgement obtained against Prusimski, subsequently overturned by the 1768 decree.]

and also [pursuant to] the Tribunal condescension decree in the ordinary general sessions of the Crown Tribunal, on the Monday after the Feast of the Visitation of the Most Glorious Virgin Mary, in the year of the Lord 1768 — between the Right Honourable Stanisław Chełmski, heir of the estates of Łukomia, Łomowo, and others, on the one part, and the Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski of Kolno,

[Translator's note: Decreti Tribunalibus Condescensionis: the Tribunal condescension decree. Tribunalibus is an unusual form in this position; the expected form would be Tribunalitii or Tribunalis (genitive). Translated in accordance with the evident meaning.]

Starost of Niszczewice, heir and possessor of the estates of Trąbczyn and others, on the other part, and others appearing for that same decree — issued at Bydgoszcz;

the third [condescension] finally, at the condescension session on the Monday after the Sunday Cantate in the past year 1770, and submitted for enrollment in the Kalisz municipal court records on the Monday after the Feast of the Eleven Thousand Holy Virgins in the same year —

obtained and published at the suit of the above-named Right Honourable Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski, heir of the estates of Łukomia and others, against the Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski, heir of the estates of Trąbczyn and others, on account of contravention of the above-specified decree, according to the meaning of the Tribunal decrees; the same process being broader in itself:

[Translator's note: alias eodem processu in se latiori existente: "otherwise, the same process being broader in itself" — a standard legal qualification acknowledging that the delivery of possession forms part of a wider and still-ongoing set of proceedings, without prejudice to the rest of that process.]

as, after full conviction according to the meaning of the law, the above-mentioned office proceeded to the delivery of possession, of the following tenor:

First, there is delivered to the Right Honourable His Worship Lord Chełmski the pine forest and woodland called Lusnia, and the olędry founded within it not very long ago, according to the description of the boundaries made by the heir of Trąbczyn, belonging to the said estates of Łukomia from antiquity, now called Olędry by the settlers. And that is, first, a cottage erected for the dispensing of drinks, with a new stable, without a master. Also delivered are the following olędry, namely: Michał Kinos, Henryk Bedka, Jan Tulka, Krystyan Tulka, Bogusław Celmer, Samuel Frinderberg, Bogusław Effthman, Krzysztofowa Kulawa, Maci Klinczpor, Brudzewski the shepherd, Antoni Pisarz, Wawrzyniec Welner.

[Translator's note: W[ielmożnemu?] [Jegomości?]: a compressed Polish honorific formula, abbreviated in the manuscript. The expansion is almost certainly Wielmożnemu Jegomości — "to the Right Honourable His Worship" — in the dative, governing Panu Chełmskiemu. The same formula appears written out in full in the Gr. 115 documents as Wielmożnego Jegomości Pana Chełmskiego.]

[Translator's note: podług opisu granic przez dziedzica Trąpczyna uczynionego: "according to the description of the boundaries made by the heir of Trąbczyn." The boundaries of the area being delivered to Chełmski were delimited by reference to a description of boundaries previously made by Prusimski's own side — the heir of Trąbczyn. This is consistent with what the 1776 commission noted: that Prusimski's uncle had originally established the olędry on these woodlands in the time of Chełmski's father, as attested by rights granted in 1746.]

[Translator's note: Chenryk: a Polish orthographic variant of Henryk (Henrik/Henry). The Ch- for H- initial is a documented period variant.]

[Translator's note: Samól: a phonetic spelling of Samuel.]

[Translator's note: Krzysztofowa Kulawa: the wife or widow of Krzysztof Kulawa. The Polish feminine suffix -owa indicates that the holder of this olęder farmstead is a woman — the widow or wife of a man named Krzysztof, with the surname or descriptive epithet Kulawa (lame/limping). She is the only female holder in the list.]

[Translator's note: [e?]: an uncertain letter or letters follow Welner's name in the manuscript. The 1776 commission translation confirms that the delivery comprised exactly twelve olędry, and twelve names are listed here; the uncertain mark is therefore most likely a trailing scribal stroke or false start rather than an additional name.]

Which delivery of possession having thus been completed, no one contesting it, and the inventory having been drawn up, [the office] left the same Right Honourable Chełmski in peaceful possession of the same estates, obtained by force of the legal process; and declared to the above-named olędry, as [those] possessing the lands of the Łukom estates, that obedience was to be rendered to the Right Honourable Chełmski, and enjoined it by virtue of the present delivery of possession.

[Translator's note: vi documenti Processu evictorum: "obtained by force of the legal process/document" — evictorum is the genitive plural of evictus (past participle of evinco, to obtain by legal process), agreeing with fundorum (estates). The estates are described as having been wrested from the opposing party by the force of the legal proceedings recited above.]

Wawrzyniec Wstowski, General Sworn Commissioner of the Voivodeships of Poznań and Kalisz, by his own hand

[Section 2 — Enrollment at the Kalisz Municipal Court]

In the Kalisz Municipal Court, on the Saturday immediately before the Feast of Saint Martin, Bishop, in the year of the Lord 1771.

To the office and present records of the Kalisz Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honourable Antoni Serlatkowski presented to the present office for enrollment and for entering in these records the Delivery of Possession conducted in the woodland, or rather the pine forest, Lusnia, pertaining to the estates of Łukom from antiquity, having ensued [from the above decrees], of the following tenor: Let it be inserted. But the original of the same Delivery of Possession, left with the present records, was sewn into the Protocol.

[Translator's note: Subsecutam: "having ensued" — past participle of subsequor, describing the delivery of possession as having followed upon and resulted from the decrees recited above. Agreeing with Traditionem (feminine accusative).]

[Translator's note: Inseratur: "let it be inserted" — a formal imperative directing the clerk to insert the full text of the delivery of possession (the text of f. 402) into the court protocol at this point. The text of Section 1 is what was inserted pursuant to this instruction.]

[Translator's note: in Protocollon Insutum est: "was sewn into the Protocol" — from insuo (to sew in, to insert by stitching). The original physical document of the delivery of possession was attached to the court register by sewing, a standard archival practice for original instruments presented for enrollment.]
app53170koningr115-4:
Done in Konin on the Monday next after the Feast of Saint Andrew the Apostle in the year of the Lord 1771.

On behalf of the Right Honourable Chełmski — Oblata of the Delivery of Possession of the Lusnia Pine Forest with the Olędry

Let it be seen here: the Oblata of the delivery of possession of the Lusnia pine forest with the olędry, issued on behalf of the Right Honourable Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski, heir of the estates of Łukomia, [placed] among the produced documents.
app53170koningr115-5:
Done in Konin on the Friday before the Feast of Saint Thomas the Apostle in the year of the Lord 1771.

On behalf of the Right Honourable Chełmski — Presentation of Weapons

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Nicolaus Krzepczyński of the village of Myszaków, Royal Court Summoner, General, by special commission of the Right Honourable Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski, heir of the estates of Łukom with their appurtenances, presented to the present office the below-listed weapons, namely: four swords in sheaths with leather belts; also one unsheathed [blade] fitted with iron; also four spears with iron tips fastened onto staffs; also three longer firearms and one firearm fitted with brass, loaded with lead and fine powder.

Which aforementioned things — besides other weapons taken away by the below-named party — in the pine forest called Lusnia, built upon by the olędry, belonging to the estates of Łukom now and from antiquity, during the violent incursion of the Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski of Kolno, Starost of Niszczewice, heir of the contiguous estates of Trąbczyn, and the besieging of the innkeeper's house by armed and lawless men, on the immediately preceding Monday — the same weapons having been seized by the Right Honourable Chełmski — the same above-named Court Summoner asserted to be so. Which, having been presented in this manner, he received back to himself, and was discharged from his office in respect of the received [weapons] in the presence of those present.
app53170koningr115-6:
On behalf of the same — Judicial Site Inspection of the Demolition of the Embankment at Łukom

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Nicolaus Krzepczyński of Myszaków, Royal Court Summoner, General, being sound, certified — because he, having with him two noblemen, namely the Honourables Antoni Wolski and Konstanty Folwarski, although absent here from the court for the present, being nonetheless present at the time at the location of the below-written matter — at the request and official requisition of the Right Honourable Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski, heir of the estates of Łukom with their appurtenances — on the immediately preceding Monday [went] to the estate of Łukomia and the Lusnia pine forest, and being there in such manner, they saw and duly inspected:

Having arrived at the fishpond [stawisko] lying in the Łukomia pine forest, they saw an embankment dug up, and in it, fourteen [elements] cut with axes — enclosure elements, posts, sluice gates, and channels — demolished completely, and the water let out with the fish. Also there: twenty thick clubs newly cut, prepared for combat, and then left behind. Also: in the pine forest called Lusnia, among the olędry, in the innkeeper's cottage, in the walls all around — eight holes cut in the structural timber for aimed shooting; three windows cut down to a single pane and shot through.

Which aforementioned things the same above-named Royal Court Summoner — namely, concerning the demolition of the embankment, [carried out] by more than thirty of the Trąbczyn subjects assembled, to be identified by name afterward, in the presence of the Right Honourable Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice; and concerning the shooting through of the house, [carried out] by licentious subordinate men, by the mandate and command of the Right Honourable Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice — asserted to have been done and inflicted on the same day. Concerning which, the present report.
app53170koningr115-7:
Done in Konin on the Tuesday next after the Feast of Saint Andrew the Apostle in the year of the Lord 1772.

On behalf of the Right Honourable Chełmski — Judicial Site Inspection of the Violated Tavern in Lusnia

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Joannes Bikierski of Węgierce, Royal Court Summoner, General, being sound, certified — because he, having with him two noblemen, namely the Honourables Antoni Fulwarski and Jakub Kraśniewski, although absent here from the court for the present, being nonetheless present at the time at the location of the below-written matter — on the immediately preceding Saturday, at the request and official requisition of the Right Honourable Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski, heir and possessor of the estates of Łukom, Łumowo, Myszakowo, and the olędry planted in the Lusnia pine forest, had officially and personally descended to the estate of the said olędry and the Lusnia tavern, and being there in such manner, saw and duly inspected:

In that same tavern, accustomed to dispensing liquors — three windows [and] four doors with iron hinges removed from that same building.

Which aforementioned things, on the immediately preceding Saturday, by the Honourable Lipiński, steward of Trąbczyn; Radzewski, revenue clerk; Władarz, keeper of the pine forests; and the one called Wąchnicki, manorial servant — deep in the night, by the mandate of the Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski of Kolno, Starost of Niszczewice, heir of the estates of Trąbczyn — seized and removed in a violent manner, together with a table and a barrel of beer, and carried off to the Trąbczyn estate with a band of Trąbczyn subjects, fitted out for attempting disturbances — he asserted to be so. Concerning which, the present report.
app53170koningr115-8:
Done in Konin on the Friday after Ash Wednesday next, namely on the twenty-sixth day of the month of February in the year of the Lord 1773.

Judicial Site Inspection of Felled Trees — on behalf of the Right Honourable Prusimski

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Bartłomiej Szepczyński of Trąbczyn, Royal Court Summoner, General, being sound, certified — because he, having with him two noblemen, namely the Honourables Piotr Makowski and Świętosław Bogusławski, although absent here from the court for the present, being nonetheless present at the time at the location of the below-written matter — on the day preceding today's act —

at the request and official requisition of the Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski of Kolno, Starost of Niszczewice, heir of the estates of Trąbczyn — to the Trąbczyn pine forests and the meadows pertaining to the same estates — descended personally and officially; and being there in such manner, saw and duly inspected and counted: namely, in the pine forest lying beyond the woodland called Lusnia, fifty-one trunks from pine trees of value for building, cut down; also, in the meadows pertaining to the estate of Trąbczyn, called Kąty, thirty-two alder trunks left [there], from a tree cut down.

Which aforementioned things — immediately at that time, by the subjects of the Right Honourable Chełmski, heir of the estates of Łukom, carried away from the pine forest beyond Lusnia; and then [by] men of the Podbiele estate of the Right Honourable Zakrzewska, cut down and intercepted from the meadows — asserting that he had duly seen, inspected, and counted [the same], he attested to the present office.
app53170koningr115-9:
The Right Honourable Chełmski against the Right Honourable Prusimski — Protest

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Right Honourable Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski, heir of the estates of Łukom with their appurtenances, possessor by force of his rights of the olędry called Lusnia, lodged this protest to the present records against the Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski of Kolno, Starost of Niszczewice, heir of the estates of the Trąbczyn tract, and likewise against his household servants and subjects — for this reason: that the same Right Honourable Prusimski, proceeding in subversion of the laws, although he well knows that possession of the Lusnia olędry has been acknowledged by law to him, the protester, nonetheless — whether by his special mandate or by his connivance — permitted the Honourables Lipiński, [his] steward, and Marzęcki, his chamber attendant, together with those recruited to them — Kazimierz, farm servant of the miller of Drzęzgi, Filip Wąchnicki, and others — to ride upon and attack the tavern and the olędry; which same violent attackers, having set aside the safety cautiously secured for the settlers dwelling there, did not scruple to carry out and perpetrate various transgressions and acts of violence — in respect of which unlawful conduct the same Right Honourable Chełmski hereby protests.

Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski, by his own hand
app53170koningr115-10:
On behalf of the Right Honourable Chełmski — Judicial Site Inspection of the Lusnia Olędry

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Joannes Bikierski of Węgierki, Royal Court Summoner, General, being sound, certified — because he, having with him two noblemen, namely the Honourables Michał Borkowski and Jakub Kraśniewski, although absent here from the court for the present, being nonetheless present at the time at the location of the below-written matter — on the immediately preceding Wednesday, [went] to the estate of the Lusnia olędry at the request and official requisition of the Right Honourable Stanisław Chełmski, having personally descended; and being there in such manner, saw and duly inspected:

At the tavern among the Lusnia [olędry]: the stove, three windows, four doors — newly repaired and fitted out by the Right Honourable His Worship Lord Chełmski — now chopped and cut out; the chimney demolished and the chimney stacks undercut; drinking vessels for beer and spirits smashed and chopped.

Which aforementioned things, by the Honourables Lipiński, Marzęcki, and others, late at night, on 29 January of the current year, violently attacking those same olędry, he asserted to have been done and inflicted. Concerning which he made the present report, and attested to the present office that he had duly seen and inspected all of these things.

app53150kaliszgr425-1:
Commissioners from the Estates of the Republic for the adjudication of the Case between the Honourable Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, Heir of the estates of Trąbczyn with their appurtenances, on the one part, and the Honourable Stanisław Ścibór Chełmski, Heir of the estates of Łukomia likewise with their appurtenances, on the other part, designated and expressed below in the signatures:

Since, both on account of the currently sitting Ordinary General Sejm in Warsaw and likewise on account of the sitting Crown Tribunal in Piotrków, some of us having obligations in Warsaw and others finding themselves at the said Tribunal with obligations, we cannot bring to a conclusion by final judicial resolution the Action between the aforementioned Parties, commenced at the present term falling from the adjournment made, for the reasons expressed therein, by the Decree issued between those same Parties on the Thirteenth Day of the Month of September of the preceding year — for such reason therefore, the term of the session adjourned to the present day by the above-mentioned Decree [we adjourn] to the First

Monday after the Feast of the Holy Three Kings in the coming year One Thousand Seven Hundred and Seventy-Seven, and we place, adjourn, and postpone it; and we preserve for the parties the peremptory term of appearing before the Commissarial Court, which was to hold its session at that time on the ground of the Łukom estates. By force of the present act. Done at our Residences, on the Twenty-Eighth Day of the Month of September in the Year of the Lord 1776.

Stefan Leszczyc Zielonacki, Deputy Judge of the Kalisz Land Court, Commissioner, by his own hand

Maciej Leszczyc Mierzewski, Commissioner, by his own hand

Tomasz Radoński, Boundary Surveyor of Kalisz, Commissioner, by his own hand

Stanisław Jabłkowski, Commissioner, by his own hand

Stanisław Otto-Trąmpczyński, Commissioner, by his own hand

app53150kaliszgr424-1:

Coming in person before the present Kalisz Starost's Municipal Court and Records, the Right Honourable Antonius Leszczyc Mierzewski [on behalf of Chełmski] asked of the present Office whether the Commissorial Boundary Decree between the estates of the villages of Łukom, Trąbczyn, and others, issued by the Illustrious Right Honourable Commissioners from the Estates of the Republic on behalf of the Right Honourable Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, heir of the estates of Trąbczyn with its appurtenances, designated on behalf of the same Right Honourable Prusimski, and issued between those same estates, had been submitted to the present Records by oblata or not. The present Office, consenting to this Requisition, betook itself to the revision of the Protocols of the Relation, where oblatas are customarily received. These having been revised and carefully examined from the act of Thursday next after the feast of Saint Hedwig the Widow, Elect, namely the seventeenth day of the month of October of the present year, to the act of this present day, the Office responded that no Commissorial Boundary Decree — between the above-written estates, issued by the Illustrious Right Honourable Commissioners designated on behalf of the Right Honourable Prusimski and brought onto the ground of those estates, and submitted by oblata — was found to have been in the present Records; of which the present Office has made, and makes, attestation by these presents.

app536046-1:
No. 16: Between the Right Honourable Stanisław Chełmski, heir of the estates of Łukomia with their appurtenances, Plaintiff, through Melchior Krzyzanowski, and the Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, cited, in person — the Court, deciding the term of the Plaintiff party brought before it, the controversies having been heard:

Although the Right Honourable Chełmski [uncertain: by this term] claims from the Right Honourable Prusimski the production of a certain act, as though a Boundary act, issued between the estates of Łukom and Trąbczyn by Commissioners designated by the Estates of the Realm and brought in by the Right Honourable Starost; and, laying before the court three searches for that same Boundary act — the first made before the records of the Kalisz Municipal Court on the Saturday after the Feast of the Presentation of the Most Glorious Virgin Mary in the year 1776, through the Right Honourable Antoni Mierzejewski in the name of the Right Honourable Chełmski; the second before the records of the Kościan Municipal Court on the 2nd day of the month of January, through the Honourable Antoni Smoliński likewise in the name of the Right Honourable Chełmski; the third before the records of the Konin Municipal Court on the 28th day of the month of October in the present year, by the Right Honourable Chełmski alone — proves that the said field act, whose production is claimed, was not in the records of its proper palatinate;

the Right Honourable Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, for his part, freeing himself from the production claimed, [lays down] a search, made through the Honourable Ludwik [uncertain: Łański] in the name of the party concerned, for the Commissorial Boundary Decree issued between the hereditary estates of the villages of Trąbczyn Minus, or Nowa Wieś, and Łukom

[uncertain: under no. 15, on the other page]

and Drzewce — a search made before the records of the Municipal Court of Brest in Kuyavia on the 10th day of the present month of October in the present year, and entered as an oblata in the records of the Konin Municipal Court on the 16th day of the same month in the present year likewise, [uncertain: its date wrongly given out] — and shows that this Commissorial Decree was entered as an oblata under the act of Tuesday after the Feast of Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist, in the past year 1776, before the records of the Municipal Court of Brest in Kuyavia.

Since, however, rights, all settlements, and decrees ought to be submitted by oblata in their own palatinate — the Court therefore decrees that the Right Honourable Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, shall submit the Decree specified above by way of oblata to the records of the Konin Municipal Court within the space of four weeks from the present act, under penalty of outlawry in case of contravention, to be published before those same records.
app536046-2:
No. 17: Between the same Plaintiff, through the same, and the same Cited, in person — the Court, etc., deciding the term of the Plaintiff party brought before it, the controversies having been heard:

Although the Right Honourable Stanisław Chełmski — by virtue of a transfer, acknowledged before the records of the Pyzdry Municipal Court on Wednesday, the Eve of the Feast of the Nativity of the Most Blessed Virgin Mary, in the year 1768 by the Excellent Jan Tracholz, merchant and inhabitant of Witkowo, of various sums claimed from the late Right Honourable Paweł Prusimski, into the person of the same Right Honourable Chełmski — instituting a suit against the Right Honourable Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, claims the production of the contract concerning the sale of the Trąbczyn pine forest entered into with the Honest Tracholz and the late Right Honourable Paweł Prusimski;

since, however, it is shown to the Court that in its earlier sessions, on Monday after Septuagesima Sunday in the year 1766, a decree of remission of the cause to a condescension term had intervened between the Honest Jan Tracholz and the Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski, the present Cited, and has not been carried out: the Court therefore, the whole matter being suspended, finds a condescension of its court to the ground of the estates of Trąbczyn to be necessary, the parties requesting it, on and for the Monday after Laetare Sunday in Lent next coming in the coming year — decreeing that the parties shall bring this same court, the absence of two or of one notwithstanding; which court, or he who is to be brought, shall order the production of the contract specified above by the Right Honourable Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, and shall finally decide and adjudge the present cause as law, justice, the tenor of the documents and the contents of the Plaintiff party's terms require, all doubts and interventions being resolved; shall decree satisfaction, to whom, how much and from whom it shall be due; shall conduct inquisitions as the matter requires; shall receive oaths where necessary and from whom it shall be due; and shall attach rigours.

The parties shall be bound and obliged to obey and to acquiesce in that court of the condescension, under penalty of outlawry, to be published before the same judge who is to be brought, upon the contravening party in case of contravention. The penalty of fourteen Polish marks is to be set off party against party, and paid to the Court forthwith, under the usual rigour, by halves. For which condescension term the parties shall cite those whom the matter requires; those cited shall appear under the rigour written above.

Upon the Manifest of Antoni Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice

Certified copy.

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honourable Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, hereditary owner of the estates of Trąbczyn — looking to the integrity of his cause and fortune and to remove danger from them — solemnly, before the same office and its records, in and against the Honourable Stanisław Chełmski, hereditary owner of the estates of Łukom, and simultaneously against the prejudicial judges of the Kalisz Land Court in the cause described below, manifests:

of the fact that the same Honourable Chełmski — of his own accord seeking lawsuits with the manifestant — dared and presumed to pursue against his property and person the illegal right acquired from the Honest Jan Tracholz, in the matter of oak timber or woodland contracted with the late Honourable Paweł Prusimski, the manifestant's uncle, already in the year 1744, confirmed and assumed by him for himself — to whom the manifestant's late uncle had not been debtor, but who had himself been debtor to the uncle — and having thus acquired that same right, without attending to the fact that the manifestant is without resources and without the documents — adhering in the hands of the successors of the late widow of his uncle, vindicated through a process by the manifestant but not yet recovered — necessary both for this cause and for the general estate of his uncle; and without attending to the fact that by reason of those same documents, first the Kalisz Land Court decree of the enjoined condescension and then that of the Piotrków Tribunal had intervened with those same successors; and hence also the cause with the same Honest Tracholz, the assignor of his right, had been remitted by decree of the Kalisz Land Court to the term of those same condescensions, designated with the successors of the widow of his uncle; and furthermore that regarding those same documents, together with the successors of the widow of his uncle, the Commission of the Estates of the Realm had been issued — not yet decided, and due to be decided by the Crown Tribunal;

yet with all these things in no way considered or attended to — and notably the Land Court decree of remission to the condescension term — contrary to which no other decree could validly follow in that same entangled court — he dared to improperly summon the manifestant to that same Kalisz Land Court without even having had a term against the remission decree; and in that same court to have issued another decree, different and contrary to the prior, of the enjoined condescension to the estates of Trąbczyn — without a term, as stated above — contrary to the remission decree, the same remission decree not reviewed, nay rather remaining untouched to this day — into a mere entanglement of the manifestant's cause and the boundary cause

pending in the Crown Tribunal — to be issued — and thereby to burden the manifestant, and to seek to draw him and his boundary cause and the discrepant decree into some entanglement;

and against the Honourable Kalisz Land Court judges: because they — not attending to the reasons and documents set out above, nor to their own decree of remission of this cause, with the Honourable Chełmski's assignor, to the condescension term together with the successors of the widow of the manifestant's uncle, contrary to which another judgment could not be issued — and that same remission decree likewise not reviewed, and unable to be reviewed without a term by the Honourable Chełmski — and without attending to the decrees of the Piotrków Tribunal and the Commission of the Estates of the Realm issued together with the successors of the widow of his uncle, by virtue of which the present cause did not fall to their forum and decision — and finally without attending to the fact that in this cause — since it is so long-standing and begun more than thirty years ago — the more extensive communication of documents ought entirely, according to the prescription of the new statute of the law and the determined degree of the right, to have been granted and decided — yet with all these things unattended to, dared and presumed to issue another decree of the enjoined condescension to the estates of Trąbczyn, entirely different from their prior decree and likewise outside the proper forum — and thereby to burden the manifestant, and to prepare danger for the boundary cause, and to refuse to admit any motion from that decree —

wherefore the manifestant, having set out these matters — not only by reason of all the foregoing but also regarding the nullity and want of substance of that same Kalisz Land Court decree issued at Konin on the Monday after the Feast of Saint Hedwig, Widow and Chosen of God, namely 20 October of the preceding year, between the same Honourable Chełmski and the manifestant, prejudicially — staying the execution of it and referring himself to the laws of the Realm, and simultaneously also against the transfer or the illegal right acquired by the Honourable Chełmski from the Honest Tracholz — again and again, most solemnly, manifests;

with all things preserved that ought to be preserved by law.
app53170koningr117-1:
Done at Konin on the Saturday next after Ash Wednesday, namely 7 March 1778.

On behalf of the Honourable Chełmski against the Honourable Prusimski — Relatio for the Condescension Term

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Jan Jankowski of the village of Łukom, Royal Court Summoner, General, sound of health, acknowledged the authenticated citation letter for the condescension term arising in the estates of the village of Trąbczyn, issued of the following tenor:

Stanislaus Augustus, by the Grace of God King of Poland, etc. — to you, the Honourable Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, hereditary owner of the estates of Trąbczyn with appurtenances — regarding your estates we command that you appear in person, lawfully and peremptorily at the condescension term — ordered in the Kalisz Land Court decree issued at Konin on the Monday after the Feast of Saint Hedwig, Widow and Chosen of God, in the immediately preceding year — and designated for the Monday after the First Sunday of Lent at the estates of Trąbczyn — at the instance of the Honourable Stanisław Scibor Chełmski, hereditary owner of the estates of Łukom with appurtenances, plaintiff; who cites you, or rather summons you to this prepared decree — as the demands of the matter previously committed to the citation require; and to the effect that you — at that same condescension term fixed and arising in the estates of Trąbczyn — produce the laboring subjects of your estates, who by the present citation are placed under arrest in your keeping, namely: Albert Livoy, Andrzej Rataj, Kazimierz the Keeper, and Albert the Shepherd of Nowawieś; for which aforesaid citations, the days set at the term — having attended to it, prepared to appear and respond judicially — under penalty through the aforesaid matters. Given at Konin, on the Monday next after the Feast of Saint Matthias the Apostle in the Year of the Lord 1778.

Served at the estate office of the village of Trąbczyn, on the table of the heated room, with a maiden present — on today's day, as contained in the act, he placed and left it.
app53170koningr117-2:
Done at Konin on the Monday next after Laetare Sunday, namely 30 March 1778.

On behalf of the Honourable Prusimski against the Honourables Chełmski and the Kalisz Land Court — to the Tribunal — Relatio

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Bartłomiej Szepczyński of the village of Trąbczyn and Mateusz Matuszkiewicz of the village of Szetlewek, Royal Court Summoners, General, sound of health, acknowledged the two authenticated citation letters issued for the ordinary general sessions of the Crown Tribunal of the Realm at Piotrków as described below, of the following tenor:

Stanislaus Augustus, by the Grace of God King of Poland, Grand Duke of Lithuania, of Russia, of Prussia, of Masovia, of Samogitia, of Kiev, etc., of Podolia, of Podlachia, of Livonia, of Smolensk, of Seversk, of Chernigov — to you, the Honourables: Stanisław Chełmski, hereditary owner of the estates of Łukomia; and Franciszek Wierusz Walknowski, Judge; Stefan Zielonacki, Deputy Judge; and Xawery Mikorski, Notary of the Kalisz Land Court — the judges complained of in the cause described below: regarding your persons, goods and office we command that in our Ordinary Courts of the Crown Tribunal of the Realm at Piotrków, from the date and service of the present citation, correctly within four weeks, or for as long as and whenever the present cause shall fall to be called and proclaimed for adjudication from the register and inscription belonging to it, you appear in person and peremptorily, at the instance of the Honourable Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, hereditary owner of the estates of Trąbczyn, plaintiff;

who, adhering to his manifest made or to be made — and to the laws of the Realm and to the decrees both of the prior decree of your court of remission to the condescension term together with the succession of the widow of the plaintiff's late uncle, and to the Tribunal and to the Commission issued by the Estates of the Realm — cites you; or rather, staying the execution of your subsequent decree — issued at Konin on the Monday after the Feast of Saint Hedwig, Widow and Chosen of God, namely 20 October of the preceding year, between the Honourable Chełmski and himself the plaintiff — cites you to see and hear that the above-mentioned Konin Land Court decree, contrary to the prior decree — the prior decree neither reviewed nor resolved, and likewise unable to be resolved without a term which the Honourable Chełmski has not obtained — and with the Tribunal decree and the Commission issued by the Estates of the Realm, which obstruct and do not admit the Kalisz Land Court forum and your decision, not being attended to — having been issued prejudicially and also without the communication of documents due to be decreed according to the new statute of the law in so long-standing a cause begun thirty years ago — be reviewed; himself the plaintiff to be freed from its bond and rigour; nay rather, the cause for the resolution of that same decree to be remitted to the Tribunal;

and nonetheless — the transfer, or right, unlawfully acquired by the Honourable Chełmski from the Honest Jan Tracholz, unduly and for mere vexation and to entangle the boundary cause and the discrepant commissarial decree-act, being cassated — in the competent forum, decided by the same action — himself the plaintiff to be freed from this legal claim; and by reason of the issued prejudicial decree — penalties against the party and likewise against the external court; and in the remainder all things that are of law, justice, and the documents — to be decided, decreed, and sentenced against you. Be prepared to attend to this citation and respond judicially. Given at Piotrków on the Saturday after Reminiscere Sunday in the Year of the Lord 1778.

The first — the Honest Szepczyński — in the town of Konin, at the house of the Honest Palszewicz, [...] with the mother of the household present; the second — the Honest Matuszkiewicz — against the Honourable Chełmski at the manor court of the estates of the village of Łukom, with [...] present — both copies on the tables of the heated rooms, distinctly, on today's day, as contained in the act, placed and left.
app53170koningr117-5:
The Honourable Chełmski against the Honourable Sokołowski — Manifest Filed

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honourable Stanisław Scibor Chełmski, Thesaurarius [Treasurer] of Wschowa — reassuming his prior manifests — attests that the commissarial boundary field decree between his estates of Łukom, [and] Trąbczyn of the Honourable Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, and others — [issued] by the commissioners engaged on behalf of the petitioning party, according to the tenor of the judicial site inspection of the year 1592 [conducted] by a court official and nobles as the custom of that time required, and according to the tenor of the Konin Land Court decree — an inspection acknowledged by the then co-heirs of the estates of Trąbczyn, or rather unchallenged to this day, authorised by the two Tribunal decrees of the years 1766 and 1768 and ordered to be observed in the delimitation — had intervened; and the mounds erected by the commissioners relying on the instrument or statute of the Estates of the Realm, had been made firm by the oath sworn by the appearing party at the last axial mound;

yet the Honourable Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, and the commissioners procured on his behalf — although they knew of the aforesaid concluded delimitation, had seen the mounds raised on behalf of the appearing party, and had full notice of the oath sworn by the appearing party, in the form of the Statute, in confirmation of the same — notwithstanding all these things, and first the commissioners on behalf of the Honourable Prusimski, abusing their authority, entrusted to the Honourable Albert Czarnecki, Boundary Surveyor of Kalisz — engaged by the Honourable Prusimski for the commencement of the commission, in the matter of the review of documents, the formation of boundary lines, and the lending of his advocacy — the lustration of the boundary line and the placing of the mounds; and admitted and designated him both for the reception of the oath from the party regarding the reality of the boundary lines and for other matters to be transacted. Which Honourable Boundary Surveyor, at his own pleasure, already after the departure of the Honourable Commissioners and an interval of several weeks, had caused the decree to be drawn up; and had allowed himself the ability to treat documents according to opportunity — in one place as legitimate, in another as invalid.

And the same Honourable Prusimski — having had full notice, as mentioned above, of the oath sworn by the appearing party — and being little acquainted even with his own boundaries, which were seldom gone over in his presence — knowingly presumed to offer oath against oath; and had recruited as witnesses to swear the like oath with him: one from among the collateral cognates, having been cited; another lacking full sense; a third who is in the service of the Honourable Czarnecki, taken to his side straight from Piotrków and never having been in these parts; and had recruited other persons of no account.

For which reason, publicly setting out the foregoing, he incriminates the Honourable Prusimski for all of them, and offers that, if need be, he will prove and deduce the aforesaid matters through sworn inquiries.

Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski
app53170koningr117-6:
Judicial site inspection of the felled pine tree from the boundary mound — in the matter of the Honourable Prusimski

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Bartłomiej Szepczyński of the village of Trąbczyn, Royal Court Summoner, General, sound of health, acknowledged that he himself — having with him two nobles, namely the Honourables Piotr Gostarski and Tomasz Jachimowicz, although absent here [from court] but present at the location of the matter described below — at the formal request of the Honourable Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, hereditary owner of the estates of Trąbczyn and others, on the Saturday next after Septuagesima Sunday, namely 21 February of the current year, descended with the above-mentioned nobles to the boundary location of the estates of Trąbczyn; and being there in such manner, declared in these words:

That, being on the boundary of the estates of Trąbczyn, he saw a pine tree — grown over several decades on the boundary mound called [uncertain: T]urnata, dividing Trąbczyn from Biskupice — marked with three crosses or boundary marks — cut down and taken away in the night-time by His Worship Lord Bogusławski, hereditary owner of the part-estates of Kurów —

he duly saw and observed; of which the present relatio of the same Court Summoner has been made.
app53170koningr117-7:
Done at Konin on the Wednesday next after Palm Sunday, namely 15 April 1778.

The Honourable Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, against the Honourable Chełmski and the Land Court — Manifest Filed

Certified copy.

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honourable Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, hereditary owner of the estates of Trąbczyn with appurtenances — looking to avert any danger to his cause and fortune and to safeguard the integrity of the laws of the nobility, and referring himself to the manifest and prosecution term against the Kalisz Land Court decree issued at Konin prejudicially, made and lodged before the records of the Konin Municipal Court in the preceding year by permission of the law — solemnly, before the same office and its records, in and against the Honourables Stanisław Chełmski, current hereditary owner of the estates of Łukom with appurtenances, and Stefan Zielonacki, Deputy Land Judge of Kalisz, judge of the cause described below both in the full Kalisz Land Court and at the condescension term on the ground of the estates of Trąbczyn — manifests:

of the fact that the manifestant — observing, for the reasons set out in the manifest and prosecution term, that the Kalisz Land Court decree issued at Konin on the Monday after the Feast of Saint Hedwig, Widow and Chosen of God, namely 20 October of the preceding year, between the same Honourable Chełmski and himself the manifestant — is contrary not only to the prior decrees but also to the Commission of the Estates of the Realm issued in this cause, and likewise issued outside the proper forum — as much because without decision of the cause with the successors of the widow of the late Honourable Paweł Prusimski, his uncle, regarding the production and delivery of documents pertaining both to this cause and to his uncle's general estate — a cause pending and entrusted and ordered to be decided by land court decrees and ultimately by the Commission of the Estates of the Realm, and to this point undetermined, nay rather pending before the Tribunal

and due to be resolved there — and that without the documents received he cannot be adjudicated in the present cause with the Honourable Chełmski, the acquirer of the pretension or the most illegal claim acquired from the Honest Jan Tracholz, the assignor — (with whom also the cause and his pretension had been remitted together with this cause and the condescension, by reason of the connected nature of the matter, as recently as in the year 1766; the same Honest Tracholz having summoned and cited the successors of Katarzyna of Rozdrażewo Prusimska, the widowed survivor of the manifestant uncle, after her death, on that same pretension of his, at his own term) — he cannot be separately adjudicated; and [attentive to the fact] that he had already conceived that the evident danger to this cause, and also some entanglement of the manifestant's boundary cause and discrepant decree, had been premeditated by the Honourable Chełmski.

Accordingly, the manifestant — from these motives — was compelled by force of law to make and file the prosecutions, namely the manifest and prosecution term, against the above-written Kalisz Land Court decree and simultaneously against the court; and accordingly, standing on those same legal remedies — namely the manifest and prosecution term — staying the execution of that same Kalisz Land Court decree given at Konin and the carrying out of the act of that condescension, he laid the same prosecutions before the Honourable Sub-judge at the condescension term; and since the entire Kalisz Land Court had been incriminated — not only through the prosecution term but also through the timely manifest on grievance and for the review of their decree — and summoned to the Tribunal.

The manifestant, therefore, unable to pursue the matter in that same Kalisz Land Court as having already been prosecuted there, and its own decree being incapable of being reviewed by it — had sought and concluded that the remission of this cause to the Tribunal should be made by the Honourable Sub-judge of the Kalisz Land Court. For the same Honourable Land Judge of Kalisz, instead of making the remission to the Tribunal by virtue of the aforesaid reasons, then — although the aforesaid prosecutions, issued to the Tribunal and not to the Kalisz Land Court, stood in the way — improperly made that remission back to himself and the whole court, who were under prosecution and by force of law already bound to desist from adjudicating that cause, at the motion of the party, namely the Honourable Chełmski; and thereby added empty litigation costs to the manifestant and derogated from his legal rights; and also of the fact that the same act of the condescension could not be completed — for reasons to be given at the prosecution term and to be elucidated through a separate manifest if necessary —

in full force of his every explanation, and also as a certain process of the manifestant's honour and aggrievance, and simultaneously regarding the nullity and want of substance of the aforesaid remission made to the Kalisz Land Court as prosecuted, and the impossibility of being adjudicated together with the Honourable Chełmski in that same prosecuted court — and also of the remission sought there from the same court to the Tribunal — again and again, most solemnly, manifests;

offering to act lawfully in respect of all the foregoing, with all things preserved that ought to be preserved by law, and with full force reserved and safeguarded to himself of augmenting or diminishing the same manifest, or of making another manifest in supplement of this one.

Antoni Na Kolnie Prusimski
app53170koningr117-8:
On behalf of the Honourable Prusimski against the Land Court and the Condescension Court Office — to the Tribunal — Relatio

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Bartłomiej Szepczyński of the village of Trąbczyn, Royal Court Summoner, General, sound of health, acknowledged the authenticated citation letters, one and the same in substance, issued for the ordinary general sessions of the Crown Tribunal of the Realm at Piotrków as described below, of the following tenor:

Stanislaus Augustus, by the Grace of God King of Poland, Grand Duke of Lithuania, of Russia, of Prussia, of Masovia, of Samogitia, of Kiev, of Podolia, of Podlachia, of Livonia, of Smolensk, of Seversk, of Chernigov — to you, the Honourables: Stanisław Chełmski, hereditary owner of the estates of Łukomia; and Franciszek Wierusz Walknowski, Judge; Stefan Zielonacki, Deputy Judge and also judge at the condescension term of the cause described below; and Xawery Mikorski, Notary of the Kalisz Land Court — judges in the cause described below — regarding your persons, goods, sums and offices, we command that you appear in person and peremptorily before us or our Crown Tribunal of the Realm at Piotrków, whenever the present cause shall fall to be called and proclaimed for adjudication from the register and inscription belonging to it — at the instance of the Honourable Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, hereditary owner of the estates of Trąbczyn with appurtenances, plaintiff;

who, adhering to the prosecutions — namely the manifest and prosecution term — previously lodged; and to this subaltern manifest made or to be made; and to the laws of the Realm; and to the prior decrees and the Commission designated by the Republic in this cause that have followed; and to the reasons and those same decrees set out in the prosecutions — cites you; or rather, reiterating those same prosecutions and staying the adjudication of the present cause in your court as having been prosecuted — cites you to see and hear the foregoing:

notwithstanding the remission of the present cause by the Honourable Sub-judge of the Kalisz Land Court to the full Kalisz Land Court as prosecuted — and himself, being one of the number of that court — improperly made from the condescension term at Trąbczyn and enrolled in the authenticated records; which remission ought to have been made not to the Kalisz Land Court but to the Tribunal by the finality of the law, as had been sought by the plaintiff:

[for] this cause — for the resolution of your decree expressed below — to be remitted to the Tribunal, by virtue both of the prior and of the present [citations] issued against you and also against the Honourable Condescension Court Judge; and also by virtue of the original decrees and the Commission of the Republic that followed together with the successors of the widow of the plaintiff's uncle; and there, having reviewed your decree of the enjoined condescension to the estates of Trąbczyn issued between the Honourable Chełmski and the plaintiff in the preceding year, on the Monday after the Feast of Saint Hedwig, Widow and Chosen of God, namely 20 October — which is contrary to your prior decree of remission of this cause to the condescension together with the successors of the widow of the plaintiff's uncle, [a remission made] together with the late Honest Jan Tracholz, the legal assignor of the Honourable Chełmski; and what is more, to his cause against the successors of that same widow of the plaintiff's uncle, instituted after her death — the same prior remission decree neither reviewed nor resolved, and likewise not having a term available from the Honourable Chełmski; and with the decrees and the Commission designated by the Estates of the Realm in this cause which also obstruct and do not admit the Kalisz Land Court forum and your decision not being attended to — unable to be reviewed, having been issued prejudicially and also without being ordered; nay rather, with the communication of documents interrupted in so long-standing a cause, begun thirty years ago after the barren decease both of the plaintiff's uncle and of his widow, and having its beginning according to the prescription of the new statute of the law, which ought entirely to be decreed — having been issued:

himself the plaintiff to be freed from its bond and rigour; and this cause — which cannot be decided in any way without the documents to be recovered from the Rozdrażewski successors — to be remitted together with the cause and proceedings against the successors of the widow of the plaintiff's uncle, namely Katarzyna of Rozdrażewo Prusimska, regarding the documents to be delivered both for this cause and for the general estate of the plaintiff's uncle — left after the death of the uncle with his surviving consort, and after the death of the widow passing to her successors, and vindicated through a process by the plaintiff to the present day — and for which final decision has been ordered through the ultimate Commission of the Republic and which can be brought to execution by the Tribunal alone — by the authority both of that Commission and of the prior Kalisz Land Court decree of remission to the condescension term — not only by reason of the connected and concatenated nature of the matter, but also because the matter demands the production and delivery to him by the Rozdrażewski successors and the advancing of the present cause's documents — to be remitted; and there for that same cause to be decided and determined; and that if the illegal right and pretension of the Honest Jan Tracholz and likewise of the Honourable Chełmski, his acquirer, shall appear from the documents to be received from the Rozdrażewski successors — then thereafter the plaintiff, with the transfer of the Honourable Chełmski annulled

and his illegal right [annulled], to be freed from this legal demand; and by reason of the right acquired unduly and for mere vexation and to entangle the plaintiff's boundary cause and discrepant commissarial decree — and likewise by reason of the undue vexation, and also in reparation of the costs of litigation unjustly caused to the plaintiff — that he himself be punished with condign penalties, or that the litigation costs be decreed to be made good by him to the plaintiff; and if moreover a greater pretension, and sums contracted by the late Honest Tracholz from the late uncle of the plaintiff and owed to the uncle, shall emerge from the documents to be produced and received from the Rozdrażewski successors — then that the same Honourable Chełmski be bound to payment of those sums, as the acquirer of his right, on behalf of the plaintiff, together with provisions; and nonetheless that penalties for the prejudicial decrees procured by the party and issued by the court be extended both against the party and against the court; and in the remainder all things that shall be required by law, justice, the requirements of the present cause and its documents — to be decided, decreed, and sentenced against you. Be therefore ready to obey this term and to respond judicially. Given at Piotrków on the Monday next after Laetare Sunday in the Year of the Lord 1778.

The first of those — against the Honourable Condescension Court Judge — at the provost's house at Trąbczyn, on the table of the heated room, with the mother of the household present, on the Thursday after Laetare Sunday; the second — in the town of Konin, at the house of the Honest Paulszewicz, where the chancellery of the Kalisz Land Court keeping its records at Konin is situated, on the table of the heated room, with the mother of the household present; the third — at the manor court of the estates of the village of Łukom, on the table of the atrium, with a maiden present — all on today's day, as contained in the act, he placed distinctly and, having notified, left.
app53170koningr117-9:
On behalf of the Honourable Chełmski against the Honourable Prusimski — Relatio

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Jan Jankowski of the village of Łukom, Royal Court Summoner, General, sound of health, acknowledged the authenticated citation letter, issued for the Kalisz Land Court sessions of the district to be held at Konin, of the following tenor:

Stanislaus Augustus, by the Grace of God King of Poland, Grand Duke of Lithuania, of Russia, of Prussia, etc. — to you, the Honourable Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, hereditary owner of the estates of Trąbczyn — regarding your person and estates, generally all claims and monetary sums, held and to be held — we command that you appear in person and peremptorily before us and our Kalisz Land Court sessions, first and next to be held at Konin, at the instance of the Honourable Stanisław Chełmski, hereditary owner of the estates of Łukomia, plaintiff; who, adhering to his manifest and likewise to the counter-manifest made or to be made, cites you; or rather

— [cites you] to the prepared decree of the remission made to the full court by the Condescension Court at the condescension term at Trąbczyn, issued expeditiously between himself the plaintiff on one part and you the cited on the other part — cites you to see and hear:

the suit of himself the plaintiff, instituted against you, to be adjudged, notwithstanding any manifests and prosecution terms of yours, if such have intervened, in connection with the plaintiff's documents; the payment of the sum transferred to him the plaintiff from the Honest Jan Tracholz, together with provisions and reimbursement of litigation costs and any processes and delays — from the reasons to be set out at the prosecution term — to be adjudicated to him the plaintiff; and all other things required by the matter, the documents, and justice — to be decreed, decided, and sentenced against you. For which, being cited, be ready to obey, to attend the term and to respond judicially. Given at Kalisz on Good Friday in the Year of the Lord 1778.

At the estates of Trąbczyn, in the estate office there, the letters on the table of the heated room, with the estate manager present — on today's day, as contained in the act, he placed and left.
app53170koningr117-13:
Let there be seen in this place a certain copy of a manifest made on behalf of the Most Honourable Prusimski against the Honourables Nosalski, as is apparent from the copy in the produced documents.

Antoni Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice
app53170koningr117-11:
Done at Konin on the Friday next after the Feast of the Conversion of Saint Paul the Apostle, namely 29 January 1779.

On behalf of the Honourable Prusimski — Pine forest [inspection] together with the presentation of axes

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honest Bartłomiej Szepczyński of the village of Trąbczyn, Royal Court Summoner, General, sound of health, acknowledged that he himself — having with him two nobles, namely the Honourables Tomasz Joachimski, present here, and Marcin Wróblewski, although absent here but present at the location of the matter described below — at the instance and formal request of the Honourable Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, hereditary owner of the estates of Trąbczyn with appurtenances, had descended on the twenty-third of the current month and year to the pine forest pertaining to those same estates of Trąbczyn; and being there thus with the above-mentioned nobles, he declared in these words:

That in the proper hereditary woodland of Trąbczyn, twelve stumps of freshly felled pines — and further, beyond the mounds and between the mounds, more, cut down by people, subjects of the estates of Rzgów —

all of which aforesaid things he duly attested to the present office that he had seen, observed, and counted; and thereupon in the same continuous act he presented to the same office twenty axes — intercepted on the day stated above in the precinct of the estates of Szetlewek from those same subjects of the estates of Rzgów as they fled at night-time with the aforesaid pine trees — which, thus presented, the same Court Summoner together with the Honourable Joachimski received back from the present office; and having received them back, he gave quietance to the present office and its chancellery. The present record quieted.
app53170koningr117-12:
The Honourable Nosalski — manifests by way of diligence

To the office and present records of the Konin Municipal Court, appearing in person, the Honourable Marcin Nosalski, son of the Treasurer of Czernihów, hereditary owner and possessor of the estates of Rzgów with appurtenances — looking to the indemnity of his estate, lest any prejudice be brought against him in any way by means of testimony to be given by the labouring men Bartłomiej Szepczyński and Mateusz Wąchnicki in the cause promoted in the land court proceedings of the Kalisz Palatinate at Konin against the Most Honourable Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice — lodges against the present records, by way of diligence, the following complaint and protests in the following manner:

That the aforesaid labouring men Bartłomiej Szepczyński and Mateusz Wąchnicki, executing the orders of the Honourable Tomasz Joachimowicz, dared and presumed [to act] against the people of his

estate —

obstructing [them] on the public road as they were carting trees on sledges from the hereditary woodland of the Honourable Chełmski; striking and beating those same [people]; bringing them to the estates of Trąbczyn together with the sledges; confiscating their axes by force; charging them with the felling of trees in the Trąbczyn manor forest; and drawing them into complicity in the deed thus constructed — and having committed all these acts of violence, they did not blush to draw the penalties wholly upon themselves.

Wherefore the manifestant, manifesting most solemnly against those same perpetrators of violence, offers to establish the aforesaid acts of violence committed by them in person through a full sworn inquiry, to have them shut out from giving testimony in this cause, and to prove their complicity in the offence in separate points; with all things preserved that ought to be preserved.

Martinus Nosalski

app53170koningr118-13:
The Plenipotentiary of the Illustrious Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, against a Decree of the Kalisz Land Court — a Manifest is lodged

Having come in person to the present Office and Records of the Konin Municipal Court, the Honourable Piotr Gosławski, in the name of the Illustrious Magnificent Antoni Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice (for whom he provides surety), acting as Plenipotentiary, lodges a solemn Complaint in the present Records — for the following reason: that although his Manifesting Principal, in the Land Courts of the Kalisz Palatinate sitting by district in Konin, on Monday, on the very day of the Feast of Saint Hedwig, Widow, Elect, namely the 15th day of the month of October in the past year, when [the court] was held, had appeared through his Plenipotentiary and had produced an attestation issued by the Illustrious Magnificent Franciszek Ksawery Nałęcz Kęszycki, Marshal of the Crown Tribunal, on the 13th day of October in the past year, and had sought a delay to be granted to him for [establishing] the principal matter — nonetheless the Kalisz Land Court, paying no attention whatsoever

to the above-mentioned attestation, had ordered [him] to prove the principal matter; and when the Appearing [party], on behalf of the Manifesting [party], had cited [the existence of] a term before the Crown Tribunal at Piotrków issued against the Illustrious Chełmski, as proof of the cause in the Tribunal Court, turning itself [there] — that the cause, from the Records of the Palatinates of Greater Poland to be promoted to the Tribunal Courts, is judged in favour of the Illustrious Zakrzewskis and others — not heedfully noting for himself the [Kingdom's] Expulsions even at the time of the Register of the Płock Palatinate, judging itself, from which [time] his Manifesting Principal had obtained a judgment in the Crown Tribunal Court at Piotrków — [the Land Court] had not admitted the delay and motion interposed by his Appearing [party]. The Appearing [party] of the Manifesting Principal, therefore, lacking documents, was compelled to withdraw from the appearance.

Therefore the Manifesting [party], in the name of the same person as above, against the Kalisz Land Court and the party presenting the above-mentioned grievances, manifests again and again — offering, on behalf of his Principal, regarding the matters promised by law of the Acts, both the cassation of the Decree ordering [its production] and [redress for] the coercively obtained Condemnation — wishing then to request that penalties for the above-mentioned interests be extended — saving all that is to be saved.

Petrus Gosławski, as [illegible]
app53170koningr118-14:
On behalf of the Illustrious Chełmski, Treasurer of Wschowa, against the Illustrious Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice — a Report

Having come in person, the Honest Bartłomiej Wrzask of the village of Sławsk, General Royal Process Server, sound [of mind], acknowledged that he had served authenticated Citation Letters for the Term of the Condescension in the settlement of the estates of Grab, being conducted, upcoming, below-written, of the following tenor:

Stanisław August, by the Grace of God, King of Poland — to you, the Illustrious and Magnificent Antoni Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, Knight of the Order of Saint Stanislaus, Heir of the estates of Trąbczyn and others; and to Ludwik, Land Court Chamberlain of Kalisz; and to Teresa of the Rozdrzewski [family], [uncertain: oto] the Illustrious Katarzyna, likewise of the Rozdrzewski [family], last [by] marriage Prusimska, Heiress of the estate of Grab; and [uncertain: oto] the Illustrious Magnificent, likewise of the Rozdrzewski [family], Molska, Castellaness of Rogoźno — having died without issue — to her successor, or mutually [Congb~is], Bogdański — concerning all your estates generally — we command: that before Us and Our Condescensorial Court, by the force of a Decree of the Crown Tribunal of the Kingdom at Piotrków issued between you, the Cited [parties], on one part, and the Plaintiffs and others on the other part, on the 3rd day of June in the present year 1782, by virtue of the last Limitation, the Condescension [session] to proceed — you appear in person and peremptorily — at the instance of the Illustrious Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski, Treasurer of Wschowa, Plaintiff, who cites you, and indeed [the] married [party] under the competent authority of her husband, adhering to their documents supporting the matter, cites [you], or rather summons [you] to any prepared decrees [and] a prepared proceeding — to see and hear yourselves [obliged] to the payment of sums, whatever and however much shall appear from the documents to be due to the Plaintiff from you, together with provisions, to be bound [thereby]; the Plaintiff's claim regarding the payment of the sum transferred to the Plaintiff [as agent] from the Honourable Tracholz, Merchant — originally instituted [against] you before the Kalisz Land Court, and afterwards, via prosecutions, [transferred] to the Illustrious Magnificent [Antoni] and to the Illustrious Magnificent [Katarzyna] Prusimska to the Condescensorial Court by remission — to be resolved at the Term of Our Condescension, notwithstanding any of your oppositions and prosecutions; to decide [regarding] the payment of the transferred sum for the Plaintiff, together with provisions, bound to the chain of Documents, [...] Mercantile Contracts, and any other Transactions proving these, to be followed by you, to be found; the penalties in respect of the evocation to the Tribunal Courts for what is at stake to be extended; court expenses to be found compensable; all-encompassing satisfaction for the Plaintiff's interest, as great as it is, to be commanded; the summoning of the labourers Albert Siwy, Andreas Rataj, Casimir the Keeper, Albert the Shepherd, of Nowa Wieś, and the subjects of you, the Illustrious Magnificent Prusimski, who, as before, so also by this Citation are detained at your place, to be decreed to give testimony; and other things which [by] the law of the cause and present matter shall be decided, resolved, and sentenced of the same [parties] — be equally ready to observe the Term and to respond judicially to these and other things which will be more fully proposed to you. Given at Piotrków, on the 26th day of the month of November, in the Year of the Lord 1781. In the estates of Trąbczyn, upon the table in the heated room, the Revenue Clerk being present, on Friday, the Eve of the Feast of the Immaculate Conception of the Most Blessed Virgin Mary, in the Year of the Lord 1781 — having placed [the citation] and having left notification.

On behalf of the Venerable Ląd Convent, against the Illustrious Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice — a Report

Having come in person to the present Office and Records of the Konin Municipal Court, the Honest Simon Głabik of Drzewce, General Royal Process Server, sound [of mind], acknowledged that he had served authenticated Citation Letters for the Ordinary General Sessions of the Crown Tribunal of the Kingdom at Piotrków below-written, of the following tenor:

Stanisław August, by the Grace of God, King of Poland, Grand Duke of Lithuania, Russia, Prussia, Masovia, Samogitia, Kyiv, Volhynia, Podolia, Podlachia, Livonia, Smolensk, Severia, and Chernihiv — to the Illustrious Magnificent Antoni Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, Heir of the estate of Trąbczyn, concerning the cause below-written and all his estates generally — we command: that before Us and Our Ordinary General Court of the Crown Tribunal of the Kingdom at Piotrków, exactly within four weeks [uncertain: seco], then when and at such time as the present cause shall fall to be judged when called, you appear in person and peremptorily — at the instance of the Most Illustrious Most Reverend Benedykt Lubstowski of Ląd, Abbot of the Sacred Cistercian Order's Convent of Ląd, and of the entire same Convent, Heirs of the estates of

Drzewce — Plaintiffs. Which Plaintiffs, adhering to their own [documents], cite themselves, or rather summon [parties] to the joinder of the cause with the Heir of the estates of Łukomia and others; and this to see and hear themselves, the Plaintiffs, [declared free] from the alleged counterclaim, and [uncertain: A] with the Heir of the estates of Łukomia, the documents having been considered — namely the Tribunal Decrees and the Survey of the Year of the Lord 1592, approved by those same Decrees — [to be] declared free [from the accusation], the penalties of the alleged counterclaim to be extended [to Prusimski], and court expenses to be found refundable; and other matters to be pursued for the cause and responded to judicially. Given at Piotrków, on the 4th day of January, in the Year of the Lord 1782. In the manor of the estate of Trąbczyn, upon the table in the heated room, a maidservant present, on this very day, having placed the contents of the present Acts and having left notification.
