app53170koningr118-17:
The Illustrious Górski, Boundary Surveyor of Inowrocław, against the Illustrious Chełmski, Treasurer of Wschowa — a Manifest is lodged

Having come in person to the present Office and Records of the Konin Municipal Court, the Illustrious Jakub Górski, Boundary Surveyor of the Inowrocław Palatinate, adhering to the new law concerning the effectuation of decrees in settled matters, and also insisting upon the other laws enacted concerning judicial security and authority, and looking to judicial security — solemnly, before the same Office and its Records, in and against the Illustrious Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski, Treasurer of Wschowa, Heir of the estates of Łukom with appurtenances — a Manifest is lodged, for this reason: Because the Manifesting [party], for the Term of the Field Condescension between the estates of Trąbczyn minor or Nowa Wieś, of the Illustrious Magnificent Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, Knight of the Order of Saint Stanislaus, and [the estates of] Łukom, the hereditary [property] of the above-mentioned Illustrious Chełmski — [said Term] assigned by the Crown Tribunal Post-Commissorial Decree at Piotrków, on Wednesday after the Feast of Saint Agnes, Virgin and Martyr, namely the 23rd day of the month of January in the present year, between the above-mentioned Parties, after the boundary cause was decided from the map and two Commissorial Decrees issued discrepantly and contrary to each other were resolved, in the matter of the erection of boundary mounds — having been obtained [at the instance of] the Illustrious Magnificent Prusimski: when he descended to the site for the Term of that Condescension, wishing to bring to effect [the decree] according to the prescription of that same Tribunal Decree and the line placed on the map by the Tribunal — that Tribunal Decree, being a Post-Commissorial [decree], not subject to any interpretation or relief pursuant to the new law of the Year 1776, enacted concerning Post-Commissorial Causes and Decrees — and intending to complete and effectuate the other contents according to the rule of the same Tribunal Decree and the line placed and subscribed on the map by the Tribunal:

the Illustrious Chełmski, Heir of the estates of Łukomia, personally himself with his retinue, rebelliously obstructed the further effectuation of the Post-Commissorial Tribunal Decree of the last instance and also the judicial [process] hedged about by so many laws — and pushed away the man drawing the geometric chain, and kicked it out of the line with his foot — and began to threaten — and also, responding to the judicial interrogation of his Office, declared himself judicially as not admitting the further laying of the Line to be carried out by the Geometer and his Office.

For which reason his Office, avoiding any danger, this rebellious obstruction notwithstanding, was obliged to suspend itself from any further act and from the execution and effectuation of the above-mentioned Tribunal Decree — and suspended [proceedings] for the purpose of obtaining military [assistance] from the Illustrious War Department.

Therefore his Manifesting [party], having recourse to the Laws of the Kingdom with respect to all the above-mentioned matters and notably this kind of rebellious obstruction and denial, manifests again and again — saving all that is to be saved by law.

Jakub Pomian Górski, Boundary Surveyor of the Inowrocław Palatinate

The Illustrious Chełmski, Treasurer of Wschowa, against the Illustrious Górski, Boundary Surveyor of Inowrocław — a Manifest is lodged

Having come in person to the present Office and Records of the Konin Municipal Court, the Illustrious Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski, Heir of the estates of Łukomia [and] Myszakowo with appurtenances, safeguarding the integrity of his estates and substance — lodges this Manifest in the present Records, on account of the matters below-written, against the Illustrious Jakub Górski, Boundary Surveyor of Inowrocław — and this for the following reason: Because the same Illustrious Jakub Górski, presuming that everything is permitted to his Office, as is apparent from his Field Acts oblated to the present Records — although he knew that Executive Offices executing each individual Decree of the Most Serene Crown Tribunal are obligated not to interpret but to execute, by the chain of laws and especially the Constitution of the Year 1768 — but the same [Górski], exceeding the prescribed rule of the Condescension for Field Courts and Offices in the settlement of the estate of Trąbczyn as prescribed by the Decree of the Most Serene Crown Tribunal, and inconveniently diverging from the Field Office likewise of the Dobrzyń Land — in the execution not only of the Tribunal Decree but also of the Acts of the Gniezno Municipal Court emanating from the same and similarly oblated to the present Records — thrust himself into [the matter of] the evacuation of the Olędry of the Illustrious Magnificent Prusimski;

and with his illegal object circumscribed the Manifesting party as if [Chełmski] had placed himself rebelliously at the field act; and nullly and unduly, contrary to the meaning of the Statute and without the consenting parties, postponed his Act until some unknown time; declaring, beyond the presumed scope of the above-mentioned Tribunal Decree and by his own private notifications, that he would descend to the site again — instead of [properly] remitting the matter to the Crown Tribunal on account of the impossibility [of execution] according to the Line on the Map, which is incompatible with the actual site locations, made by the Most Serene Tribunal — without accounting for the Olędry adjudicated to [Chełmski] and the Manifesting party; and for military forces remitted his Acts to the Military Department of the Permanent Council — and thereby also transgressed against [the sanctions of] the Tribunal, and in his [further] proceedings greatly injured the Manifesting party, and caused litigation expenses.

Therefore in fact the Manifesting party, on account of all the above-mentioned matters, against the same [Górski], regarding the nullity of his Act, in the most solemn legal form, manifests — offering to proceed by law with the same [Górski] for the badly conducted office, for penalties and the nullity of the act inserted above — and to vindicate by law, through legal mediation, the harm and injuries caused to him, where it shall come by right — the present Manifest's improvement, diminution, or augmentation to be made as the business opportunity requires, reserved to himself with full force, and the right guarded.

Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski

At the requisition of the party, namely the Honourable Piotr Gosławski, as the bonded Plenipotentiary of the Illustrious Magnificent Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, acting in the name of the same [person as] his Principal — in the presence of the Honourables Tomasz Reczkowski and Świętosław Bogusławski, and also the Honest Mateusz Matuszkiewicz of Szetlewek, General Royal Process Server — for this interval, on account of information not given for enrollment and the copy not submitted — the requisition was made on the 16th day of the month of August.

Petrus Gosławski

Stanisław Ścibor Chełmski
app53170koningr118-20:
For the part of the Illustrious Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice — Requisition of the Report issued on the part of the Illustrious Chełmski [for the Crown Tribunal at Piotrków]

Having come in person to the present Office and Records of the Konin Municipal Court, the Honourable Piotr Gosławski, Plenipotentiary of the Illustrious Magnificent Antoni Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, in the name of the same Magnificent Principal of his — sound [of mind] — acknowledged: that he, having with him two Nobles, namely the Honourables Tomasz Reczkowski and Jakub Bogusławski, although present here — at the instance and official requisition of the Illustrious Magnificent Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, Knight of the Order of Saint Stanislaus, Heir of the estates of Trąbczyn, Trąbczynka, and others — had descended here to the present Chancellery with the above-mentioned Nobles, and there requisitioned from the present Office and requested the production [of the document]: whether the Citation Return in the estates of Trąbczyn, on the part of,

the Illustrious Stanisław Chełmski, Treasurer of Wschowa, Heir of the estates of Łukomia and others, against the Illustrious Magnificent Principal of his [the] Requisitioner, for the Ordinary General Sessions of the Crown Tribunal of the Kingdom at Piotrków — issued — was recognised before the present Records or not. To which Requisition the present Office, consenting, wished to produce the same. Therefore the present [document] attests to the non-existence of that same recognised Report and the impossibility of its production.

Petrus Gosławski

app53170koningr118-23:
Done in Konin, on Saturday, on the very day of the Feast of Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist, namely the 21st day of the month of September, in the Year of the Lord 1782.

On behalf of the Illustrious Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, against the Illustrious Zakrzewskis and others — a Report

Having come in person to the present Office and Records of the Konin Municipal Court, the Honest Bartłomiej Szepczyński of the village of Trąbczyn, General Royal Process Server, sound [of mind], acknowledged that he had served authenticated Citation Letters of one and the same essence, three in number, for the Ordinary General Sessions of the Crown Tribunal of the Kingdom at Piotrków below-written, of the following tenor:

The following: Stanisław August, by the Grace of God, etc. — to you, the Illustrious Casimir, Judge of the Brest-Kuyavia Land Court, father; Nepomucen, Judge of the Radziejów Municipal Court; Ignacy, Land Court Chamberlain; and Ludwik, [Judge] of Brest-Kuyavia — his sons — the Zakrzewskis; together with the late Illustrious Marianna Prusimska, first [wife] of the late Honourable Józef Tomicki, second [by] marriage wife of the same Illustrious Casimir Zakrzewski, Judge of the Brest-Kuyavia Land Court — the children begotten in the second marriage; and to Paweł and Józef Tomicki, sons begotten by the above-mentioned Honourable Józef Tomicki with the same Illustrious Marianna Prusimska in the first marriage, and other children of the same Honourable Tomicki; and also to Franciszek, Pantler of Podlachia, [and] Elżbieta, wife of the Illustrious Jakub Taczanowski, Huntsman of Trębowla — brother and sister among themselves, of the Tworowicz [family], son and daughter begotten by the late Honourable Michał Tworowicz with the late Illustrious Wiktoria Prusimska, first [by] marriage Wysocka, in the second marriage; and to the same Illustrious Jakub Taczanowski, husband of the Honourable Elżbieta Tworowicz, or to both the Taczanowski spouses jointly; and also to Kunigunda Kowalska, wife of the Honourable Piotr Kołaczkowski, daughter begotten by the late Honourable Jan Kowalski with the late Honourable Konstancja Prusimska, or rather both the Kołaczkowski spouses; and finally to the Illustrious Stefan Leszczyć Zielonacki, Land Judge, Andrzej Bogdański, Sub-judge, Ksawery Mikorski, Notary, and also Ignacy Rapacki, Chamberlain, then Sub-delegated Grievance Judges of the Kalisz Land Court — concerning your persons, estates, sums, and Office, we command [uncertain: ott~] that before Us and Our Ordinary General Court of the Crown Tribunal at Piotrków, when and as the present cause from its Register and appropriate inscription falls to be judged when called and proclaimed, you appear in person and peremptorily —

at the instance of the Illustrious Magnificent Antoni of Kolno Prusimski, Starost of Niszczewice, Knight of the Order of Saint Stanislaus, son of the late Illustrious Stefan Prusimski begotten with the late Illustrious Wiktoria Malczewska, grandson of the late Illustrious Krzysztof Prusimski and Teresa Golińska, spouses, [descendant] of the late Illustrious Jan, Bogumił, Antoni, and Paweł Prusimski, sons of the above-mentioned Krzysztof and Teresa Golińska, spouses, brothers among themselves and blood brothers of the late father of the Plaintiff, and blood paternal uncles of the Plaintiff himself, and [as] sole natural and legitimate successor after the childless deaths of the Illustrious Antoni and Paweł — the Plaintiff

who cites you, needing due legal assistance, adhering to his manifests made or to be made, and to the Tribunal Decree of the Year 1738, at Piotrków, on Tuesday after the Feast of All Saints, issued between the late Illustrious Jan and Konstancja of the Prusimski family, Kowalski spouses, on one part, and the Illustrious Antoni, Paweł, and Stefan Prusimski, father and uncles of the Plaintiff, on the other part — adjudicating against the late Kowalskis in the claimed succession after the late Illustrious Jan and Bogumił Prusimski who died without issue; [and also] the subsidiary Decree of the Year 1760, likewise at Piotrków, on Thursday, the eve of the Feast of the Presentation of the Most Glorious Virgin Mary, between the late Illustrious Antoni Prusimski, his

uncle, and himself the Plaintiff, and you the Cited — confirming, after the sterile death of the third brother namely Paweł, the said Decree of 1738 together with other Transactions and the paternal disposition, and approving it; and to the paternal disposition of the late Illustrious Krzysztof Prusimski [uncertain: Aci] his grandfather, and other documents supporting this cause; and also to the law of the neighbouring Prussian Territories, and the precedents in similar causes following, and the admitted motion —

cites [you], or rather summons [you] to the above-mentioned, to see and hear:

the above-mentioned Tribunal Decree of 1738 not having been vitiated even by the parties, but rather confirmed by the subsequent Decree of 1760, the same also again approved and declared to be stood by — [the Plaintiff seeks:] the Kalisz Land Court Decrees, first indeed ordering the sharing of documents regarding the successive substance devolved upon the Plaintiff after the late brothers and uncles, also without the Plaintiff's competence having first been resolved, contrary to law and usual practice, to be set aside; then another [decree] for the place of the remission, with the intervening Tribunal decree, the appropriate forum having been found, together with the grievance sentences regarding the accessories of the ordered proceeding and prosecution of the cause, and the grievance decrees following between you the Cited and himself the Plaintiff, and the threatening of the loss of the cause to the Plaintiff being relieved; and also the Kalisz Land Court Decree on the very day of the Feast of Saint Hedwig, Widow, Elect, in the Year 1781 — issued contrary to law, denying and indeed cutting off the delay lawfully due to the Plaintiff without heeding the Tribunal Decrees — and also the last [decree] by which the competent action and plaintiff-standing was found in favour of the Zakrzewskis and others — to be cassated; and penalties both upon you for having procured these decrees, and upon the Illustrious Judges for transgression of the law in their judging, to be imposed; and now any process unduly obtained against the Plaintiff from your part to be cassated, and the Plaintiff to be freed from the chain and rigour of the Kalisz Land Court Decrees, from your demand and the pretended undue succession after the late Illustrious Antoni and Paweł Prusimski, blood brothers of the late father of the Plaintiff and blood uncles of the Plaintiff himself, who died without issue; the incompetent action claimed by you regarding such succession after the late Antoni and Paweł, unduly claimed by you — as also after the late Illustrious Jan and Bogumił Prusimski, their earlier deceased brothers — according to the Tribunal Decree of 1738 and the paternal disposition and the precedents in similar causes following, and the law prohibiting daughters exdotated by their father to claim nothing from brothers, and also [the law] of the neighbouring Prussian Territories — to be declared [incompetent]; the right of action of the Honourable Tomicka rather regarding the improvement of the dowry than the claimed succession, as appointed without a term, to be declared; and perpetual silence to be imposed upon you in the present cause; and penalties for the resuscitation of a matter already decided, for undue harassment, for the issued and procured grievance decrees, and in the force of litigation expenses unduly caused to the Plaintiff, upon you [uncertain: Voles]

and the Kalisz Land Court to be extended — and as for the rest, all those things which shall be [decided] according to law and documents, to be decreed and sentenced against you. Be therefore equally ready to attend this Term and to respond judicially.

Given at [P]iotrków, on Monday, next after the Feast of Saint Bartholomew the Apostle, in the Year of the Lord 1782. The first of them, against the Illustrious Tomickis, in the manor of the estates of the village of Zieleniec, in the presence of the Cited party, on the Thursday most recently past. The second, against the Illustrious Zakrzewskis, in the manor of the estates of the village of Mostki, in the presence of the Cited party, on yesterday, the day preceding today's act. The third, against the Kalisz Land Court, in the town of Konin, in the house of the Renowned Wiśniewska, citizen of Konin, and in the Kalisz Land Court Chancellery existing there during the court sessions, before the same Renowned Wiśniewska, on this very day — having placed [the citations] upon the tables in the heated room at all three [locations] distinctly, and having left notification at every location.
