agad14320139-1:
[To His] Reverence the General Superintendent
of the Warsaw Evangelical-Augsburg
Consistorial District.

The Pastor-Administrator [of the]
Evangelical-Augsburg [congregation of]
Zagórow.

In consequence of [Your Reverence's] order
of the 30th of October [text lost],
No. 267, I have the honour to submit the following annual report
concerning the parish of Zagórow.

I. Church affairs.

a.) External church affairs.– The congregation of Zagórow possesses a brick-built church; for its complete furnishing it still lacks a baptismal font, an organ and bells.– Both the parsonage and the cantor's house are very small and low, and in very poor condition.– The schoolroom is adequately spacious for the number of children.– Besides the religious school in Zagórow there are 7 more schools combined with prayer houses in the congregation, among them only one elementary school, at Michalinowo.– The number of children in the 8 schools of the congregation may come to about 240.– There is no separate dwelling for the sexton[?].– As for the cemeteries, of which there are 8 in the congregation, they are [text lost] in good condition and provided with crosses.–

b.) Inner church affairs.– Church spirit and church attendance satisfactory.– Baptisms are mostly performed by the pastor.– Open despisers of the Lord's Supper: none known.– The number of communicants: men 726, women 871, total 1597, [text lost]

[text lost] 45 more.– [uncertain: A demand] for still more schools [text lost] is not present, since almost every larger colony has a [text lost].– For the mission to the heathen, 10 roubles 71 kopecks were [collected] in the course of the year at the mission services, which the Pastor-Administrator sent on to Superintendent Pastor Manitius at Warsaw.– Morality and domestic life are in general very satisfactory.– Baptists, Irvingians or other sects there are none.– Particular vices[?] in the congregation are [not] present. Conversions to other confessions do [not] take place.–

Remarkable events.– None have taken place.–

[To His] Reverence the General Superintendent
of the Warsaw Evangelical-Augsburg
Consistorial District.

The Pastor-Administrator [of the]
Evangelical-Augsburg [congregation of]
Lissewo-Pyzdry.

In consequence of [Your Reverence's] order
of the 30th of October [text lost],
No. 267, I have the honour to submit the following annual report
concerning the filial Lissewo-Pyzdry.

I. Church affairs.

a.) External church affairs.– The filial possesses neither a church [text lost] sexton's house.– Divine service in Pyzdry is held in rented premises.– In the filial there are five religious schools combined with prayer houses, all of them in good condition.– The number of children in the five schools of the filial comes to about 120.– There are five cemeteries in the filial, all fenced and provided with crosses.–

b.) Inner church affairs.– Church spirit and church attendance satisfactory.– Baptisms are performed by the cantors concerned in the prayer houses; the pastor, when he is present in the prayer houses, confirms the baptisms performed by the cantors, and holds the churching[?] with the women [text lost].– Open despisers of the Lord's Supper: none known.– The number of communicants: men 326, women 408, total 734, [text lost] compared with the year 1881, 131 more.– The inhabitants of Pyzdry would gladly set up an Evangelical school among themselves, [but] are too poor for it, since the little town counts only 9 families[?], and [text lost]

[text lost] lay people can be brought in for it, since the [text lost] colonies have their own teachers and prayer houses.–

For the mission to the heathen, 3 roubles 40 kopecks were collected in the course of the year at the mission services, which the Pastor-Administrator sent on to Superintendent Pastor Manitius at Warsaw.– Morality and domestic life are in general satisfactory.– Particular vices in the congregation not present.– Baptists, Irvingians etc. there are none.– Conversions to other confessions do not take place.–

Remarkable events.– None have taken place.–

Number of confirmed.– Boys 13, girls 10, together 23.–

Candidates living in the congregation.– None.–

Collections.– For the benefit of the congregation itself nothing was collected, but for other purposes the following: 1.) For the support of grammar-school pupils who intend to study theology, 1 rouble 76 kopecks, which the Pastor-Administrator sent to his High Evangelical-Augsburg Consistory at Warsaw.– 2.) For the widows' and orphans' fund [text lost] roubles 36 kopecks were collected, and the same sent to Superintendent von Boerner at Plock.–

E. Erdmann
Pastor

middle schools, namely: the German boys' gymnasium at Lodz, the German

perhaps "coeducational gymnasiums"] at Pabjanize [Pabianice], Zgierz
and Sompolno, have, as has already been mentioned, come to an
understanding on a common basis. The subject matter, from pre-school I
up to 0-I [as written], is to be worked through in 12 school
years, although individual gentlemen argued for an eleven-year course.
However, in view of the abundance of material and the overburdening
involved in learning three foreign languages, the majority came out
for keeping the 12-year school type. Judged from the cultural
standpoint, the coming into being of a directors' conference is to be
welcomed most warmly. What remains to be wished is that subject
conferences of the teachers active at the German institutions soon
follow the directors' conference, which has discussed the great number
of manifold school questions in general outlines. For lack of time the
directors' conference could not settle various fundamental questions
exhaustively, still less matters of the utmost importance, such as a
rebuilding, a partial reduction of the individual subjects. In this
respect the judgement of the teaching staff long employed at the
schools is in any case decisive. The holding of subject conferences
would also counteract the dangerous going-it-alone at present to be
observed in the individual institutions and [obscure]. It would lie in
the interests of the former [written "Frugerspielnischen"] Deutschtum
if we would like to receive word [written "garbeli-Kunde"] of the
coming into being of the subject conferences.

[The page begins mid-sentence.] … recall lost, [written "geborsteres"]
folk property. If we take a walk today through Warsaw, Lublin,
[written "Stadoni"], even through a market town lying far from the
great trade routes, we come everywhere upon German family names on the
shop signs. The bearers of the German names will put up with most
things; on no account may one address them as Germans. Dead and spoiled
is here the smallest trace of the former folk property. As a public
scandal, nothing is left to such people but their German family name.
Often one takes the legal route to be rid of the troublesome name.
Whoever leafs attentively through the first volumes of the state
newspaper "Monitor Polski" will find many a fine blossom of this kind.
This way, however, is beset with greater or lesser difficulties, and of
late a considerable sum is charged for a lawful change of name. The
resourcefulness of some commune heads, even of the evangelical pastors
(Pastor Winkler in Wieluń, Pastor v. Boerner in Zduńska-Wola), has here
found a simpler way, one leading more comfortably to the goal, namely

These Witów files have long been sought in the registry at Trąbczyn, where I myself supposed and maintained [that they would be lying]. They were, however, upon my moving out

that they would be lying.

from my lodgings at Wrocław to Wilhelmsruh, found among the papers of my wife, because these files were received by my wife at a time when I was absent from Wrocław, and were laid for safe keeping among her belongings, where the papers are never read, and thus it was forgotten to hand them over to me afterwards.
